:d:
Actually ":D", in lower case due to technical restraints. Represents a wide, open-mouthed smile or grin. If the character is also winking, use ;d instead.
For a ":d" expression, use :q or licking lips.
:i:
Actually : 工 but not capitalized due to technical restrictions and lack of serif.
Similar to :t except with lines at both sides of the mouth. Usually indicates that the character is holding their breath or pouting.
:o:
Round mouths of all sizes.

:p: Someone sticking out their tongue with their mouth closed.
:q:
Running the tongue along the upper lip in a "licking lips" sort of way.
Indicates anticipating tasty food, but can also show playful mischief or teasing.
:t:
pouting with one cheek puffed out, forming a :T shape with the lips. Typically representative of jealousy or indignation, or unamusement.
Also used when the character is eating with their mouth full.
:x:
Often used for stuffed animals, especially rabbits, to show that the stitch is their lip.
It also means to be tight-lipped.
:|: When the mouth is a horizontal line. Usually represents a sad, expressionless or unamused face.
;3: Represents a cat's smile like :3, except the character is also winking.
;<: Like :<, but with a winky face instead.
;>: Like :>, but with a winky face instead.
;d:
Actually ";D", in lower case due to technical restraints. Represents a wide, open-mouthed smile or grin like :d, except that the character is also winking.
For a ";d" expression, use ;q
;o: When a character has one eye closed either from winking, wincing or yawning and their mouth open.
;p: Winking while sticking the tongue out downwards of the mouth.
;q: Winking while sticking the tongue out upwards of the mouth.
;t: When a character is winking and has one cheek squashed against the lip. Usually happens out of annoyance, when a character is eating, or when they're pressing their cheek hard against something.
<|> <|>: Emote meant to represent cat eyes.
= =:

It is primarily used to express contentment but can occasionally be used for anything from exasperation to embarrassment or sleepiness.
>3<: A facial expression that combines > < eyes with puckered lips (o3o).
> <: Eyes tightly closed in a literal >_< shape. This usually indicates extreme happiness, but it can also be used to indicate pain, embarrassment, or sadness.
> o: A wink with the closed eye drawn the same as the > < face.
>o<: A facial expression that combines > < eyes with an open mouth (:o).
?: Shows that the question mark is visually present in the image, standing alone either inside or outside a text balloon. Usually denotes wonder, confusion, or curiosity.

\\m/:
The 🤟 hand gesture. The thumb, index, and pinkie fingers are held out, while the middle and ring fingers touch the palm of the hand.
Not to be confused with \n/ (🤘), where the thumb is held down instead of extended out.
In anime, it is well known for being part of the sailor moon's famous tsuki ni kawatte oshioki yo ("I'll punish you") pose, for ranka lee's dance move in macross frontier while singing the song seikan hikou, and for the association with yazawa nico's catchphrase, nico nico nii.
\\n/:
The 🤘 hand gesture. The index and pinkie fingers are raised, while the middle and ring fingers are held down by the thumb.
Known in the West as "the sign of the horns", "the devil's horns", or "throwing the horns". Often associated with heavy metal music, which was made popular by ronnie james dio. Originated as an apotropaic gesture to ward off the "evil eye," a curse cast by glaring at someone with hostility.
Not to be confused with \m/ (🤟) (when the thumb is held out) or with fox shadow puppet (when the fingers are extended forward to make a fox muzzle).
\\o/: An emoticon depicting a person with arms raised in joy.
\\||/:
A hand gesture wherein the middle and ring fingers are pressed together, while the index and little fingers are angled away from the middle two.
Not to be confused with the fox shadow puppet or the vulcan salute.

ak-47:
The AK-47 (Автомат Калашникова образца 1947 года) is a 7.62×39mm assault rifle of soviet origin, developed between 1944–1946 by mikhail kalashnikov. The AK platform has a reputation for its ruggedness, reliability, simple mechanism and ease of manufacture. It can perform well with poor quality ammunition and under harsh conditions.
Visual cues of the original AK-47 are its slanted fixed buttstock profile, a milled receiver with a large rectangular indentation as the magazine guide and a smooth dust cover, (see post #4852784).
ak-74: The AK-74 (Автомат Калашникова образца 1974 года 'Kalashnikov assault rifle model 1974') is a 5.45×39mm assault rifle, developed in Izhevsk Mechanical Plant, 1974. It largely replaced the larger-caliber akm in soviet service, and many of its parts are interchangeable with the earlier AKs. First used by Soviet forces during the Afghanistan conflict from 1979.
ak-74m:
The modernized variant of the ak-74 assault rifle, introduced in 1991. The most noticeable feature is the whole standard black finish, as well as black synthetic side-folding stock and handguards. Its full-bodied stock retains the "full" shape of the original AK-74. Compatible with earlier AK-74 magazines and gp-25 series of grenade launchers.
The letter M stands for Модернизи́рованный (Modernizírovanny), a Russian word for "modernized".

akm:
The AKM (Russian: Автома́т Кала́шникова модернизи́рованный "Kalashnikov's Automatic rifle Modernized") is a soviet 7.62×39mm assault rifle, designed in 1950s as the major improvement from the earlier ak-47. Main features of the AKM are its stamped receiver (visible rivets) instead of heavier milled one, slanted muzzle brake, and straighter fixed buttstock profile.
Its design was copied and manufactured by various Soviet satellite states, such as Hungarian amd-65 and East German mpi-km.

albino:
Complete or partial absence of skin and hair pigment due to an absence or defect of an enzyme needed for the production of melanin. Due to this, people and animals appear very light-skinned and typically have red eyes because while there is no pigment in the irises, the blood vessels can still be seen. This does not disqualify blue eyes, however, as most people with ocular albinism have blue eyes that bear a slight red tint due to the blood vessel still present. 
Characters with albinism must have the following to qualify:
- Either white or grey hair.
- Red, blue, pink or purple eyes.

alternate breast size:
When a character has breasts noticeably larger or smaller than their canonical size, usually by greater than two cup sizes.

alternate color: Different colored versions of a character's original attire and overall appearance. If the different colors are from official sources, use official alternate color instead.
alternate costume:
A character wearing a costume other than the one they are typically depicted in, typically fanmade/unofficial. These can range from casual or contemporary attire to adaptations of their costume into different forms.
For official alternate outfits, such as those found in video games, or special chapters/episodes, please use official alternate costume.
alternate element: When an elemental character is portrayed to be using a different element outside of their canon element.
alternate eye color:
When a character is drawn with eyes of a different hue from the canonical color. A type of artistic license and should not be considered an error. 
- Examples: 
  - hong meiling is often depicted with green eyes instead of the canonical blue eyes.
If a character's eye color is inconsistent in the official material (izayoi sakuya has been shown with both red and blue eyes, kochiya sanae has been shown with both gold and blue eyes, etc.), only apply this tag for colors that do not appear in any official works.
alternate facial hair:
Characters who are drawn with a facial hair style different from their default one.
A common example of this is ryu (street fighter) from street fighter.
Sometimes it can be an artistic error with artists drawing a full beard for characters with long sideburns and goatee.
alternate form:
A character or being in another look then usually, the transformation into something new. The body must have changed remarkably. age progression does not count. Alternate forms are often shown in the related manga/anime/game.
Examples:
- A few pokemon like giratina or shaymin
- frieza from dragon ball z
- tony tony chopper from one piece
alternate hair color: Characters whose hair is drawn in a color different than the usual color.
alternate hair length: When the hair of a character is longer or shorter than the official length. Do not use this tag when the the different hair length has an official origin, use official alternate hair length instead.
alternate hair ornament: Characters that are drawn with a different hair ornament than they usually wear.
alternate hairstyle:
Characters which are drawn with a hairstyle different from their default hairstyle. This also includes changes in hair length.
Do not use this tag if the alternate hairstyle is of official origin, use official alternate hairstyle instead.
alternate headwear:
When a character that typically wears a piece of headwear wears a different one instead.
For example, someone who officially wears a porkpie hat is wearing a baseball cap in fan art.
alternate height: When a character's height is depicted notably differently from their canonical size.
alternate language:
An image that has been hard-translated to another language (usually English) by the artist themselves, or by someone authorized by the artist (the company officially publishing a localization, a translator with the permission of the artist, etc).
In most cases the artist posts the translated version alongside the original version. In some cases the official translation may be poor quality, even though it was sanctioned by the artist.
This is different from hard-translated, which is generally done by third parties.
alternate legwear: A character wearing legwear they normally wouldn't wear, such as a character wearing thighhighs when they normally wear pantyhose.
alternate muscle size: When a character has bigger or smaller muscles than they have in canon.
alternate pectoral size:
When a character is depicted with pectorals noticeably larger or smaller than their canonical size.
Do not use this tag if the character's canonical chest size is ambiguous, or the character is being depicted as older or younger.
alternate shiny pokemon: A Pokémon that is alternate-colored, but not the canonical shiny color.
alternate size: When the character's physical size is noticeably larger or smaller than their canonical size.
alternate skin color:
When a character is portrayed with skin that is significantly different to its canonical color.
For skin darkened due to exposure to the sun, use tan instead.
alternate species:
When a humanoid character is depicted as a member of a different humanoid race than their own. This includes humans being depicted as a fantasy race or alien, as well as members of fictional races being depicted as other fictional races.
Do not use this tag when humanization, monsterification, slimification, furrification, or mechanization applies unless there is also an instance of alternate species in the same image.
alternate universe: Used for hypothetical, non-canonical situations, such as exploring the implications of a deceased character still being alive (a.k.a. what ifs, WIs or alternate timelines) or a radical shift in setting like fantasy to urban (a.k.a. alternate universes, AUs).
alternate weapon: When a character's signature weapon is depicted in any form other than what has been shown in canon.
alternate wings: When a character who canonically has wings is depicted with a different or uncommon depiction of their wings.

american flag:
The flag of the United States of America, colloquially known as the Stars and Stripes. It serves as a symbol of the country's unity, independence, and democratic ideals. 
The design of the American flag consists of 13 horizontal stripes alternating between red and white, representing the original 13 colonies that declared independence from British rule. In the top left corner, commonly referred to as the canton, there is a blue rectangle containing 50 white, five-pointed stars arranged in nine rows. These stars represent the 50 states of the United States.

Known as the rhinarium. It is referred to as the tip of the snout, and breeders of cats and 
dogs sometimes use the term nose leather.
Informally, it may be called a "truffle", "wet snout" or "wet nose," because its surface is moist in some species: for example, healthy dogs and cats.
Animal noses are often drawn colored black as slightly big dots on anthropomorphic characters.
animal on arm: Used for when any animal is resting on someone's arm.
animal on chest: An animal or creature on top of one’s chest/breasts, whether the person is lying down or standing.
animal on hand: An animal sitting on a character's hand.
animal on head: Used for when any kind of animal is resting on someone's head or hat. stuffed animals count.
animal on lap: Umbrella tag for any kind of animal sitting on a person's lap. Specific animals include cat on lap and bird on lap.
animal on shoulder: When an animal rests on a person's shoulder.
animal penis: Use this tag whenever an animal-type penis appears in the picture.
animal print: An article of clothing or an object that has a printed design of an animal, or is modeled after the fur or external appearance of an animal.
animal request: A request to identify animals in the post.
animal skeleton:
Any skeleton of an animal or other non-humanoid creature.

animal skull: The skull of an animal rather than a human. From a tagging point of view different mammalian skulls are easier to tell apart than others due to horns.
animal slippers: slippers in the stylized likeness of an animal. The canonical example is bunny slippers, but there are many variations.
animal-themed food:
food that is shaped like or themed after an animal.
For the opposite, see food-themed creature.
animal-themed umbrella: An umbrella designed after a particular animal.
animalization:
When a human or humanoid character (such as furries and humanoid robots) is depicted as an animal.
Not to be confused with animification, which is the depiction of non-anime characters in an anime art style. When the person is present too, add person and animalization.

animate object: The opposite of an inanimate object. When an object which is normally not alive is depicted as living. Doesn't apply to re-animated matter like corpses or zombies.
animated: An animated sequence, whether an animated gif, animated png, flash, ugoira, or video file. Posts should always be tagged one of these more specific tags in addition to animated.
animated gif:
A GIF image which has multiple frames. GIFs with only a single frame should not use this tag.
GIFs created from an episode of anime should also be tagged with anime screenshot.
animated png:
An animated image in the APNG format, an unofficial, backwards-compatible extension to the PNG format created by the group behind Mozilla/Firefox. Comparable to animated gif files, but with support for 24-bit colour and 8-bit transparency.
Not fully supported by all browsers. Internet Explorer and EdgeHTML-based Microsoft Edge will only display a preview image, but the animation should display properly in Firefox, Chrome (v. 59 onwards), SeaMonkey, Safari, Opera (prior to v. 15) or Chromium-based Edge.
animation paper:
Standardized paper used in the traditional hand-drawn animation process, usually features trim marks to show the framing of the cel, and punched holes at the top to be held in alignment with other sheets in an animation peg bar.
May feature differently colored line art (color trace) or annotations such as the scene number being depicted or timing information.  Sometimes seen in pre-production animatics giving a rough feel for the intended animation.
anime coloring:
A 2D rendering technique consisting of hard-edge shading, as opposed to any soft-edge coloring techniques, such as those prominent in painterly styles. 
It is the most common technique in 2D anime production. 
For the similar technique employed in artworks that are 3d - or that intentionally mimic 3D media - see cel rendering.
anime screenshot:
A still image of an animated sequence (usually animated gif or video), extracted from an anime.
For non-anime equivalents, such as stills from eroge or game cgs, see screenshot instead.
animedia: Animedia is a japanese monthly anime magazine by IID. It was first published on June 9, 1981.
animegao: Animegao (アニメ顔; anime face) is a mask designed to look like a human anime character, and is typically worn by cosplayer.
animification:
Non-anime characters depicted in an anime art style. This can apply to characters from live action television shows/movies, cartoons, western comics, and video games, as well as real people.
Does not apply to characters from western comics or cartoons that already have anime-like designs. (e.g. avatar: the last airbender, rwby, peni parker from spider-man: into the spider-verse)
Note: Some sites use the term "animification" to refer to art depicting humans or objects as animals. On Danbooru that concept is tagged as animalization.

ankh:
The ancient Egyptian hieroglyphic character that read "life". Egyptian gods are often portrayed carrying it by its loop, or bearing one in each hand, arms crossed over their chest.

ankle bell: A bell worn on the ankle- may be on an anklet (e.g. post #2577975) or tied on with a string/ribbon (e.g. post #2174305).
ankle boots: boots that don't stretch beyond the calf.
ankle bow: A bow tied at either one or both of a character's ankles. Often connected to an ankle strap.
ankle cuffs:
cuffs that are worn around the wearer's ankles.
Not to be confused with ankle garters.
For the metal cuffs used for restraint, see shackles.
ankle flower: A flower that is attached to an anklet and worn around the ankle.
ankle garter:
A frilly elastic band worn around the ankle.
Not to be confused with ankle cuffs.
ankle grab: grabbing an ankle, whether a character is doing it on themselves or another.
ankle lace-up:
cross-laced footwear with laces that wrap around the ankle, and often up to the shin or knee.

ankle ribbon: A decorative ribbon worn around the ankle(s) - similar to an anklet.
ankle scrunchie:
A scrunchie that is worn like an anklet around the ankle.
Not to be confused with an ankle garter.
ankle socks:
socks that are at "ankle length".
Despite the name, the tag refers to socks that are slightly above the ankles, not the extremely short ones that stop exactly at or below the ankles. They end before the shins, if they go over the shins, they become kneehighs.
Not to be confused with booties, a sock-like garment that is also ankle length.
See post #86570 for reference, read the translation notes.
ankle strap:
A strap worn around the ankle.
DO not confuse with anklet, which is jewellery worn on the ankle.
ankle wings: wings that are on a character's ankles or feet. They can be attached to the feet or footwear, or detached wings like in post #1644032.
ankle wrap: A strip of cloth (usually bandages) wrapped around the ankle.
anklet: A piece of jewelry, resembling a bangle or bracelet, but worn around the ankle.

anniversary:

annotated:

For characters that need to be tagged, use the character request tag instead.  To request annotations, use the annotation request tag.

annotation request: This tag is a request to label everyone in the image with translation notes. Once this has been done, change it to annotated.
announcement celebration: An artist's illustration to celebrate a series getting an additional season, anime adaptation, OVA, and/or manga serialization.

april:

bikesuit:
A type of bodysuit designed for riding a motorcycle.
Bikesuits are typically skin tight and cover the entire body except for the head, and have a zipper down the front. Bikesuits are often paired with boots, gloves and motorcycle helmets, and female characters are often drawn wearing them with the front partially or entirely unzipped.
bikini:
A bikini is a two-piece swimsuit for women, typically comprising a bra-like top and a panty-like bottom; however, the bottom can also be in the style of a bikini skirt or bikini shorts.
Bikinis come in a wide range of styles, with most designed to reveal more of the body, especially around the midriff and cleavage.
The key distinguishing feature of a bikini is that it prominently exposes the midriff, whereas other types of two-piece swimsuits may have a higher waistline and/or a top that extends further to cover the area.
bikini armor:
Skimpy, bikini-style armor.
Usually worn by attractive female warriors to maximize exposure of body parts such as cleavage, midriff, buttocks, hips, legs, etc. The top part covering the breasts is either a bikini top or, more commonly, is usually shaped much like a bikini top but with some obvious metal reinforcement marks. The bottom may be a bikini bottom, a short loincloth, a long loincloth, a skirt, full pants, or possibly some combination. Armored boots and capes can be expected, along with options like helmets, gauntlets, elbow pads, knee pads, shoulder pads, power suits, etc.
bikini around one leg: bikini around one leg, as opposed to both which would be bikini pull.
bikini bottom aside: bikini bottoms pushed to the side, to expose or give access to the vagina.
bikini bottom only:
Wearing a bikini bottom without a bikini top. For example, wearing a bikini bottom with a shirt or jacket, or while completely topless.
Don't use when you can't see the character's upper body, or you can't tell whether they're wearing a bikini top or not. This tag is for when you can tell they're not wearing a bikini top.
Don't use when the character is wearing a tankini, bandeau, or other bikini-like top.

bikini day: A day commemorating the bikini, celebrated on July 5.  French clothing designer Louis Réard unveiled the eponymous two-piece swimsuit on that date in 1946.

bindi:

bodice:
A close-fitting garment, often reinforced by stays, worn to support and shape the waistline, hips and breasts. A bodice is basically a corset that also covers the breasts.
Worn over the blouse, the bodice is a common piece of women's traditional dress among many European ethnic groups.
body armor:
Any form of modern protective gear that is worn over a person's body for protection against melee attacks (e.g. stabs), arrows, bullets, shrapnel, or frags. and Typically worn by military personnel, military operators, police officers, security guards, medics and reporters/journalists in warzones, sometimes worn by bodyguards.
Notable examples are Kevlar bulletproof vests, plate carriers that can contain ballistic plates, flak jackets, and the bulky bomb suits.
If the armor looks archaic or medieval, use armor instead.
body blush: Blushing of body parts other than the face due to embarrassment, heat, or otherwise.
body bridge: Also known as a "bridge position" in disciplines such as gymnastics and yoga. A stretch performed when someone's balancing on all fours with the body facing upward, resulting in an arched back and the abdomen being the highest point of the body.
body exploration: Characters examining their own or another person's genitals in a non-sexual manner, sometimes using a mirror. Different from masturbation.
body freckles: freckles scattered across a character's body. If the freckles are only on the character's face, just use freckles.
body fur: Fur on a character's body that isn't part of their clothing. If it's on the clothing, it should be tagged fur (clothing) instead. Commonly found on furry (anthropomorphic) characters.
body hair:
Hair in places other than the head and face, chest, armpits, pubic or anal regions, etc. 
Essentially, use this tag if there isn't a specific tag for the region of the body on which the hair is growing.
This tag applies regardless of the subject's gender. Unusually thick body hair may be tagged body fur, especially in monster boys and monster girls.
body horror: A subgenre of horror (theme) that intentionally showcases grotesque or psychologically disturbing violations of the human body. These violations may manifest through aberrant sex, mutations, mutilation, zombification, gratuitous violence, disease, or unnatural movements of the body.
body jewelry: Body jewelry is a style of clothing/jewelry that is worn as embellishment or as a lingerie piece. It typically includes gold, gems, chains, and/or beads covering intimate areas (or not). Usually it is the entire outfit, but it does not have to be and can be draped/worn over clothes.
body markings:
Permanent markings which can be seen on the skin of characters who have human anatomy but are typically either mutated, partially human, or a non-human.
Body markings on humans are also known as a birthmark. Unlike tattoo, these typically look like straight lines, random shapes and patterns, and markings found on animals.
body pillow:
A long pillow used for full-body support while sleeping, often by hugging it.
For images featuring body pillows that have an anime character on them instead of a simple design or pattern, use the dakimakura (object) tag instead.
body switch:
When two characters swap bodies.
This means the characters' entire identities (including memories etc) have been transferred to the other's body (in contrast to personality switch, where only the personality is switched).
There should be some clear indication that the swapping has taken place in the picture or in the commentary, otherwise it's just a personality switch.
A good example is post #4619026.
body writing: Words, characters or numbers written anywhere on the human body.
bodycon:
("bodikon," wasei-eigo for "body conscious")
A Japanese fashion of form-fitting clothing, typically tight minidresses. The look was pioneered in the 1990s by the dancers of the Shibaura nightclub, Juliana's. 
A pair of fans is a common bodycon accessory.
bodypaint:
Painted marks, symbols or designs on a person's body. Can be either full-bodied or various small marks. Often used by tribal cultures.
Not to be confused with paint on body which is for paint splatters on a character's body.
cammy white from street fighter shows an example of bodypaint, she has it as stripes on her legs.
Also tag as painted clothes if the paint is used to replace clothes.
See body writing for words written on the body.
bodystocking:
A bodystocking is similar to a bodysuit, but usually made of sheer material or soft fabric, while a bodysuit is more rigid and thick.
Think of it as a full-body pantyhose.
tharja (fire emblem) and isolated island oni are examples of characters who wear bodystockings.
bodysuit:
A skin tight, one-piece garment that covers the body from the neck to at least the upper legs.
Note that it has to be one piece of clothing, not separate pieces of clothing, such as a leotard over a pair of pantyhose.
If it covers only the upper body and not the legs, like a one-piece swimsuit, use leotard instead. If the fabric is obviously sheer or thin, use bodystocking instead.
bodysuit pull: When a bodysuit is partially removed from the character's body, but not entirely so that the removed portion is still hanging from the worn portion. Likewise, this can be used when the bodysuit is simply being tugged by either the wearer or someone else.
bodysuit under clothes: A bodysuit being worn under some other form of clothing.
boiling: The act of heating up a liquid (generally water) to the point of vaporization. steam and air bubbles are often present.
bojji:

bokeh:
A photographic effect where circular out-of-focus points of light appear in the background of the image.
Bokeh can represent known light sources in the background of an image, but can also occur in seemingly random places all over the image. The latter, known as orbs are from light reflected off of particles in the air which would otherwise not be visible.
lens flare artifacts can look similar to bokeh, but are due to bright light being reflected inside the camera, and don't line up with the original light source (which may not even be visible in the image).
bokken:
A lethal kendo practice sword made of solid, heavy wood. It's shaped and balanced like a katana. 
A bokken is a wooden weapon normally used for solo training, not for sparring. For that, the shinai is used, as sparring with a bokken will usually lead to broken bones... or worse. 
Legendary samurai swordmaster Musashi Miyamoto (1584? - May 19, 1645) fought and killed katana-wielding rival samurai by using just a bokken against them.
boku dake ga inai machi:

boku no hero academia: Boku no Hero Academia (僕のヒーローアカデミア My Hero Academia) is a manga series by horikoshi kouhei that has been serialized in shounen jump since 2014.
boku no kokoro no yabai yatsu: Bi-weekly romcom manga by sakurai norio, serialized from 2018. Received an anime adaptation that ran in 2023 and 2024.

bollard: A short, thick metal post sturdily set in the ground. Bollards are generally used to moor ships at docks, but use of the term has broadened to include similar posts used to control traffic or protect buildings and pedestrians from moving vehicles.
bolo tie:
A thin cord or braided strap, fed through a decorative clasp and secured around the neck in place of a necktie. Commonly associated in the US with Texas and other Western US fashion. Also known as a spaghetti tie.  
Not to be confused with cross ties, which are made out of a wider strap of fabric and commonly shorter than bolo ties; nor neck ribbons, which rather than being held together with a clasp are simply tied in a bow.
bolt action:
A type of gun mechanism by which the shooter has to manually cycle the action to chamber a new round for each time they need to shoot, by directly moving the bolt via a bolt handle (also known as a cocking handle). The earliest example of bolt-action gun that is fielded by an military is the Prussian dreyse needle gun

bone: The substance that forms the skeleton of the body. It is composed chiefly of calcium phosphate and calcium carbonate. It also serves as a storage area for calcium, playing a large role in calcium balance in the blood. There are 206 bones in the adult human body.

bookmark: Piece of cardboard or plastic inserted between the pages of a book used to a mark a point in the book the reader intends to restart from or refer to in a later time.

boom barrier: A barrier to prevent people from crossing a road or intersection. Common at security checkpoints and railroad crossings, and usually has either yellow-and-black or red-and-white hazard stripes.
boombox:

boomerang: A curved piece of wood or other similar material, most of which are designed to return to the thrower. Probably the most well known is the Australian version, although boomerangs in other shapes (and from other cultures) also exist. Boomerangs are used mainly as toys and hunting weapons.
boonie hat: A type of wide-brim sun hat commonly used by military forces in hot tropical climates. Its design is similar to a bucket hat but with a stiffer and flatter brim.
booth seating:

- dou (胴): A breastplate for chest & stomach protection.
- Tare (垂): A belt of heavy cloth flaps to protect the groin and waist.  The center flap often has a place for the name of who the competitor is representing.

- Sune-ate (すね当て):  Shin-guards.

Do not use this tag for a character who is a clone of another character, unless both are present in the scene.
Not to be mistaken for multiple views, where multiple images of the characters are independent, and do not react to one another, or inhabit a common environment.
clone harem:
When a character is romantically and/or sexually involved with more than one copy of a different character.
Note that despite the tag's name, the copies do not have to be completely identical (that is, they do not have to fall under the clone tag).
close-up: An image in which the subject is shown at very close range.
closed eyes: When a character has both eyes closed. If one eye is open, use one eye closed.
closed mouth: The opposite of open mouth, where the character is keeping their lips together and not showing any interior portion of the mouth.
closed umbrella: An umbrella or parasol that is not opened up.
closers: Closers Online - Dimension Conflict is a Korean cel shaded combat MOARPG released by NADDIC GAMES.
closet: Either a built-in wardrobe or a room with a door used for storing things, specially clothes.
closing door: An opened door that is in the process of being closed in the image.
cloth:
A piece of fabric adapted for a particular purpuse, usually related to cleaning. 
Don't use this tag on the following cases:
- If a cloth is used to cover the top of a table use tablecloth instead. Example: post #7826355
- If it's used to clean or dry a person use wash cloth or hand towel, respectively. Examples: post #1874434,  post #7553186
- If it's actively used to clean objects use cleaning rag. Example: post #6847143
- (post #7581533: red cloth)
- (post #6757310: white cloth)
cloth gag: A type of improvised gag made by wrapping a piece of cloth around the gagged person's head, with part of the cloth either in their mouth or covering it.
clothed after sex: When a character is shown putting their clothes back on (e.g. post #1660407, post #2431121) or already fully dressed (e.g. post #1645318) but with some obvious clues that they've very recently had sex or masturbated. Some common indicators are if they have cum pooling inside their clothes, or if they forgot to remove any stray pubic hairs. The character should have all of their clothes on or be at least mostly decent, to a level that they wouldn't have been during the actual sex act (i.e. there must have been some effort to get their clothes back in place after they finished).
clothed animal:
Non-anthropomorphic animals wearing human clothing.
Be careful not to confuse with anthropomorphic animals, who behave like people and naturally walk on two legs like people (not rearing).
clothed bath: For when a character is showering or bathing with clothes on.  Don't use this tag if they're wearing a swimsuit, just a towel, or just a pair of panties.
clothed female nude female: An image where one female is wearing clothes, with another who is nude.
clothed female nude male:
An image where the female is wearing clothes, but the male is nude. This is sometimes used to imply dominance.
The opposite of this is clothed male nude female.
clothed male nude female:
A picture where the male is wearing clothing, but the female is nude.
The opposite is clothed female nude male.
clothed male nude male: A situation where a male is fully clothed, but the other is nude.
clothed pokemon: A pokemon (creature) wearing clothes, including hats.
clothed robot:
A robot (humanoid or otherwise) wearing clothes.
Do not use this tag for androids or other especially human-like robots. As a rule of thumb, if it looks human enough that you'd expect it to wear clothes, it should not be given this tag.
clothed sex: sex where at least one participant is mostly wearing clothes. This can be any sex act, not just intercourse.
clothes:
Tag is used when clothes are seen but not worn (e.g. in a closet or scattered about). This may not include footwear.
Use unworn clothes and clothes in front instead where applicable.
clothes around waist: Any article of long-sleeved clothing tied around a character's waist.
clothes between breasts: When an article of clothing is nudged in between the breasts.
clothes between thighs: Clothing that is distinctly caught between the legs around the crotch area. Naturally a result of loose clothing like a skirt/dress or a pelvic curtain, but can also be utilized as a form of convenient censoring.
clothes down:
When the top part of clothing is still on, but pulled far down or almost taken off so as to expose a lot of skin. Also applies when there is only one clothing article, as with a jacket.
This tag is mainly for when shirt pull, open shirt, or either of these + off shoulder no longer cuts it.

clothes gag: An improvised gag made by stuffing clothing into the gagee's mouth. If the article of clothing is panties, you should also add the panty gag tag.
clothes grab: When a character grabs or holds on to their own or someone else's clothes, without the intent to move the clothing (i.e. exposing what's underneath or covering up, see shirt tug and shirt pull). Also describes lightly tugging on another character's clothes to get their attention, often by someone who is sad or pouting.
clothes hanger: An object meant to imitate human shoulders so clothes can be hung on it. It is triangular in shape, with a C-hook at the top.
clothes in front: A situation wherein a person holds a piece of clothing in front of their body to see how it would look without actually wearing it.
clothes in mouth: A piece of clothing being held in the mouth. Usually a type of clothes lift where the clothing is lifted by the wearer and held in their mouth.
clothes lift: Clothing that has been lifted up to reveal the breasts or crotch.
clothes on/clothes off: A character depicted in the same image in both a state of dress and undress. May overlap with variations.
clothes only:
For images that depict only articles of clothing, with no visible characters (wearing them or otherwise).

clothes pin: A clamped pin used for hanging laundry on a line, or for holding up hair.
clothes pull:
Clothing that has been pulled down to reveal the breasts or crotch.
See clothes lift for clothing that is lifted up to show the breasts or crotch, clothes tug for clothing that is tugged down to cover oneself, and clothes grab for grabbing or holding on to clothing without the intent to move it.
clothes rack: A rack for storing or displaying clothes, often seen in a retail setting.
clothes theft: Stealing the clothing of another character.
clothes tug: When an article of clothing is pulled with the intent of adjusting the fit of the clothing or to cover the wearer's body or other garments.
clothes writing:
Clothing that has writing on it, such as English, Japanese, Korean, and so on.
Do not confuse this tag with name tag.
clothesline: A rope or cord tied up outdoors to hang clothes on so they can dry.
clothing aside: Clothing normally worn over the genitals has been pulled aside to expose them, often for sexual activity of some kind.
clothing cutout: An intentional hole or opening in a piece of clothing designed to expose part of the body. For example, a cleavage cutout is a hole in the chest that exposes the breasts, while a navel cutout is a hole in the stomach that exposes the navel.
clothing request: Use this tag when the appropriate tag for clothing is unknown.
cloud: A cloud is a mass of water vapor that floats in the sky.
cloud focus: When clouds are the main focus, subject, or theme of the image.
cloud hair: Hair made out of or resemling clouds.
cloud hair ornament: A hair ornament or hairpin shaped like a cloud.
cloud print:
An article of clothing or anything made out of fabric that has the printed motif of clouds.
Add xiangyun if it's East-Asian styled - such as on post #6061447.
cloud strife:
The spikey-haired primary protagonist of final fantasy vii. An ex-S.O.L.D.I.E.R operative, now part of a rag-tag band of resistance known as Avalanche.
Also a supporting character in the kingdom hearts series, a fighter in super smash bros., and a hidden character in final fantasy tactics.
cloudy sky:
A sky with a significant amount of clouds. Use some common sense with this tag; a sky with only a few scattered clouds, like post #3442541 or post #3545927, is not a cloudy sky. As a general rule, this tag should only be used for skies that are at least 50% covered by clouds (topic #14412).
If the sky is completely covered by clouds, use overcast instead.
clover:
Any plants in the genus Trifolium, usually with leaves of three leaflets and flowers that have spiked petals.
A shamrock is a type of clover that is the national symbol of ireland.
clover earrings: A pair of earrings shaped to resemble a clover, usually one with four leaves.
clover hair ornament:
A hair ornament that's shaped like a clover, regardless if it has three or four leaves.
For the clover-shaped card symbol, see club hair ornament.
clover theater: Clover Theater is a video game.
clow card:
Clow Cards are magical cards in cardcaptor sakura.
Each of them has a "true form", who appears when kinomoto sakura calls the cards to use their magical powers. Most true forms are personifications; they are girls with colorful themed costumes. Except some, who are animals or creatures instead, such as The Fly (a bird), The Thunder (a giant dog), etc.
All the true forms are seen together in post #1103127.
The Clow Cards were created by the clow reed, in their backstory. At some point in the story, the cards change appearance to become pink-ish Sakura Cards.
clown:
A general term for a person who entertains others with their funny appearance, words, and actions. There are various forms all over the world, such as street performers, circus clowns, Pierrot of commedia dell'arte, the jesters of medieval Europe, kabuki dōkekata, and so forth.
For tagging purposes, this tag is reserved for circus clowns. For other varieties, please tag accordingly.
clown nose: A spherical, usually red, costume accessory made of foam or rubber worn over the nose by circus clowns.
clownfish: A small, warm-water marine fish, colored red, orange, yellow, or black, with white bars or patches belonging to the subfamily Amphiprioninae. Commonly associated with sea anemones, with which they live in a mutually beneficial relationship.
clownpiece: touhou character introduced as the stage five boss in legacy of lunatic kingdom. Later appeared as a prominent character in the manga Visionary Fairies in Shrine. A Hell fairy and subordinate of hecatia lapislazuli.
cloyster:
Pokémon #091 in the National Pokédex.
Evolves from shellder.
Japanese name: Parshen
Prior Pokémon: shellder
Next Pokémon: gastly
club hair ornament: A hair ornament shaped like a club (shape) (♣).
clubroom: A room within a school where students can engage in various club-related activities such as music, art and games.
clueless: A character being oblivious to the situation around them, for instance being oblivious to another's advances.
clumsy:
A character making a mistake due to their clumsiness, lack of attention, etc. A good example is when a character gets tangled up in their legs and falls. 
It's not the same as you're doing it wrong, where normally the error happens due to lack of knowledge of the character rather than clumsiness.
clutching chest: A character is gripping or clawing at their own chest.
coaster: A coaster is a small, circular object typically made of cork or PVC plastic. It is designed to protect surfaces (particularly wood) from staining or other water damage caused by the condensation on cups and drinking glasses.
coat:
A long garment worn for warmth, protection or fashion. Coats are made from thick material, therefore they have weight.
Coats tend to be longer than jackets. A jacket goes to the waist or hip. A coat goes down to thighs or past that.
They often feature lapels.
coat dress: A tailored dress typically fastening down the front and resembling a coat.
coat of arms: Originally heraldic insignias unique to a noble person, his family or a religious order, the idea of having a coat of arms has been adopted by the governments that succeeded them. Many countries, provinces or military units directly inherited the heraldic arms owned by their former lords, but even countries that were never feudal have taken to creating coats of arms for their governmental bodies, provinces and military units.
coat on shoulders:
A  coat draped over the shoulders, rather than worn with the arms in the sleeves.
While this may be done for a variety of reasons, the most common reasons are to cover up oneself, use as an improvised blanket to stay warm, or use as an improvised cloak or cape.
coattails: Flaps at the back of a coat that are not joined together but continue to extend past the waist area.
cobblestone: A naturally rounded stone, larger than a pebble and smaller than a boulder, formerly used in paving streets. Cobblestones were largely replaced by setts in the 19th century.
coca-cola: The world-famous carbonated soft drink (soda) produced and manufactured by The Coca-Cola Company. Also known simply as Coke.
cock ring: A ring at the base of the penis that constricts blood flow to help maintain an erection. Some vibrate.
cockatiel:
Scientific name: Nymphicus hollandicus 
Japanese: オカメインコ (阿亀鸚哥)
A bird native to Australia, popular as a pet. A number of different color mutations exist, but cockatiels can usually be identified by their orange cheek patches.
cocked eyebrow: One eyebrow raised, one lowered. Similar to raised eyebrow, but with one eyebrow down as well as one up.
cocked hammer: A gun with the hammer cocked back, ready to fire.
cocking gun:
A general term for a variety of actions used to chamber/prime guns before firing them. This may include:
- Manually pulling back the hammer of a revolver
- Racking the slide of a semi-automatic handgun
- Racking the slide of a pump action shotgun
- Cycling the bolt of a bolt action rifle
Usually performed after loading a magazine to chamber the first round, but can also forcibly remove an existing round or clear a jam. May also depict a handgun slide being forced back during normal operation for dramatic effect.
cockpit:
A cockpit (also called flight deck in big airplanes) is the area, usually near the front of a vehicle, from which its pilot controls it. 
Most modern cockpits are enclosed, except on some small aircraft, and cockpits on large airliners are also physically separated from the cabin. From the cockpit an aircraft is controlled on the ground and in the air.
Most mecha also contain cockpits for a human operator.
cockroach:
Common insect pest, often censored for comic effect. In Japan, the word for them is "gokiburi", sometimes shortened to G -- especially by terrified girls who don't even want to speak their name.
Contrary to popular belief it is not poisonous and thus easy to handle manually.
cockroach girl: An arthropod girl based off of a cockroach.
cocktail: A mixed drink, usually a mixture of alcohol with fruit juice, flavored syrups, cream, or other ingredients. Usually served in a specialized cocktail glass, but an ordinary drinking glass may be used as well. More exotic cocktails are typically garnished with fruit and flowers and may be served in a coconut shell.
cocktail dress: A dress suitable at semi-formal clothes occasions, sometimes called cocktail parties.
cocktail glass:
A drinking glass with a long stem and a wide conical bowl, designed to serve cocktails such as martinis.
When using this tag, pay attention to the shape of the glass bowl. Not every glass containing a cocktail is a cocktail glass.
cocktail shaker: A device for shaking and mixing alcoholic beverages. Filling the shaker with ice allows the drink to be quickly chilled before serving.
cocktail umbrella: A miniature paper umbrella often used as a garnish for elaborate tropical beverages.
coco bandicoot: Coco Bandicoot is the young sister of crash bandicoot.
coco's:
The uniforms, buildings and logo of Coco's, a Japanese casual dining restaurant chain. It is run by Coco's Japan, a consolidated subsidiary of Zensho.
For the brand name's origin in the United States, use coco's bakery.
Not to be confused with coco ichibanya, a completely separate and unrelated restaurant chain.
coconut:
The fruit of the coconut palm. It has a hard brown shell, which holds edible white flesh; the liquid inside the cavity is called coconut milk. The entire fruit is covered by a fibrous outer husk which is usually removed before the coconut is further processed.
Coconuts vary in appearance, ranging from having a smooth green shell, to a yellow one, and of course the common brown color that is covered in bark strips.
coconut tree: A type of palm tree that coconuts grow on.
cocoon:
An outer casing produced by many larval insects, such as caterpillars, for the purpose of metamorphosis into adulthood.
Can also refer to things that are completely covered and bound for other reasons, such as prey caught by a spider.
Frequently used in fiction as a means to achieve mutations, evolution, or other growths and transformations.

code geass: lost stories: A code geass game developed by f4samurai and DMM Games. Launched for smartphones and browser in 2022.
code vein: An anime themed souls-like game developed and published by Bandai Namco in 2019.
codpiece:
Literally "bag piece" or "scrotum piece" in Old English.
A covering flap or pouch enclosing the male genital area, attached to the crotch region of pants or some other garment. Essentially the European equivalent of a penis sheath.
Most codpieces are made out of cloth or leather, though metal ones also exist, sculpted to fit a man's scrotum and penis.
coefont: An online text-to-speech service developed by CoeFont Co.,Ltd. The company's name was changed from Yellston in 2021.
coelacanth: A fish. Famous for once being thought to have gone extinct around 66 million years ago, but were rediscovered in 1938 off the coast of south africa. Ovoviviparous, only two species survive, both critically endangered. They are easy to spot because of their strange appearance; however not all primitive or strange-looking fishes should be tagged as coelacanth. They are lobe-finned fish (from where tetrapods come), as opposed to the most common ray-finned fishes.
cofagrigus:
Pokémon #563 in the National PokéDex, a Ghost type Pokémon.
Cofagrigus is a blue and yellow sarcophagus with red, menacing eyes and four ebony hands that appear to be shadows. A simply designed face is prominent on the "forehead" of the Pokémon.
coffee:
A hot drink that is made by filtering hot water through ground coffee beans, popular for its aroma and concentrated dose of caffeine. Use this tag when coffee itself (ordinarily a black or dark brown liquid) is visible in an image.
It is normally served in a porcelain coffee mug, but it can be taken on the go in a stainless steel mug, styrofoam cup, or in a paper disposable coffee cup. For the traditional porcelain or ceramic "coffee cups" that aren't mug-shaped, see teacup.
As coffee can be quite bitter, it is often served accompanied by sugar and milk or cream.
coffee beans: Refers to the seeds that coffee is extracted from. Not actually a type of bean, despite the name.
coffee grinder: A machine used to grind roasted coffee beans into a fine powder that can be used for brewing coffee. Most of the posts with this tag depict old-fashioned manual grinders.
coffee maker: Any type of appliance used to brew coffee from coffee beans.
coffee mug: A type of mug that holds about 2 cups of hot coffee. It's made of ceramic or glass and designed to be thick enough to be able to hold the hot beverage in the hands.
coffee pot:
A container designed for serving coffee. This may mean:
- A small pourable pot, usually glass or metal, that is placed under a coffee brewer to capture the finished product and dispense it into a coffee mug.
- A metal or ceramic vessel similar in design to a teapot, but tall and slender, usually with a long spout attached near the base.
coffee table: A low table, typically placed in front of a couch.
coffin:
A commonly 6-sided funerary box with removable lid used in the display and containment of dead people, either for burial or cremation.
Vampires often sleep inside this container.
For a 4-sided funerary box with hinged lid, see casket.
coif:
A coif ('kwaff') is a close fitting cap of medieval origins worn by both men and women that covers the top, back, and sides of the head. Sometimes had long, dangling fabric called lappets.

coiled: Snake (or similar) body rolled or twisted to support to itself.
coin: A round metal disk used as money.
coin flip: Someone is flipping a coin, possibly in order to choose between two options.
coin hair ornament: A hair ornament shaped like a coin.
coin on string:
A coin on a string, usually used in hypnosis.
Alternatively seen on onozuka komachi's sash.
coin purse: A small handbag with no shoulder strap, designed for carrying coins or small objects.
coke-bottle glasses:
Distinctive round glasses with a swirly pattern that often obscure the wearer's eyes. A simple, distinguishing item for otaku or nerdy characters.
The naming comes from the thickness of the lens being reminiscent of looking through the thick bottom of glass coca-cola bottles.
cola:
A type of soda drink that is colored brown and flavored with an extract of cola nuts. coca-cola and pepsi are the world's most well-known producers of cola.
This tag is for cola depicted in an image that does not specify a brand.
cold: When a character is affected by cold temperatures.
cold pack: An adhesive pad treated with chemicals that produce a cooling sensation, commonly stuck to the forehead as a topical treatment for headache.  In art, they are frequently used as a visual shorthand to show that a character has been working hard at some intellectually challenging task, and/or is ill and feverish.
colette brunel: The main heroine of tales of symphonia, and Lloyd's childhood friend/primary love interest. The Chosen of Mana of the world of Sylvarant, beneath Colette's dojikko exterior lies a responsible young girl who would go to extremes to make sure her friends do not worry about her.
collaboration request: Used along with artist request when not all artists of an artist collaboration are known.
collage: A collection of several images in one, usually of screencaps or characters drawn by different artists.
collar:
A band worn around the neck as a fashion accessory.
This tag is for standalone collars not part of a shirt. Do not use this tag for collared shirts, collared dresses, wing collars, sailor collars, etc.
Not to be confused with a choker, which is usually tighter-fitting and made of thinner material.
collar grab: When a character grabs another by the collar of their shirt, usually to threaten or attack them, but can happen with a kiss.
collar jewel:
gem attached to a collar.
If it could swing or flap, it is also a pendant collar.
collar tabs: insignia in the form of paired patches of cloth or metal attached/sewn on the collar of a uniform (gorget). Used in the police, military and civil service in some countries. Collar tabs sign the military insignia (group of ranks), the rank of civil service, the military unit, the office (department) or the branch of armed forces and the arm of service.
collar tug:
When the collar of any piece of clothing is pulled down or out, often to indicate that a character is feeling hot and is getting fresh air into their clothes or as a sign of nervousness.
Not to be confused with shirt pull or any other form of clothes pull, which is used for when a character intentionally pulls down on the collar of a shirt/dress/etc. to reveal the cleavage, breasts or pectorals, although sometimes it may come as a result of a collar tug, in which case it should be tagged as both, and even as accidental exposure if it applies.
collar x malice:
An Otome game developed by Design Factory Co., Ltd. & otomate for the Playstation Vita and Nintendo Switch. It was released in 2016.
The game follows hoshino ichika (collar x malice), a policewoman who works in Shinjuku, which had become a dangerous city after a series of brutal incidents popularly …
collarbone: Describes images depicting characters with fully or partially exposed collarbones (clavicles).
collared cape: A cape with a folded collar.
collared coat: A coat with a folded collar.
collared dress: A dress with a folded collar.
collared jacket:
Any style of jacket with a prominent collar.
Not to be confused with jackets that only have lapels, such as blazers or suit jackets.
collared leotard: A leotard with a folded collar.
collared shirt:
A shirt with a folded collar. 
Do not tag collar or any colored collar tags (e.g. white collar) for a given collared shirt. Those tags are for neck collars.
collared shrug:
A shrug with an attached collar; think of a detached collar that spans the shoulders at minimum, and covers a majority of the arms at maximum.
- (post #6997761)
collared vest: A vest that has a distinctive folded collar around the neckline. May involve the popped collar tag as well.
colonel sanders: Harland David Sanders (September 9, 1890 – December 16, 1980) was the founder of the fast-food chain Kentucky Fried Chicken (KFC). Always at odds with ronald mcdonald in fan works.
color connection:
When characters and/or objects are grouped together based upon their theme color, or one character is referencing or cosplaying as another who shares the same theme color.
If multiple different color groups are present at the same time, (e.g. post #2996021), use color coordination instead.
color contrast:
An image with strongly contrasting or opposing colors.
Opposing colors contrast with each other more than any other color pair, making both colors appear brighter, or to bring focus to a certain part of the image.
color coordination:
Characters and/or objects match each other in color, or create a sense of symmetry.
The characters/objects must be put into multiple pairs/groups based on their color to create the sense of "coordination". If there is only one group of characters/object put together based on their color, use color connection and the corresponding "color theme":/tags?search[namematches]=theme&search[category]=0&search[hideempty]=yes&search[order]=name&commit=Search if applicable.
color drain: When a character or comic frame turns monochrome in reaction to something. Indicates shock, anger, horror, despair, or a broken mind.
color guide: A palette of colors of an image shown within itself. In the context of printing, these are known as color bars and are used to measure print quality.
color halftone:
An effect that can be seen when printed media is scanned at very high resolution, causing solid colors to appear as dotted patterns.
For more information on how to remove screening from scans, see: "yande.re forum #2007":[https://yande.re/forum/show/2007], "yande.re forum #2290":[https://yande.re/forum/show/2290].
color switch:
Similar to a costume switch, except the character has retained their original costume, but switched their colors with someone else's.
Not to be confused with palette swap, which refers to a single character's palette being changed.
color timer: A light bulb-like instrument usually attached on an Ultraman's chest. Emitting a steady, blue light at full power, it blinks red if an Ultraman is running out of power or if he is approaching to his time limit. If the Color Timer stops emitting light, it signals either the death of an Ultraman or he'll simply reverts back to his human form.
color trace:
lineart drawn in different colors.
Traditionally done with colored pencil  in the animation pre-production process, often on animation paper, and used in the production of animatics.  The different colors indicate things like highlights that would be painted in different layers.
Use colored lineart instead for fully colored pieces.
color wheel challenge: A twitter artist challenge consists of drawing various characters to fit into the seven rainbow + pink color wheels.
colored condom: Condom with a distinct coloration instead of the usual transparent.
colored extremities:
A type of multicolored skin where extremities are differently colored than the rest of the body. Commonly seen in the hands and/or feet of a demonic character fading to black. This can be anything from only the finger tips being discolored to extending from the toes all the way to the thigh and be a gradual fade or sharp transition.
This does not include wearing wearing gloves or socks, nor feathers, fur or scales on differently colored skin (If the skin underneath fades to match the color it does count).
colored eyelashes:
Non-black eye outlines, with or without prominent eyelashes. Consider adding eyelashes only in the former case.
Not to be confused with eyeshadow.
colored eyepatch: An eyepatch that is not black or white.
colored inner animal ears: When the inside of the ears is an unusual colour that doesn't match natural fleshy colours or the character's hair/fur.
colored inner hair:
Hair that is a different color on the inside than on the outside.
If each side consists of a single color then it is also two-tone hair.
colored lineart:
Lineart that is distinctly a different color other than black. This should be noticeable from the thumbnail.

Do not use if there's regular lineart with a colored outline - use the corresponding outline tag instead, e.g. pink outline. (post #3049904)
Do not use for images of uncolored animation frames, use color trace instead.
colored nipples: Uncommonly-colored nipples or areolae (i.e., not the typical human range of pink to brown).
colored pencil: Colored pencils appearing as objects in the picture.  For images created using colored pencils as the art medium, see colored pencil (medium).
colored pubic hair:
Unnaturally colored pubic hair, such as white, green, pink, or red. Don't use this tag if the hair is black, brown, or any other natural color and if the pubic hair is barely noticeable.
Use mismatched pubic hair when the pubic hair color doesn't match the color of hair on the head.
colored sclera: When the sclera - the white part of the eye - is a color other than white.
colored shadow: A shadow in any color that isn't black. If it's black, just use shadow alone.
colored shoe soles:
Outsoles that do not match the body and are colored, white on non-sneakers, or black on white footwear.
This tag does not implicate shoe soles since the bottom side surface may not be significantly visible, particularly high heels which are most likely able to apply this tag from non-below angles compared to other footwear.
Avoid this tag when:
- feet lie flat and the toes are facing directly toward or away from the viewer resulting in a tiny amount of visible soles.
- the footwear is viewed from above in standing position.
colored skin: Skin that is any color that would be unnatural for a normal human. Often seen on fantasy races, furries, demon girls, demon boys, aliens, zombies, and other not-entirely-human characters.
colored smoke: smoke that appears to be colored other than white, grey, or black.
colored speech bubble: speech bubble that is colored any color other than black or white.
colored stripes: Stripes of only two colors, with neither stripe being white. For more than two colors, use multicolored stripes.
colored tips:

colosseum:
Originally the Flavian Amphitheatre, an elliptical amphitheatre in the centre of the city of rome (city), italy, the largest ever built in the Roman Empire, built of concrete and stone. It is considered one of the greatest works of Roman architecture and Roman engineering and is also famous as a gladiatorial arena. The name is derived from the Colossus of Rhodes, a giant statue of Apollo which stood near (but not inside) the Amphitheatre.
Note that this tag is not limited to the real life colosseum, as it also includes fantastical depictions of an arena inspired after the real life arena.
colt single action army:
A six-shot single-action revolver, developed by Colt's Patent Fire Arms Manufacturing Company starting in 1869, adopted (in its .45 Colt chambering) as the official sidearm of the United States Army in 1872, and mass-produced starting in 1873.
The military version was called the Single Action Army, Model 1873, for reasons that should be obvious; its proper civilian product name when first introduced was "New Model Army Metallic Cartridge Revolving Pistol", which, astonishingly, failed to catch on. Common nicknames include "Peacemaker" and "The Gun That Won the West".

different reflection:
When something in the reflection in a mirror or any reflective surface does not match up with what viewers realistically expect, for instance showing a character's dual persona.

diffraction spikes:

sparkle, glint, and diffraction spikes all refer to similar patterns of bright lines radiating from a point. They are not clearly differentiated, and usage tends to be context-sensitive. In general:
- sparkle is considered the base case. Usually four lines at right angles radiating from a point. Associated with eyes, liquid or particulate matter (e.g. raindrops, snow, sand), or nothing (appearing mid-air).

dirigible:
A type of aircraft, usually cigar-shaped, that floats by means of a large balloon, usually filled with hydrogen or helium.
There are three types of dirigibles:
- Blimps have a non-rigid airframe; its shape is maintained by the pressure of the gas within.
- Zeppelins have a rigid airframe which holds its shape even when uninflated. Zeppelins are named after their pioneer, Ferdinand von Zeppelin.
- Semi-rigid, a hybrid of the other two.
On Danbooru, dirigible refers to real life floating aircraft; for fantasy airships, see airship.

The position of the apron bow can indicate a woman's marital status:
- Bow on left: Single
- Bow on right: Married
- Bow in middle: Virgin
- Bow in back: Widow (or waitress)

emoji:
Emoji are Unicode characters designed to represent pictograms and emoticons. The term itself, however, is most often used to refer to the pictograms and emoticons themselves. The word "Emoji" comes from the Japanese word "絵" (e, "picture") + "文字" (moji, "character"). Its resemblance to the word "emoticon" is purely coincidental.
Emoji as we know them originated as a proprietary system by a Japanese mobile phone operator ntt docomo using a Unicode private-use block to encode their emoticons.

emphasis lines:
Lines drawn in a burst pattern, radiating outward from a part of the image to which the artist wants to draw attention. They cause the area surrounded by the lines to stand out more in the viewer's eye.
These are not the same as speed lines, which indicate motion; emphasis lines indicate focus, rather than motion.
A similar technique used in filmography is to focus the camera toward a specific part of the shot (sometimes off-center) while allowing other parts of the image to become unfocused, thus drawing extra attention to the focused area.

energy barrier:
