This can include text on clothes (like post #357728) or an accessory moving as if it was part of the character's body (like post #432551).
expressive hair:
Hair that is an extension of expressing certain emotion, such as excitement or depression. Signified by flapping, lowering, or (in the case of an ahoge) forming a heart ahoge.
Not to be confused with prehensile hair, when hair is being actively used as a ligament, tool or weapon.
extended downblouse: A downblouse where more than just cleavage is visible, such as the chest or lower abdomen. Also includes when a gap between the legs or a large area of the inside of the surrounding clothing is visible. See post #1706712 for an example.
extra:
Instead of using this tag, consider creating the appropriate chartag for the character you're trying to identify.
- If the character has an official name or a widely used fan name, simply use that: for example, tachibana himeko
- If the character is part of an organization, you can use the organization's name: for example, justice task force member (blue archive)
- If the character has no affiliation, use their major traits to name the tag: for example, dark haired kappa, office lady (madoka magica)
To create a character tag, simply write "char:" followed by the tag you want to create.
extra arms:
Having more than two arms. For example: a humanoid having a 3rd arm growing out of them, a cyborg having a added mechanical arm, or a monster having additional pairs of arms, such as machamp.
Do not use this tag for tentacles.
extra breasts: When a character has more than two breasts.
extra digits:
Having more than five fingers or toes. Usually an artistic error which amateur and professional artists alike are prone to on occasion. Earlier versions generative AI are especially infamous for getting hands wrong this way. When not an error, extra fingers can often be found on mutant or otherwise monstrous humanoids.
Polydactyly is a real, albeit rare, genetic condition. Human characters with polydactyly include:
- hannibal lecter - the silence of the lambs (novel)
- Count Tyrone Rugen - the princess bride
- iwamoto kogan - shigurui
- stanford pines - gravity falls
extra ears:
A character possessing both human ears and animal ears.
fake animal ears do not count.
For a character with more than one pair of animal ears, see multiple animal ears.
extra eyes: Characters with more than the standard two eyes. Extra eyes must be integrated on the body (e.g. no floating eyeballs such as komeiji satori) for the tag to apply.
extra faces: When a character is shown with more than one face. This is distinct from multiple heads in that the additional faces may be located on somewhere else that doesn't necessitate an extra head, such as the side of the head, chest, stomach, etc..
extra hands: When a character is having more than a pair of hands. Typically an artistic error, though some characters does possess extra arms also has extra hands in the process. Some, such as nico robin, can spawns an additional hands at will.
extra legs:
A character with more legs than normal.
These additional legs should be abnormal for the character, such as a human having a third leg. If the legs are normal, such as a spider girl having eight legs, then use the multiple legs tag instead.
extra mouth: A character having more mouths than they're usually depicted with.
extra penises: A single character having more than one penis.
extra pupils: For when eyes have more than one pupil per eyeball.
extra tails: When a character is depicted with more tails than usual. Not to be confused with the multiple tails tag for characters who have their normal amount of tails.
extraction: An image of a character or group of characters that has been taken from another image and has had all other characters, objects, and backgrounds removed from it.
extreme dangling: When a girl is dangling her shoe in a very extreme manner, so like when it seems like her shoe is about to fall off
extreme gaping:
gaping to an extreme degree. 
Use this tag when the gaping hole is larger than the character's own fist.
eye beam: A common attack used in anime, notably in the dragon ball series, where the character uses energy fired from their eyes to attack.
eye black: Eye black is a grease or strip applied under the eyes to reduce glare, although studies have not conclusively proven its effectiveness. It is often used by American football, baseball, softball, and lacrosse players to mitigate the effects of bright sunlight or stadium floodlights.
eye contact:
Two characters looking directly into each others eyes. Not for images where two people simply face each other, avert their gaze, or are looking at the viewer.
Not to be confused with contact lens, which can be referred to as an "eye contact".
eye focus: When a picture has a focus on eyes, or the eyes are especially well drawn.
eye mask: A piece of cloth that goes over the eyes, but leaves them exposed. Commonly seen on bandits, superheroes, and zorro.
eye of horus:
An ancient egyptian symbol, also known as the eye of wadjet, wedjat, or udjat.
Often refers to a specific tattoo visible on pharah (overwatch) from overwatch or an Egyptian motif from yu-gi-oh! series.
eye of providence: A symbol originating in medieval Christian iconography, representing the "all-seeing eye of God". It is an eye enclosed by a triangle, usually emitting rays of light. It is commonly recognized today for its depiction on the reverse of the American one-dollar bill.
eye of senri: A symbol originating in len'en, consisting of three semicircles - one white, two black - that share a straight edge. The Eye of Senri's significance is not currently known, but it is a recurring element in Len'en character designs.
eye pop: When a character's eyes pop out of their sockets, usually due to surprise or shock. A common gag in classic Western cartoons. Essentially a more extreme version of bulging eyes.
eye print: Clothing or a fabric item that has the printed design of an open eye.
eye reflection: A reflection of an object visible in someone's eyes.
eye socket:
A concave, semispherical depression in a skull which houses the eye.
Visible if the eye had been removed.
eye tattoo:
A tattoo that depicts an eye.
For makeup on and around the eyelid, see eyeshadow or eyeliner.
eye trail:
A glowing light trail following a character's eyes. Often used to show anger or determination.
Although there's overlap with glowing eyes, the two tags should not be confused together.
eyeball:
Eyes are organs that detect light, and give visual stimulation.
Tag can be used when eyeballs have a strong or obvious presence in the picture, such as floating, being held, scattered around, on characters' attire, in foreheads, etc.
Examples:
- backbeard the giant floating eyeball from gegege no kitarou
- nightmare (soulcalibur) with his Soul Edge sword, which has a large eye near it's hilt.
eyeball hair ornament: A hair ornament or hairpin shaped like an eyeball.
eyebrow cut:
An eyebrow grooming style where one or more thin vertical stripes are shaved from one or both eyebrows. Also called slits or notches.
Commonly with scar across eye.
eyebrows: Most characters on danbooru have eyebrows. Use a better tag for unusual eyebrows instead, such as:
eyebrows hidden by hair: When a character's eyebrows are fully or partially hidden behind bangs or any form of hair. They should not be showing through, as if the hair is translucent, in any way.
eyecatch: The frames before and after the commercial break in the middle of the show and usually illustrated by the production studio doing the show or official illustrators of the series. Mostly also bears the show's logo.
eyelash ornament:
Cosmetic embellishments designed for decorating the wearer's eyelashes.
Not the same as fake eyelashes.
eyelashes: For use when a character's eyelashes were given a particular attention by the artist.
eyeliner: A type of eye makeup. Eyeliner is applied in a line along or near the lash line to define the eyes or create a cat eye effect.
eyepatch: A small flap or strip of cloth worn over an eye to protect it from damage or to cover up an injured eye. Favored by assassins, pirates, and warlords.
eyepatch bikini: A strapless bikini where the top consists of two square-cut pieces of fabric resembling a medical eyepatch and held together with two parallel straps. Often seen in a micro bikini size that only barely covers the nipples.
eyepatch lift: When an eyepatch that is being worn is lifted to show the eye (or lack thereof) underneath.
eyes in shadow:
When the eyes of someone or something stand out (can be seen) while the area surrounding the eyes are covered in shadows that completely obscure all details. Think "glowing eyes peering out of a cave" level of darkness.
Not to be confused with shaded face, faceless, or hair over eyes.
eyes of grima:
Distinctive pattern of six stylized eyes associated with the Fell Dragon Grima from fire emblem. This pattern is sometimes found on clothing and tattoos worn by characters associated with the Theocracy of Plegia in fire emblem awakening.
As the 'eyes' are often split into two groups of three on either sides of a character's clothing (with only one side being visible), the presence of two to three such eyes should generally suffice to tag eyesofgrima.
Avoid tagging this if the eyes are barely visible (i.e.
eyes visible through eyewear: Eyes visible through tinted eyewear with dark degree of tint and other garments that cover the eyes, such as blindfolds.
eyes visible through hair:
When a person's eyes should be obscured by their hair, but are somehow not. An artistic quirk seen in some anime-styled drawings.
Includes when only the eyelashes are visible through the hair.
eyeshadow: A type of eye makeup. A colored powder applied to the eyelids to make the eyes stand out or look more attractive.
eyeshield 21: Eyeshield 21 (アイシールド21, romanized as Aishīrudo Nijūichi) is a Japanese manga series written by Inagaki Riichiro and illustrated by Murata Yuusuke. Its 333 chapters have spawned a 145-episode anime, two OVAs, music albums, videogames and miscellaneous merchandise.
eyewear around neck:
Eyewear worn around a character's neck, e.g. glasses that are attached to a necklace.
For eyewear hanging on clothes, see eyewear hang.
eyewear hang: glasses or sunglasses hanging from a piece of clothing, to hold them while they're not being worn. Usually this is glasses hung from the neck of a shirt, but in general it can be any piece of clothing.
eyewear in mouth: When a character is holding eyewear with their mouth.
eyewear on head: When a character is wearing a pair of eyewear on their head rather than over their eyes.
eyewear on headwear: When a character is wearing a pair of eyewear on their headwear or hat rather than over their eyes.
eyewear strap:
A strap attached to eyewear to prevent them from falling off during movement.
This doesn't include eyepatches or monocles because they're generally attached to a strap, string or wire by default.
eyewear switch: Used when either a character is trying on another character's eyewear while the original owner is present in the image, or when two characters wear each others' eyewear.
eyewear view: When the point of view is through the lenses of a pair of glasses or goggles. This is often used where the glasses impart some sort of special view to the viewer (e.g. x-ray vision or reverse x-ray vision).
ezio auditore da firenze:
Protagonist of assassin's creed ii and its sequels assassin's creed: brotherhood and assassin's creed: revelations, and ancestor of desmond miles. He at one point becomes the Mentor of the Assassin Brotherhood in Italy.
His attire is a bit more elaborate than Altaïr and consists of a side cape.
ezreal: A human Champion from Piltover in league of legends usually played as an AD carry. He is known for his arcane magical prowess and equally significant pluckiness, as well as his exploring and excavating feats. Hinted to be in a romantic relationship with lux (league of legends).
f-14 tomcat:
The Grumman F-14 "Tomcat" was a large and heavy twin-engine jet fighter-interceptor, first of the "Teen" series of US jet fighters and the last "Cat" manufactured by Bethpage, New York-based Grumman "Iron Works" Aerospace Corporation. The swing-wing two-seater entered service with its main user, the united states navy, in 1974 and was retired in 2006. However, iran, the only country that the F-14 was exported to (prior to the 1979 revolution), still operates the type with local modification.
The F-14 is widely recognized in various forms of pop culture.
f-15 eagle: The Boeing F-15 Eagle is a twin-engined fighter jet developed by McDonnell Douglas (now part of Boeing). It is one of the most easily recognized of the "Teen" series of fighters, with its prominent bubble canopy, dual vertical tailfins, sawtoothed elevators, and broad delta wing. It was designed in the 1960-1970s under the Fighter Experimental program as a replacement for the f-4 phantom ii and to counter aircraft like the mig-25 with record-setting climb performance and impressive top speed while retaining good dogfight capability.
f-22 raptor:
The Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor is an American fifth generation single-seat, twin-engine state-of-the-art advanced fighter aircraft that uses stealth technology. It was designed primarily as an air superiority fighter, but has several additional capabilities that include ground attack, electronic warfare and reconnaissance. 
The F-22 was developed from the original YF-22 prototype flight tested during 1990. The first mass produced F-22s first flew in 1997 and were officially introduced several years later in 2005.
f-ism: F-ism, a series of art booklets by Murakami Suigun, featuring erotic CGs with original characters.
f-zero: A series of futuristic racing games by nintendo.

fabric: A piece of cloth that has not yet been sewn into a finished object (including but not limited to clothing, curtains, and toys). Do not use for fabric where the raw edges have been finished such as with hemming or a fringe.
fabulous:
Used for male characters who are flamboyant and campy in their style and actions; applicable to men of any sexual persuasion, and of any physical build. Notably attractive to rampant sparkles, rainbows, bishie sparkles, and/or pastel colors.
The term "fabulous" for describing such flamboyant characters can be traced to a meme involving the mannerisms of koizumi itsuki of The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya and the theatricality of lelouch vi britannia (particularly, his Zero persona) in code geass. There, it is written as "FABULOUS".
face between breasts: When a character is face first in between the breasts of another character.
face down: When the person's face is on contact with and pointed down at the ground, a pillow, or similar surface.
face filter: An overlay drawn above a character's face, in the style of a selfie taken with a snapchat filter (or any other similar app). Usually takes the form of drawn whiskers or drawn ears.
face grab:
grabbing another person's face.

face in ass:
Pressing one's face in between another persons's ass cheeks.

face in crotch: One character's face is being pressed or nudging against another's crotch.
face in pillow: Burying one's face in a pillow.
face in shadow:
When a character's face is completely covered in shadow, rendering it almost, if not completely hidden.
Can still overlap with eyes in shadow.
face punch: A punch to the face. May or may not be fatal.
face shield: A protective covering for all or part of the face that is commonly made of clear plastic and is worn especially to prevent injury (as from impact, extreme temperature, or a dangerous substance) or to reduce the spread of transmissible disease. It is commonly used by soldiers and riot police.
face to breasts: When a character's face is against the breasts of another character.

face-to-face: When two characters are facing one another within close proximity.
facebook:
Social media site created by mark zuckerberg. Currently the Largest and Most Famous social media site in the world.
If you upload image/pictures that source is based on Facebook, You can input source by open the image tab and open the new tab of the image in another browser tab and copy the link.
facebook logo: The facebook logo is present in the image. Often accompanied by the artist's facebook username.
facebook username: A line in the artwork pointing to a user's Facebook account.
faceless:
Use when the entire front of the head is within the frame, but obscured or not completely drawn.
If the character is meant to literally be without a face (not just for artistic style/due to concealed features; EX: slender man), use hole in face or some combination of no eyes, no nose, or no mouth.
faceless female:
When a female's facial features (mainly the eyes) don't appear, either because they're hidden, covered by hair, in shadow, or not drawn at all.
This tag does not apply when the character's head is completely out of frame. For instance, this tag doesn't apply to pov images that display only the viewer's own body.
faceless male:
When a male's facial features (mainly the eyes) don't appear, either because they're hidden, covered by hair, in shadow, or not drawn at all.
This tag does not apply when the character's head is completely out of frame. For instance, this tag doesn't apply to pov images that display only the viewer's own body.
faceoff: When two opposing characters or groups are facing each other in an antagonistic manner, often signaling a rivalry or the beginning of a fight.
facepaint:
Painted marks or symbols in a person's face. Often used by tribal cultures.
Not to be confused with paint splatter on face which is for paint splatters on a character's face.
See drawing on another's face for the act of facepainting (applying facepaint to someone else).
facepalm:
"Because expressing how dumb that was in words just doesn't work."
A meme-ish action inspired by an "image":[https://imgur.com/gallery/iWKad22] of Jean-Luc Picard holding his hand to his face, with the intended context of calling something or someone wildly stupid.
faceplant:
When a character falls to the ground face first.

- full scorpion
facial:
cum on someone's face.
See simulated facial for facials performed with sexually suggestive fluids.
facial mark:
Markings on the face, simple in design. Either drawn on, pasted on, tattooed, or formed as a unique birthmark.
If the design is elaborate, use facial tattoo instead.
[b]Does not include injuries, such as scars, and does not include moles. [b]
facial tattoo: A tattoo located on the face.
facing ahead: A character facing directly in front of themselves with their eyes closed or obstructed, and not at the viewer. facing ahead is relative to the character’s front, not the viewer perspective. If they are facing viewer, use that instead.
facing another:
Someone is facing someone else with the eyes closed.
If someone is looking at someone else (in other words, with the eyes open), use looking at another.
facing away:
An image where the subject is facing 180 degrees away from the camera such that only the back of their head is seen. This could include, but not limited to, from behind.
This does not include when a character is looking to the side, or when a character who is not the main subject is facing away from the camera.
facing back: Similar to looking back, but the character has their eyes closed or otherwise obstructed.
facing down: There is still no description for this tag. Consider head down: "A character is tilting their head downwards."
facing to the side:
A character facing to their side with closed or covered eyes.
The character should be facing to the "side" relative to their body, that is, turning their head without turning their body. If the entire body is facing to the "side" relative to the camera, use from side instead.
facing up: A character’s face pointing up, usually also looking up.
facing viewer:
A character facing the viewer with their eyes closed or covered. This tag may also apply to characters facing toward the viewer but with their eyes turned in another direction, as in post #2834076.
Don't confuse with looking at viewer, which should be used when eyes are open.
factory:
A building or facility designed for the development, production or construction of certain kind of objects or products.
h1. See also
- industrial (for factory-like environment setting)
- junkyard

fading:
When a character is gradually vanishing into nothingness. Typically rendered as the person being partially transparent or parts of the body disappearing from one end to the other. This tag may require context and be subjective.
- Not to be confused with projected inset, when a character is inset at a lower opacity for dramatic or comedic effect.
- Not to be confused with zoom layer, where an image has a semi-transparent, upscaled version in the background.
fading border: When the borders of a picture fade out gradually, instead of meeting a sharp outline.
failure: When a character being unable to accomplish what they set out to do, or an event/object that does not accomplish its intended purpose.
failure penguin: The failure result of development and modernization with a single ship-girl. Consists of a crying penguin stuffed animal(?), accompanied by miss cloud (a curly hairball with a face and some hair bows), in a cardboard box.
fainted: The end result of fainting, where the person in question loses consciousness but doesn't die.
fainting:
Characters becoming unconscious and collapsing due to (mental) shock, asphyxiation, blood loss, etc.
The medical term is Syncope which strictly refers to the brain not getting enough blood and temporarily shutting down, recovering in a few second when it gets enough blood.
For danbooru however, fainting refers to merely to the act of becoming limp and collapsing.
Also applies to a character that has fainted, though not to be confused with sleeping.
fairy:
Fairies (s. fairy) are legendary creatures. They're usually depicted as small beings, although this is not strictly necessary. 
Human in form, playful in nature, fairies are wielders of magical powers. They are commonly depicted having fair skin and gossamer wings.
fairy tail:
A manga and anime series by mashima hiro.
The story involves natsu dragneel, one of the members of the titular Fairy Tail guild, and his adventure in the Magical world.
fairy wings:
The wings of a fairy. Extremely diverse and can range from insect-like designs to those resembling specific shapes.
Does not include butterfly wings.
fake animal ears:
animal ears that are not real. Commonly found on hairbands and hoods but can also show up on hats.
Not to be confused with kemonomimi mode, in which a character is depicted with actual animal features which they do not normally have.
fake antennae: Pretend antennae (mimicking e.g. a bug's or alien's) that are not actually part of a character, perhaps as part of a costume.  These are often attached to a hairband, sometimes utilizing things like small balls, shapes, or pom pom (clothes)s attached to spring (object)s or metal wire, or via the reuse of old radio antennae or rabbit ears antennae.
fake antlers: antlers that are not real. Commonly found on hairbands.
fake blood:
A substance that appears to be blood, but isn't - in color artworks, commonly ketchup, red bean paste, jam or paint; though monochrome ones might also use other substances, like chocolate.
Not every instance of a red fluid is necessarily faux blood - look for crazed expressions, knives, signs of "injuries", or people lying lifelessly on the floor (with the source of "blood" visible).
fake box art:
Pictures that are edited to look like box art for existing merchandise, but are actually not.
Also, make sure to include the parody tag if it's parodying something along with a tag for what it's parodying.
fake censor: When censorship is not used to cover sexually explicit material, copyrighted material (such as product names), an individual's identity, obscene gestures or scenes of graphic violence or gore.
fake claws: Fake claws are artificial appendages designed to replicate the appearance of real claws. These imitation structures are commonly crafted for ornamental or costume purposes, simulating the aesthetic of authentic claws without possessing any functional attributes.
fake cover:
Pictures that are edited to look like a cover of an official publication, but are actually not.
This includes but is not limited to...
- cover page
- magazine cover
- manga cover
- album cover
- video game cover
- movie poster
- Packaging cover
Also, make sure to include the parody tag if it's parodying something along with a tag for what it's parodying.
fake facial hair:
facial hair that is obviously not real. Females may wear fake beards or mustaches if it’s part of a disguise or costume, like santa claus.
If a female has a beard or other facial that appears to look real, see bearded girl.

fake phone screenshot:
A fake screenshot of a cellphone screen.

fake photograph:

fake screenshot: When the picture is drawn to look like a screenshot from a video game, user interface, a software menu, a TV series and so on.
fake tail: When an object is used to simulate having a tail. These may be glued directly on the skin, sewn onto clothes or attached to sex objects.
fake transparency:
A grey-and-white checkerboard pattern that emulates a transparent background or alpha transparency within the image. The grey-and-white pattern comes from the way that transparency is shown in adobe photoshop and other programs.
In May 2019, it became a Twitter meme for artists to create art using fake transparency. This came from an event in which The Pokemon Company revealed a real life geodude mascot for the prefecture of Iwate in Japan. Since Geodude doesn't have legs, the costume used fake transparency to "hide" the legs of the performer inside the costume.
fake video: A fake screenshot of a video, or of a video hosting website, such as youtube or niconico.
fake wings:

falcon:
Latin: Falco sp.
JP: ハヤブサ hayabusa (falcon, peregrine falcon)
A type of bird of prey with thin, tapered wings, which enable them to fly at high speed and change direction rapidly. This group of about 40 species includes kestrels, hobbies, merlins, gyrfalcons and peregrine falcons. Unlike hawks and eagles, falcons kill prey with their beaks, which have a tooth-like ridge.
A male falcon is called a tiercel (British spelling: tercel); downy chicks are eyas.
The technique of hunting with trained captive birds of prey is known as falconry.

Players must master techniques such as blocking, counter-attacking, and chaining together sequences of attacks known as "combos". Most fighting games allow the player to execute special moves by performing specific button combinations.

- Two: v
- Three: w or middle w
- Four: double v (with two hands)
- Five: open hand (with one hand) or v plus w (with two hands)

first aid kit:
An emergency kit containing basic medical supplies for fast treatment of an injury.
When first aid is being administered, use first aid
first high school uniform: school uniform worn by students of Magic High School in the mahouka koukou no rettousei series.
fish:
Any of various mostly cold-blooded aquatic vertebrates usually having scales and breathing through gills.
For the Nuclear Throne character see fish (nuclear throne).
fish bone:
Very thin bones from a fish that must be removed prior to cooking.
Use fish skeleton instead if the bones are linked so they form the overall skeleton of the fish.
fish boy: monster boys that have fish characteristics. Differs from a merman or mermaid in that while they can be humanoid, they have more blatantly fishy characteristics than a fish tail, such as gills, mutlicolored skin, scales across the body, or different fish physiology like head protrusions.
fish girl:
A fish-like monster girl with human legs, unlike a mermaid. Commonly identified by head fins and other fins, fish-like scales, webbed hands or webbed feet, and/or gills. They may also have a fish tail in addition to their legs.
When in doubt (e.g. the lower body isn't visible), use mermaid instead.
fish hair ornament: A hair ornament or hairpin shaped like a fish.
fish in mouth: When a character has a (whole or visually identifiable piece of) fish in their mouth.
fish print: Any type of clothing that has printed patterns resembling fish.
fish tail:
A character with a fish-like tail growing from the base of their spine.
The character should still have human legs. If the character has a fish tail but no legs, use the tag mermaid or merman instead.
fish tank: A small-sized aquarium for displays of aquatic animals at home or at a restaurant.
fishbowl: A type of round glass bowl that small aquatic pets, such as goldfish, are sometimes kept in.
fishbowl helmet: A helmet that is reminiscent to a fishbowl or bubble.  A common design used for space helmets and diving helmets in science fiction.
fisheye:
A type of camera lens that takes photos in a distinct, distorted appearance, wherein straight lines appear increasingly curved the farther they are from the center of the image.  Use this tag for pictures that simulate this effect.
For the bishoujo senshi sailor moon character, see fish eye (sailor moon).
fishing: As a verb, it is the act of catching fish. As a noun, fishing refers to the recreational sport. Most examples of fishing on Danbooru are of the type performed with a fishing rod and baited hook, but methods of fishing vary widely, from fishing with nets to fishing with solar guns and harpoons (spearfishing) to the use of explosives (dynamite fishing). Fishing may be done from a boat, from a shore or pier, or while underwater.
fishing hook: A small metal hook attached to a fishing line that is used to catch fish.
fishing net:
Any type of net used for fishing, from small handheld nets to very large nets towed behind boats.
Do not confuse with fishnets.
fishing rod: A tool used to catch fish with a line and hook.
fishnet armwear: See fishnet gloves, fishnet sleeves etc.
fishnet bodysuit: A bodysuit or leotard made out of fishnets. If there is nothing beneath the fishnets, then the characters skin will be fully visible.
fishnet legwear:
Deprecated tag. Use one of the below tags instead:
- fishnet socks (also includes kneehighs)
- fishnet thighhighs (also includes over-kneehighs)
- fishnet pantyhose
- fishnet leggings
fishnet leotard:
A leotard fully or partially made out of fishnets.
If the leotard does cover at least the upper legs, do not use this tag. Use fishnet bodysuit instead.
fishnet top: Clothing for the upper body made at least partially of fishnet fabric.
fishnets:
A material with an open, diamond shaped knit. It's most often used as a material for stockings, tights or bodystockings and is usually black. Ironically unsuited for catching fish.
Do not confuse with fishing net.
fist bump: The meeting of fists together at the fingers used as "the ultimate expression of affection and trust." Used in combination with as well as an alternative to (for hygienic reasons) a high five or a handshake.
fist in hand: A pre-fighting gesture, where the fist (palm-side down) is placed into the receiving palm (also palm-side down).  For the more formal fighting gesture, see palm-fist greeting.
fist pump:
The act of raising your fist in the air, usually in celebration of something.
Can be done with one arm bent halfway or fully raised in the air.
fisting: Insertion of the entire hand into a body orifice.
fitting room: Small rooms in clothes shops where shoppers can try on new clothes in privacy. These rooms usually include mirrors and a hook where clothes hangers may be hung. They may have privacy curtains in lieu of doors.
five nights at freddy's: Five Nights at Freddy's, abbreviated as FNAF , is a series of indie survival horror game series made by Scott Cawthon in which the player must protect themselves from hostile animatronics.
five nights at freddy's: security breach: The eighth installment in the five nights at freddy's series, released in 2021.
five of hearts: A playing card with five hearts.
five star stories:
The Five Star Stories (ファイブスター物語, Faibu Sutā Monogatari?) is a space opera and mecha manga series created by nagano mamoru, building on his work on the anime series juusenki l-gaim. 
The first volume of the manga was published in April 10, 1986 and is still ongoing.
fixed: Tag used for scans that had any creases or scan artifacts digitally removed, making the illusion of a cleaner image.
flaaffy:
Pokémon #180 in the National Pokédex, an Electric type Pokémon.
It evolved from mareep and evolves into ampharos.
Japanese Name: Mokoko
Prior Pokémon: mareep
Next Pokémon: ampharos
flaccid:
A limp (non-erect) penis.
Can apply to bulges under clothes as well.
flag:
A flag is a piece of fabric, often flown from a pole or mast. Often decorated with emblems, symbols, or shapes to represent one's country or an event. Soldiers may be carrying a war flag.
flag is only applicable if the fabric in question is horizontally-oriented, if it flows vertically use banner instead. 
If the flag is of a specifically known real country, please add that country as a tag.
flag background:
Any background with colors or design that belongs to certain flags. (e.g. post #1195250). 
Also applies if an actual flag predominantly appears on the background. (e.g. post #1224962)
Not to be used for solid-colored background despite actual flag designs with only single color exists (e.g. former flag of Libya under Gaddafi).
h1. See also
- tag group:backgrounds
flag print: Clothing or an item that is designed with printings resembling a nation's flag.
flagpole: A pole used for flying a flag.
flags of all nations: flags of various nations (real or fictional) hanging from a rope or string. A common prop in sports festival settings.
flail:
The flail is a medieval weapon, made of (one or more) weight(s) attached to a handle with a hinge, rope, or short chain. They originated from farming flails, which were used to thresh grain.
A rule of thumb, if the weapon has a chain over an arm's length (and more so over 1.5 arm's lengths), then the weapon is most likely a ball and chain (weapon) instead.
flailing: The act of waving the arms around dramatically, usually to get attention during a temper tantrum or if the character is in trouble.
flak jacket: A type of body armor designed to protect from from explosive weaponry such as anti-aircraft artillery ("flak" is a German contraction for Fliegerabwehrkanone, "aircraft-defense gun") or grenade fragments. Its prominent usage was by the US military during the vietnam war, but cannot provide protection against higher velocity (rifle) bullets.
flame print: Clothing or an object with the printed motif of flames from a fire.
flame-tipped tail:
A fire at the tip of one's tail.
If the whole tail is made of fire, use fiery tail instead.
flamenco dress: A dress used to dance flamenco.
flamethrower:
A weapon designed to launch fire over a distance, generally using pressurized-gel that either ignites in contact with the air or is otherwise lit as it exits the nozzle. The gel sticks to anything that it touches as it burns. Has a distinctive whoosh sound.
It has been used throughout world war i and world war ii and saw limited use as late as the vietnam war, usually to attack enemies inside fortifications or hiding among the trees.
warhammer 40k makes extensive use of flamethrowers. It is also the primary weapon for the pyro (tf2) in team fortress 2.
flaming eye:
A single eye with fire emitting from it.
Popularized by black rock shooter (character) and sans (undertale).
Also use eye trail when the fire leaves a trail.
flaming eyes:
Fire emitting from the eyes, so as to show passionate, determined or "burning" emotion and spirit. 
May also apply to use of powers.
flaming halo: A halo that is either on fire or made entirely of flames.
flaming hand: When a burst of fire is engulfing a character's hand or fingers. May be the result of a pyrokinetic using their powers, or someone channeling a tremendous amount of energy to create fire on their hand.
flaming sword: A sword that is either made of flame or that is giving off flames.
flaming weapon:
A weapon ablaze with flame, or made entirely out of fire.
roy (fire emblem) and rengoku kyoujurou both use flaming weapons.
flamingo:
Any of several aquatic birds of the family Phoenicopteridae, having very long legs and neck, webbed feet, a bill bent downward at the tip, and pinkish to scarlet plumage.
Flamingos are filter-feeders and famously derive their color from the aqueous bacteria in their diet. Captive flamingos which are given insufficient amounts of carotene may turn pale pink or white.
flandre scarlet: A touhou character (alt. spelling Frandre, Flandoll, Frandoll). The "Diabolic Wave". Extra Stage boss of touhou's embodiment of scarlet devil and Playable Character in sunken fossil world.
flapper shirt: A shirt that is tied at the top, but then splits in the middle and opens up to expose the wearer's abdomen.
flapping: The act of moving one's wings up and down to initiate flight. Can also be done with the arms.
flare:
A type of pyrotechnic that produces a bright light or intense heat without an explosion. Flares are used for distress signalling, illumination, or defensive countermeasures in civilian and military applications.
For the photographic effect, use lens flare.
flareon:
Pokémon #136 in the National Pokédex.
A fiery evolution, its red-furred body sports thick wisps of flame-shaped yellow fur (esp. tail and forehead).
Evolves from eevee.
Japanese name: Booster
Prior Pokémon: jolteon
Next Pokémon: porygon
flash:
As of March 31, 2021, uploading flash files is no longer possible. See forum #183397 for details.
This tag is for games, music videos, and animations created using Adobe Flash.
While Flash enjoyed success from the late 1990s to the late 2000s (especially because of the failure of the Java platform in the web), it eventually declined as JavaScript and other browser-agnostic platforms like HTML5 and WebGL matured.
flashback:
The recalling of past events involuntarily. Could stem from outer or inner stimuli; eg: a loud sound, a familiar smell for the former. Thinking about someone could be the latter. If the recollection is voluntary, use remembering.
Frequently associated with PTSD, and heightened under situations of emotional distress.
flashbang:
A less-lethal grenade used for crowd control by emitting a blinding flash and loud sound to impair vision and hearing. While they are less-lethal than regular grenades, they are still able to cause unintended consequences such as permanent vision or hearing loss to the receiver.
Commonly depicted ones are usually the M84 stun grenade.
flashing: Deliberately moving clothing aside in order to briefly reveal something intimate, often in a teasing manner. Revealed contents can range from panties, a nipple, the whole nude body under a coat, etc.
flashlight:
An artificial, handheld light source that relies on a battery or some other way of storing energy (magic et al).
Not to be confused with a torch, since English speakers outside of America also use that word to mean this tag.
flask: A glass container commonly used in laboratories to hold liquids. The most common shapes of flask are a conical body with a tubular neck (an erlenmeyer flask) and a spherical body with a tubular neck (a round-bottom flask).
flat ass: Barely flat or not so prominent buttocks.
flat cap:
A style of soft hat with a short brim and a flattened crown.

flat chastity cage: A flat variant of a chastity cage where the penis is squished flat, usually with holes.
flat chest:
A female character with a completely flat chest, that is, no breasts whatsoever. For breasts larger than flat yet smaller than normal, use the small breasts tag. 
Flat chests should not be tagged as breasts.
child characters should not be tagged with flat chest.
flat chest grab: When a character with a flat chest has their chest grabbed.
flat chest joke: An image joking about or making fun of a character's lack of breasts.
flat color: When an image is colored in solid blocks of color, without shadows, highlights, or gradients. The image is "flat" in that there are little to no indications of depth.
flat screen tv:
A flat-screen television, or more accurately a flat-panel television, is a television set with a thickness usually under 10 cm (~4 in.).  This is opposed to cathode-ray tube televisions or rear-projection televisions whose designs required rather thick housing.
This tag is specifically for flat-panel tvs, which the term "flat-screen tv" is used interchangeably with today.  It should not be used for rear-projection tvs or flat-screen cathode-ray tube tvs, which were particularly common before LCD and similar technologies become the dominate technology used for televisions.
flat sign: The ♭ musical note used to denote that a particular note should be one semitone lower in pitch. For instance, a semitone lower pitch of the B note is written as B♭, or B flat.
flat top chef hat: Same as a toque blanche, except the top has been made to be flat. It resembles a block hat with a hole on the length and width area.
flats: A shoe generally worn with chinese clothes, casual clothes, etc.
flattop: A flattop is a type of haircut where the hair on the top of the head is cut and styled upright to form a flat profile when viewed from the front or side.
flcl: FLCL (フリクリ, Furi Kuri, pronounced in English as Fooly Cooly) is a science fiction and comedy OVA series written by Yōji Enokido, directed by Kazuya Tsurumaki and produced by the FLCL Production Committee, which included gainax, Production I.G, and Starchild Records.
fleeing: A subset of running where a person is hurrying away from someone or something. Typically indicates that they're escaping from some danger, or are panicking.
fleet: A group or formation of military vehicles.
fleki:
One of the "Canaries" in dungeon meshi, a squad of elven criminals and nobles sent to dungeons to evaluate the danger they post to the world.
Fleki has notches cut out of her ears, which mark her as a convict (this may or may not have anything to do with her drug habits).
flesh: Posts containing undifferentiated or disembodied chunks of human or animal tissue. For muscle that has become visible from having the skin removed, use exposed muscle.
fletchling:
pokemon #661 in the National PokéDex, a dual-type Normal/Flying Pokémon. 
It evolves into fletchinder starting at level 17, which evolves into talonflame starting at level 35.
Fletchling are small, avian Pokémon similar in appearance to robins.
fleur de lapin uniform:
The waitress uniform used by the café "Fleur de Lapin" in the series gochuumon wa usagi desu ka?. kirima syaro, who works for the café, is typically seen wearing it, though other characters may wear it too.
The uniform itself is inspired by maid uniforms and has lop rabbit ears attached to the headdress.
fleur-de-lis: The fleur-de-lis (⚜) is a a stylized lily (in French, fleur means flower (symbol), and lis means lily) or iris that is often used as a decorative design or in heraldry.
flexible: Referring to the ability to perform positions requiring a higher amount of body mobility than the average human has. This can be achieved through stretching or yoga. If the position requires extreme levels of flexibility this act will be referred to as contortion instead.
flexing: When a character is striking a pose or moving in a way that shows off their muscles.
flick: To strike with a light, quick, snapping stroke of the finger.  May be used to cause light pain as a punishment, such as with a forehead flick; to propel objects, such as a paper football; or to perform other various actions, such as removing a lid, lighting a match, etc.
flight attendant: Also known as a cabin crew, stewards/stewardesses, or air hosts/hostesses; a member of an aircrew employed by airlines primarily to ensure the safety and comfort of passengers aboard commercial flights, on select business jet aircraft, and on some military aircraft.
flight deck: The flight deck of an aircraft carrier is where aircraft take off and land, a miniature airfield at sea, so to speak.
flight goggles:
Protective goggles worn by pilots. Notable for having tinted lenses and metal frame (post #3865211 for example).
The AN-6530 goggles is a prominent real life example.

- aviator hat
- flight helmet

flinch:
Sudden jerking motion in response to surprise or shock. Usually portrayed as sharp motion lines popping out of a character's body.
See twitching for similar motion in response to agitation or stimulation.
flintlock: An Old World firearm that used the flintlock mechanism to propel bullets. A mechanism where a hammer holding flint strikes a piece of steel and produces sparks. The sparks fall into a pan of gunpowder and ignites the powder. A small hole from the pan to the barrel allows flame to travel and ignite the powder in the barrel. Replaced the matchlock and wheellock. This mechanism was eventually replaced by the more reliable cap-and-ball percussion system.
flip flappers: A Fall 2016 (Q4) original anime by Studio 3Hz.  Directed by Oshiyama Kiyotaka and character designs by kojima takashi.
flip phone:
A cellphone that features a clamshell design that flips open.
With the advent of smartphones, flip phones have generally fallen out of favor. However, with developments in flexible OLED screens enabling foldable smartphones, some modern smartphones have begun using a flip design.
flip-flops: Flip-flops are a type of light sandal-like shoe, typically worn as a form of casual footwear. They consist of a flat sole held loosely on the foot by a Y-shaped strap known as a toe thong that passes between the first and second toes and around both sides of the foot. (From "Wikipedia":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip-flops])
flipped bangs:
When a character's bangs sweep upwards. 
Note that this tag can be used with flipped hair if both apply.
flipped hair:
When hair is curled outward at the ends.
This is not for character's tossing their hair with their hand. For that, use hair flip.
flippers: A common term for appendages of aquatic mammals, or more widely, any flat appendages suited for movement through water. May also mean the footwear commonly associated with scuba diving, otherwise named swimfin.
flipping food:
When someone is cooking food in a frying pan, on a barbecue or a stovetop and turns the food on the other side to evenly cook it. When a frying pan is used, a skilled cook uses a flick of the wrist to deftly flip the food in midair. When a spatula is used, expect an over-dramatic toss of the food into the air.
Common foods flipped during cooking include meat, sunny side up eggs, pancakes, noodles, rice, and stir fry.
A mistake in flipping food with a frying pan leads to failure.
flirting: The act of making romantic advances towards someone else.
floating:
Moving or hovering in the air, seemingly without the help of an outside propulsion system (i.e wings).
For the act of floating in water, use afloat.
floating book: The use of levitation magic on a book.
floating breasts: Breasts that are floating in water.
floating cape: A cape, cloak or capelet fluttering behind the wearer, either through wind or movement.
floating card: Any sort of card that appears to be falling, flying, or floating in midair, for any reason.
floating castle:
Either a castle/castle like structure on a floating island or a single man made structure floating in the air on its own. 
If there are several floating structures consider using floating city instead.
floating city:
Either a city built on one or more floating islands or a collection of buildings floating in the air.
See also: floating castle.
floating clothes: Clothing that is blowing in the wind, floating in midair, or otherwise not being held down by gravity.
floating crown: A crown that is hovering just over the wearer's head. This is different from unworn crown because it's implied the character is still wearing it in this case.
floating earring: earrings that appear to be floating, not being directly connected to an ear.
floating hair:
Hair that is blowing in the wind, floating in midair, or otherwise not being held down by gravity.
Generally does not apply to tails or hair that is messy or styled to appear gravity-defying.
Not to be confused with hair flowing over, which is hair draped over a surface, or hair spread out, which is hair spread over a surface, or  detached hair, which is hair magically disconnected from the head.
floating head: When the picture shows a character's head that seems to be floating in the air. Is a common feature on movie posters.
floating headgear: A headgear that is not directly conncted to the head of the character, but levitates around or over them.
floating island:
A piece of natural land floating in the sky.
Se also: floating castle and floating city
floating object: An object such as a book or weapon floating in air without visible, physical support.
floating scarf: A scarf floating or flutter in the air, usually due to wind.
floating sword: A sword floating on its own with no apparent propulsion system or force applied, usually next to a character.
floating weapon: A weapon floating on its own with no apparent propulsion system or force applied, usually next to a character.
flock: Multiple birds (near always the same species) behaving as a group. Distinct from too many birds in that the birds must be a grouping in some way (Eg, being clustered together or flying together), for instance a pet store featuring countless cages with a few birds each or a series of taxidermy animals would be not count as flock but could be toomanybirds.
floette:
pokemon #670 in the National PokéDex, a Fairy-type Pokémon. 
It evolves from flabebe starting at level 19 and evolves into florges when exposed to a Shiny Stone. 
Floette has a white body and a green tail, shaped like a spade, and green eyebrows.
flonne: Flonne is an angel from the disgaea series. She appears both in the first game and the second, often accompanied by laharl and etna (disgaea). She has waist length blonde hair, blue eyes, small angelic wings (or small demonic wings in some depictions, due to a certain ending in the first game) and a…
flood: An overflow of water (or rarely other fluids) that submerges land that is usually dry, such as populated areas.
floor: A floor is the bottom surface of a room or vehicle. The tag is used primarily for a room.
floor lamp: Contrary to a desk lamp, a floor lamp is a lamp that stands on the floor. It is often taller than the former.
floorplan:
The inside of a room or building as seen from the outside from a cutaway, generally with furnishings and people.
Don't use this if there isn't at least the ceiling or a wall missing or if the room extends past the edges of the image. For top-down plans and cross-sections that look like architectural drawings, generally with no people, use layout plan instead.
floppy disk: A computer storage device consisting of a magnetic storage medium sealed in a plastic carrier. The disk is read by a computer's floppy disk drive. This storage medium's popularity is rapidly declining due to its limited storage space compared to CDs or jump drives.
floppy ears: Long animal ears that hang limp against the head, unable to perk up on their own. The ears must be completely limp, or almost completely limp, unless they are being lifted by another source, like the wind or someone's hand.
florakinesis: Florakinesis is the ability to create, control and manipulate all types of plants and vegetation.
floral arch:
Also known as "wedding arch".
An arch made of plant and/or flower.
floral background: Catch-all tag for posts with flowers in the background. The flowers can be a simple pattern or real.
floral border:
Image border that has floral pattern or ornate border with floral decoration.

floral dress: When the dress is designd to look like a flower. Don't confuse it with dress flower, which is used when the dress is decorated with at least a flower, or floral print which is used when the dress fabric has some flowery mottif or pattern.
floral print: When there are flowers printed on any article of clothing. They can be abstract or realistic.
floral print kimono: A print kimono with a floral print.
flour: Often used in baking, it is made by grinding grains or seeds into a fine powder. Originally spelled "flower", referring to flour being the best or finest ("flower") part of the ground grain.
flower:
The reproductive structure of a tree or other plant.
A structure having showy or colorful parts; a blossom.
flower basket: A basket used to hold flowers.
flower bed: A small garden of either one or various types of flowers.
flower bracelet: A bracelet with a flower on it.
flower braid: hair flower located on character's braid.
flower choker: A choker with a flower on it.
flower eyepatch:
An eyepatch with a flower on it.
This tag is for actual eyepatches only, for example, if you can see the fabric or strings attached to the flower. For a generic flower covering one eye situation, use flower over eye.
flower hairband: A hairband decorated with a flower.
flower in eye:
When a character has a flower design located in the iris of their eyes. This isn't to be confused for flower-shaped pupils.
hanami kotoha / cure felice is well known for this trait.
flower in mouth: When a character is holding a flower with their mouth.
flower knight girl:
A dmm game which you lead of an army of female personifications of flowers. There is a safe version and an 18+ version which includes sexual scenes.
Please see the list of flower knight girl characters for the complete list of tagged characters.
flower knot: A rope or taut string is looped several times and tied in the center so the loops resemble flower petals. May be a thin ribbon tied in this fashion.
flower necklace: A necklace made from flowers or having flowers in its design.
flower on head:
Use this tag when a flower (or a bunch of flowers) grows on top of a character's head, usually with a stem and a set of leaves. The Pikmins from the eponymous series are examples of this tag.
In anime and manga, a flower growing from a character’s head is sometimes an allusion to the Japanese term "脳内お花畑 (nōnai o-hanabatake)":[https://www.japandict.com/%E8%84%B3%E5%86%85%E3%81%8A%E8%8A%B1%E7%95%91] - literally "garden in the brain" - symbolizing that a character is being "carefree, happy-go-lucky, silly, or stupid":[https://www.japanesewithanime.com/2021/06/flower-on-head.html].
flower on liquid: When a flower is resting on the surface of a liquid, most often water.

flower over eye:
When one of the character's eyes is covered by a flower.
This tag is for flowers that appear to stay in place on its own. Do not use this tag when the flower is clearly attached to a string or fabric or otherwise supported, use flower eyepatch instead.
flower over mouth: A flower over a character's mouth.
flower pot: A flower pot is a container in which flowers and other plants are cultivated and displayed.

flower tattoo: A tattoo shaped like any kind of flower, whether it'd be realistic or abstract in design.
flower trim: An article of clothing that has a trim made of flower or flower-shaped decorations around at least one of its edges.
flower-shaped pupils: Use when a character's pupils are shaped like a flower. Not to be confused with flower in eye, where the flower pattern covers the iris of the eye.
floyd leech: Floyd Leech is a second-year student in twisted wonderland's Octavinelle. He's Jade's twin but their attitude and speech are totally different. He's kind of unpredictable so it's difficult to know what he's thinking.
fluffy: A trait of being soft, light and airy. Invokes a feeling of wanting to cuddle it (e.g. animals with thick fur).
fluorescent lamp: A type of electric lamp which produces light by the fluorescence of mercury vapors. Fluorescent lamps generally take the form of long glass tubes that produce a white or bluish-white light. They are widely used in non-residential applications such as classrooms, offices, and shops.
flustered: A state of agitation that comes from being caught off guard. Often occurs as a result of sudden, unexpected romantic or sexual situations.
flute: A cylindrical wind instrument with one embrochure hole and six to eleven finger holes or keys. It is usually made of wood or metal.
fluttershy:
A yellow and pink pegasus and one of the six primary characters in my little pony: friendship is magic. 
She lives by herself but has many animals in her care. As her name suggests, she is very timid, easily frightened, and she dreads social pressure and teasing.
fly: Insects of the order Diptera, which use only a single pair of wings to fly, the hindwings having evolved into sensory organs.
fly agaric: A large red-capped mushroom with white spots, also known by its scientific name Amanita muscaria. Its distinctive features have made it the iconic toadstool in popular culture, notably as the inspiration for power-ups in the Mario series. It is a known hallucinogen but can be made edible by boiling.
flyer: A piece of paper with an information about certain products, services, or event. It was intended as a cheap form of advertisements and typically handed to strangers to promote the subject.
flygon:

flying: The act of being in or moving through the air with the help of a propulsion system (usually wings, a magic broom or a mechanical device) or being hurled to the air for some distance by either a person or hit by something.
flying boat: A type of seaplane that utilizes a specially-designed hull to take off from and land on water. Distinct from a floatplane, which is usually much smaller and relies on external pontoons to achieve the same purpose.
flying button:

flying car: A car-sized vehicle that flies or hovers instead of rolling on wheels. This tag is for car-like hover vehicles specifically, not posts of regular cars flying.

fn fal: The FAL (Fusil Automatique Léger, "Light Automatic Rifle") is a Belgian-designed 7.62×51mm NATO battle rifle. It was developed between 1947-1953 by "Dieudonné Saive":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dieudonné_Saive] at fn herstal. Known as "the right arm of the Free World", it was the second most widely used military rifle in the world (after the AK) during the cold war, being used by 77 different nations. was nearly adopted by the United States Army as well, but was rejected in favor of the M14.
fn five-seven: The FN Five-seveN is a hammerless, polymer-framed, semi-automatic handgun developed and manufactured by fn herstal in Belgium. It is chambered for the high-velocity 5.7×28mm cartridge which is also used by the earlier p90. The gun has ambidextrous controls and a short Picatinny rail under the slide to accommodate accessories.
fn fnc: The FNC (Fabrique Nationale Carabine) is a Belgian 5.56×45mm NATO assault rifle, developed in 1976 by fn herstal. It is derived from the unsuccessful CAL which was a scaled-down version of the FAL. The weapon features a side-folding stock and a tubular reciprocating charging handle.
fn scar: The FN SCAR (Special Operations Forces Combat Assault Rifle) is a family of gas-operated short-stroke gas piston rifles developed by fn herstal in 2004. There are two major variants, SCAR-L (light) assault rifle and the SCAR-H (heavy) battle rifle. The weapon is quite recognizable by its ugg boot-shaped adjustable folding stock.
foam: A cluster of minute bubbles shown coming from someone's mouth, poured beverages with head such as beer or root beer, et cetera. For bubbles produced while using soap products during bathing, see soap bubbles.
foaming at the mouth:

folding chair:

folding screen:
Furniture composed of several joined panels connected by hinges originated in China.

folding stock:
A firearm buttstock that can be folded while not in use, reducing the weapon's overall length for easier storage or transport. It usually utilizes a hinged attachment to the receiver.
It is a prominent feature of modern small arms design. Most folding stocks fold to the side, while few models fold to the top (e.g. spas-12) or bottom (e.g. mp40).
foliage: Collective vegetation, leafage, or greenery, as from bushes or trees, particularly en masse, in a natural rather than cultivated setting, and especially when grown together or indistinct enough that individual bushes, trees, or plants aren't particularly tag-worthy as individuals.

frutiger aero:
Frutiger Aero is a visual aesthetic primarily utilized in the 2000s to early 2010s for commerical purposes, focusing on the mix of nature with technology, as well as an overall "glossy" look.
The name, coined by the Consumer Aesthetics Research Institute, originates from the "Aero" style from windows 7, and the Frutiger font.
Color palettes tend to consist of whites, blues and greens, and the occasional orange. Glossy textures are very common, as are semi-transparent elements. lens flares and bokeh are also frequently seen, along with "swirly" freeform shapes.
frutiger metro:
A visual aesthetic popular in the mid-late 2000s to early 2010s, and a derivative of frutiger aero, mixing flat minimalist design styles with overall maximalist imagery.
Common visual elements include gradients, "bloom" or "flourish" shapes, glossy textures, bokeh, abstract backgrounds, splatter effects, lineless vector drawings, shapes such as star (symbol)s and circles, and silhouettes. Bright color palettes consisting mainly of lime green, electric blue, hot pink and neon orange are a staple.

gibson brands inc:
Gibson Brands Inc, formerly Gibson Guitar Corporation, is a famed maker of electric guitars.  In addition to guitars they also produce other musical instruments and professional audio equipment.
The Epiphone company and brand is owned by Gibson.
gibson flying v: Solid body electric guitar created and manufactured by American instrument maker Gibson since 1958. Built with a futuristic design in mind alongside its closest sibling the Explorer, it was initially deemed a failure with less than 100 units being built and sold between 1958 and 1959. The Flying V eventually catched the interest of certain guitarists and slowly gained success until its boom in popularity since the 80's, being popularily used in Metal subgenres for its aggressive looks.
gibson les paul: Solid body electric guitar manufactured by Gibson since 1952, designed with input by famed jazz guitarist Les Paul whose name ended up as the name of the guitar itself, work and prototypes commenced in 1950, with 1951 prototypes being strikingly similar to the final product until its introduction in 1952. The Les Paul eventually caught big success in a seemingly endless array of genres, pinning it as one of the most well known and popular guitars along with its contemporaries, the fender telecaster and fender stratocaster.
gibson sg: Solid body electric guitar made and manufactured by American instrument maker Gibson first introduced in 1961, originally as a new, lighter double-cutaway version of the gibson les paul when its sales had been declining due to the fender stratocaster's rapid success. However, Lester Polsfuss (Les Paul) hated the new design and demanded that his name not be associated with the guitar. The name change would eventually occur in 1963, being renamed SG which literally stands for Solid Guitar.
gif artifacts:
The animated gif image format is made to display a maximum of 256 colors in one image.  When an image containing more than 256 colors is saved as a GIF, the color limitation of the GIF format creates artifacts (defects) such as dithering (e.g. post #720057) or color banding (e.g. the background of post #76332).
Note that despite artifacting in high-color images, GIFs have legitimate uses, such as for pixel art, low-color oekaki images, and animated images.

glint:
The sparkle of a polished or metal object. This should come from a physical object, such as jewelry, a sword, or teeth.
sparkle, glint, and diffraction spikes all refer to similar patterns of bright lines radiating from a point. They are not clearly differentiated, and usage tends to be context-sensitive. In general:
- sparkle is considered the base case. Usually four lines at right angles radiating from a point. Associated with eyes, liquid or particulate matter (e.g. raindrops, snow, sand), or nothing (appearing mid-air). Can appear in large numbers.

greyscale:
A completely colorless, black-and-white image. The image is composed exclusively of shades of black, white, and grey. It is very common for comics and doujinshi to be in greyscale.
The image may have small highlights of color (known as spot colors), but the image as a whole should be predominately greyscale.
Don't use color tags like black eyes or black hair when tagging greyscale images. The exception is color background tags, so tagging white background, grey background, or black background is fine.
greyscale with colored background:
An artwork where the subject is in greyscale but the background is colored, it's usually also a simple background.
Do not tag these as greyscale, partially colored or spot color.
However if there're parts of the image other than the background is colored, such as the subject's eyes, spot color can be used. If the subject has enough coloring on itself that you'd tag it partially colored, simply use that tag instead and do not tag it as greyscale with colored background.
grid background:
A typically single-color background formed into a square grid by a series of thin lines.
The lines must be perpendicular or parallel with respect to each other, but not necessarily to the sides of the image; a square grid that has been rotated is still a square grid.
Not to be confused with checkered background, where the squares contain two alternating colors, or border, a line that runs along three to four edges of the image.

Guinea pigs are highly vocal rodents and are noted for making a characteristic "wheek" sound when excited or hungry. This sound is rendered as "pui" in Japanese onomatopoeia. 
The scientific name of the species is Cavia porcellus. It is sometimes also called "cavy" by breeders and owners.

gyaru:
Gyaru (ギャル), also known as gal, is a Japanese fashion style that peaked in the 2000s. Although it has generally declined in real life, it still has many followers and remains popular in various Japanese media, particularily the manga & anime industry.
It has many diverse substyles, with some commonalities. Gyaru style typically involves styled and coloured hair, trendy and often sexy gyaru-style clothing (especially from the shops in the mall Shibuya 109), and heavy makeup, with a focus on false eyelashes, enlarging the eyes, contouring, and circle lenses.
gyaru v:
An upside-down v gesture.
The original term is called "Gyaru-peace", which is a combination of the Japanese pronunciation of "Gal," an English slang for women and girls, and the English word "Peace," which means finger gesture v.
Originating from Japan's gyaru culture, it is a hand gesture that first extends the arm forward and turns the palm up and down after making a V-shape by hand.
gyaruo:
The male counterpart to gyaru. While the term originated from the styles reported on by fashion magazine Men's Egg, it has since gone on to become a moniker for the youth subculture that wore it.
Like their female counterparts, typical gyaruo attire comes in different flavors. The most common depictions have tans or dark skin, blonde hair, or some sort of loose fashion. However, not everyone who is tan or blond may be part of the gyaruo subculture.
Also spelled as "gyaru-oh" or "gal-o":[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1EKTw50Uf8M] alternately.

gyuudon: A Japanese dish consisting of a bowl of rice topped with beef and onion simmered in a mildly sweet sauce flavored with dashi (fish and seaweed stock), soy sauce and mirin (sweet rice wine). It also often includes shirataki noodles, and is sometimes topped with a raw egg. A very popular food in Japan, it is commonly served with beni shōga (pickled ginger), shichimi (ground chili pepper), and a side dish of miso soup. Gyū means "cow" or "beef", and don is short for donburi, the Japanese word for "bowl".
h&k g11: A prototype assault rifle developed by heckler & koch during the late 1970's and 1980's which was notable for its mostly polymer construction, boxy bullpup design, and caseless ammunition held in a box magazine under the integral scope.
h&k g3: The G3 is a West German 7.62×51mm NATO battle rifle developed by heckler & koch in the 1950s, based on the earlier Spanish cetme model 58. It became the standard bundeswehr service rifle from 1959 until early 1990s. Utilizing roller-delayed blowback mechanism, and having major variants available with fixed buttstock or retractable metal one, its design also became the basis of other H&K weapons such as the MP5 submachine gun.
h&k g36:
The G36 is a 5.56×45mm NATO assault rifle, designed in early 1990s and manufactured by heckler & koch in Germany. It was intended to supplant the failed G11 project and the G41 which was too heavy, the G36 features a conventional configuration with short-stroke piston operation. Notable variants include the shorter G36K, the shortest G36C, and the MG36 light machine gun.
The weapon is characterized by a large carrying handle with an integrated optical sight and skeletonized folding stock. It lacks a front sight post as well.
h&k hk416: An AR-15-style assault rifle made by heckler & koch. Looks a lot like the m4 carbine but has a railed forearm with folding front sight and internal changes. It can be outfitted  with a variety of barrels, ranging from 228-505mm (9-19.9 inches) in length.
h&k mp5:
The MP5 (Maschinenpistole 5) is a submachine gun of German origin, developed in the 1960s and manufactured by heckler & koch. Its design is based on scaled-down G3 rifle. The models are available in fixed buttstock version and the retractable one.
This tag should be used for the original full-sized MP5 models without integrated suppressors.
h&k mp5k:
Shortened (Kurz) version of the MP5A2 submachine gun, introduced in 1976. It has a shorter barrel and a vertical foregrip. The MP5K PDW variant has a triangular side-folding stock.

h&k ump:

A slab-sided weapon, lighter but bulkier in comparison to the h&k mp5 it was designed to supplant, the UMP is equipped with Picatinny accessory rails, a skeletonized folding buttstock, and is available in three calibers: 9mm (H&K UMP9, distinguishable by its curved box magazine), .40 S&W (H&K UMP40), and .45 ACP (H&K UMP45). hagoromo:

Tales associated with the hagoromo include the Japanese legend of tennin (spirtual beings who wear hagoromo) and some folkloric stories set in China, for example, orihime (tanabata) and hikoboshi.
Buddhist deities' hagoromo-like shawls are called "天衣" (Chinese: tian yi, Japanese: tenne, ten'e, or ten'i).

hair around ear: Hairstyle that braiding or wrap around the ear or the ear is poking through the tied lock of hair.
hair beads:
beads that are strung together and worn as a hair ornament. The beads can either just be decoration, or a hairpiece that keeps hair into a ponytail, twintails or similar.
For hair ornaments resembling pairs of larger beads, see hair bobbles.
hair behind ear: When a character's ear is used to keep some of their hair off of their face.
hair bell: A bell used as an accessory for hair.
hair between breasts: A lock of hair falls between a character's breasts.
hair between eyes: A hair bunch from long bangs that falls over the middle of the forehead, long enough to reach at least between the eyes of the person.
hair between horns: When a character with horns towards the from of the head has their bangs cross between them, most often seen in characters with skin-covered horns, since they tend to be located on the forehead, might also include center-flap bangs.
hair bobbles:
A hair ornament consisting of an elastic band with one or more bobbles, frequently two large balls, used to tie the hair. It works by wrapping the band around a bundle of hair and securing it by stretching the band over and around the bobble.
Stereotypically associated with young or teenage girls.
Not to be confused with hair beads. Hair beads usually consist of many smaller beads and aren't always used to tie the hair. Hair bobbles usually consist of two larger beads normally used to tie the hair.
hair bow: A bow tied into the hair in some way. It will often be used by girls with long hair to tie back a ponytail or twintails. It will also be used to keep loose hair back without a tail or as simple decoration.
hair brush: A stick brush with rigid or soft bristles used in hair care for smoothing, styling, and detangling human hair, or for grooming an animal's fur.
hair bun: Any hairstyle in which the hair is wrapped into a round bun.
hair censor: long hair positioned so that it covers the nipples or the crotch, often as a form of convenient censoring.
hair color connection:
Pictures in which grouping at least 3 characters with the same hair color together is a major focus of the image. It's also acceptable if a character is cosplaying as another character with an extremely similar hue of hair color, or a similar form of multicolored hair.
If the characters have the same style of hair (not necessarily the same color), see hairstyle connection.
hair down:
A character who would normally have an up hairdo now has it down. For characters originally with short hair having their hair grown longer "down", use alternate hair length or official alternate hair length instead.
###### Examples
- hiiragi kagami is known for her twintails, but is seen in post #642362 relaxing with her hair down.
- tainaka ritsu who is seen in many posts without her trademark hairband, such as post #1936138.
hair dryer: A handheld electric appliance used for drying and styling hair.
hair ears: Hairstyles mimicking animal ears, can be used alongside impossible hair if it looks unrealistic enough. Could be the result of intense hair intakes, cone hair buns, or hair flaps.
hair extensions: Pieces of (often synthetic) hair that are clipped or sewn in to add fullness or length to one's existing hair.
hair flaps:
Tufts of hair coming from the side of the head. A frequent target for expressivity.
Examples of characters with hair flaps include: remodeled Yuudachi, remodeled Shigure, hotarumaru, miya utsutsu, and saya (saya no uta).
hair flip:
The act of using one's hand to flip a strand of hair away. Usually associated with elegant characters.
This is not the tag for the winged type of hairstyle where the hair curls at the tips. For that, use flipped hair.
Not to be confused with whipping hair.
hair flower: One or more flowers, living or artificial, being worn as a hair ornament. If the flowers encircle the character's entire head, it's a head wreath instead.
hair flowing over:
Long, flowing hair that is draped over an object, item, or irregular surface in such a way that demonstrates proper observation of hair physics and/or gravity. 
Not to be confused with floating hair, which is hair blowing in the wind, or hair spread out, which is hair spread over a surface.
hair focus: An image whose main point of focus is hair, favoring showing of hair or hairstyles over the subject (the person with the hair).
hair half undone: When one of a pair of twintails or twin braids is undone, but the other is not. Can be use alongside hairdressing.
hair horns: fake horns that are made with a character's hair. Almost like cone hair bun, except the hair is tied a lot tighter so that they resemble horns. Can also be produced when a character's hair naturally sticks up to form a spike.
hair in own mouth:
When a character is holding a lock or single strand of their own hair in their own mouth.
See eating hair for when someone is chewing on someone else's hair. See stray pubic hair for when someone has pubic hair in their mouth.
hair intakes: A hair style that creates twin forward-facing scoops. Might become hair ears when intensified.
hair lift:
When someone lifts their hair using their hands, arms, or other objects.
Not to be confused with floating hair: Hair that is blowing in the wind or floating in midair.
hair on horn: Hair is resting over a character's horns or antlers.
hair ornament:
An accessory worn in the hair for decoration or ornamentation purposes.
Accessories used to tie or hold the hair together, such as bows or ribbons, are not considered to be hair ornaments. Hair ornaments are strictly decorative.
hair ornament request: A request to tag specifically what type of hair ornament a character is wearing. When the hair ornament is tagged, please remove hair ornament request.
hair over breasts: A female's hair draping over her breasts, whether it results in censorship or not. When it does result in censorship, be sure to add hair censor.
hair over crotch: A person's hair draping over their crotch, whether it results in censorship or not. When it does result in censorship, be sure to add hair censor.
hair over eyes: long bangs that hang over both eyes. For the asymmetric version of this where only one eye is covered, use hair over one eye.
hair over face:
Hair that drapes down over a character's face, significantly obscuring at least a third of their face. If the hair only covers the eyes, it's hair over eyes instead.
Not to be confused with hair between eyes.

A light fixture that hangs from the ceiling by a chain, cord, or metal rod. They are a common light source over kitchen counters and restaurant tables.
This tag is distinct from chandelier in that chandeliers are large fixtures that branch out into multiple lamps, whereas hanging lights are of simple design and only have one or two lamps each. Hanging lights are often arranged in multiples to evenly illuminate an area.

hanging scroll:
A hanging scroll, called by the generic terms 立軸 (lìzhóu) in China and 掛軸/掛け軸 (kakejiku) in Japan, is an illustration or piece of calligraphy affixed to a scroll of cloth or paper.
When hanging scrolls first took their modern form during the Northern Song Dynasty of China, they were strongly characterized as portable murals to be used in religious ceremonies, but later came to be appreciated as art objects.
In the Japanese Way of Tea, these scrolls are called 掛物 (kakemono), and are emphasized as an indispensable piece of equipment for the tea ceremony.
