- post #4407224
- post #6622903
head on table: Someone is resting their head atop a table.
head only:
Character's head on its own, without a body. A neck and shoulders count as a body, if they're visible use cropped shoulders instead.
Can be used when multiple heads or chibi (inset) are present.
Do not use this tag for images where a (headless) body is present or as the  aftermath of decapitation, whether the body actually belongs to the head or not. In such cases, use severed head instead. 
h1. See also
- cropped shoulders
- disembodied head
- portrait
- tag group:image composition
head out of frame:
When the main subject's head is fully or partially cropped out of frame, but their torso is still in the frame. The head may be only halfway out of frame. The nose and mouth may be visible, but not the eyes.
The main emphasis should be on a single character's torso. Do not use this tag for faceless or mostly out of frame background characters, or for close-ups or a character's ass or lower body. This tag is for when the main subject's head is cropped out of the frame, not most or all of their body.
head rest: Resting one's head or chin on something, such as on the hands, another person, or an object.
head steam:
Steam billowing out of a character's head, as if their embarrassment, anger or other emotion has reached a boiling point.
Contrast steaming body, which is usually sexual or from being literally hot.
head tilt:
When a character tilts their head to one side, which is commonly done as either an inquisitive gesture, or a cute gesture, though it can be done for any reason.
Use common sense when applying this tag: the head tilt has to be noticeable, otherwise every single picture on site could be tagged with it.
Use head back if tilted upwards.
head under another's clothes: When someone's head is under another's clothes, usually because they are a pervert.
head under skirt: When someone has their head under another person's skirt. Usually seen with implied cunnilingus or implied fellatio.
head wings: wings that are attached to the head. A common feature on the demon girl, but other creatures may have them, such as bird girls. If a character's hair is actually wing-shaped, use hair wings. If the wings are attached to a character's headgear rather than being part of the character's body, use winged helmet or winged hat.
head wreath: A circular band of flowers, foliage, or any ornamental work, for adorning the head.
head-mounted display:
A display device which completely covers the eyes and is not transparent, often divided by a thin horizontal strip in the middle. It doesn't need to be used for virtual reality, but odds are that the visor displays some sort of visual or tactical image to the user. Otherwise they'd just wear glasses.
Often seen used by mecha or scifi fightercraft pilots or for use with training simulators, or for characters wearing VR visors.
headband:
A strap worn across the forehead, such as a sweatband, a strip of cloth worn during martial arts or athletic events, or a piece of ninja armor (however apocryphal). While a headband may be used to keep hair out of the eyes, it is usually worn under at least part of the hair. Headbands often end with a long tail trailing behind the head where they are tied. 
For a band worn over the top of the head, that is principally used to maintain a hair style, see hairband.
headbutt: When a character hits someone with their head.
headdress:
"An ornamental covering or band for the head, especially one worn on ceremonial occasions."
(— Oxford Languages dictionary.)
Use this tag for ornamental headdresses, such as the native american headdress. Most headgear that can be described as "'headband' but with lots of rigid(ish) decorations attached" or "hat/bonnet but truncated to only the middle 'band' part" are generally headdresses.
This tag can also be used as a fallback tag for ornamental headgear in general, but try to avoid using this tag for hats, helmets, hair ornaments, fake animal ears and simple ribbons.
headgear: Specialized head accessories that don't fall into the categories of clothing (hats, hoods) or hair ornaments (hairbands, hairclips). Often but not exclusively floating instead of being directly attached to its wearer.
headlamp:
A type of small flashlight (or other similar illuminating device) worn on the head to provide light while leaving the hands free. 
Often attached to a headband or hard hat (such as a mining helmet), but may also be affixed directly to the head.
headless: When a character or object appears without a head. Not to be confused with the head out of frame tag.
headlock:
A wrestling hold in which the opponent's head is locked between the crook of the elbow and the side of the body.
See scissorhold for when a person's head is locked between another person's thighs.
headphones:
A pair of speakers worn on the ears so only the wearer can hear the sounds emitted.
For tagging purposes, this tag covers devices where the two speakers are held in place by a strap over or behind the head and usually cover the entire ear. 
For devices not held in place by such a strap, see earphones or earbuds.
headphones around neck: Wearing a set of headphones around the neck like a collar, rather than on the head as they're supposed to be worn.
headphones removed: For when headphones are in the image but not being worn.
headpiece:
A decorative type of headwear that is fitted around one's head (usually being fitted near/on the forehead) and doesn't fit the traditional definition of a crown, tiara, hairband, et cetera. A headpiece can be worn with a hat though is usually shown being worn on its own. Headpieces are usually depicted as jewelry, though it can be made out of nearly anything such as cloth, machinery, and so forth.
Jeanne d'Arc from Fate and Yomi from Puzzle & Dragons are good examples of characters that wear a headpiece.
heads together: Multiple characters putting their heads together.
heads-up display: A user interface typical of video games and other interactive media. Commonly displays health bars and minimaps.
headset:
A set of headphones with an attached microphone. The headphones are usually small and sometimes cover only one ear, while the microphone is usually a small flexible tube that sits in front of the mouth.
Headsets are often used by customer service employees, by idols performing onstage, and by military operators for communications.
headshop:
A headshop is a type of third-party edit in which a character's head is replaced by the head of another character. Uploading headshops is against the upload rules and should not be done.
Not to be confused with head swap, in which the artist intentionally draw character(s) with their head swapped.
headshot:
"Boom, headshot, yeah!" - FPS Doug, Pure Pwnage
When a character's head is hit with bullets, arrow (projectile)s or other projectile weapons. Usually fatal or severely wounding unless the weapon is non-lethal, the head is protected or the victim can somehow regenerate health.
Do not confuse with an alternate term for photos focusing on the face (portrait or upper body).
headwear request:
A request to identify specific type of hat, helmet or such.
h1. See also
- tag group:attire
- tag group:headwear
headwear switch:
When one character wears the hat/headwear typically associated with another character.
If the character is wearing another's hat and clothing, then consider the cosplay tag instead.
headwear with attached mittens: hat or hood with attached mittens or gloves.
headwear writing:
Any form of headwear that has writing or text on it.
h1. See also
- clothes writing
- tag group:headwear
healin' good precure: The seventeenth installment of the precure series, released in 2020. It primarily focuses on animals. It is also the very first Precure title fully released in the reiwa era, as star twinkle precure was released in late heisei.
healing: When a character is using curative magic to repair a wound or injury. Popularly associated with the white mage (final fantasy) from the final fantasy series, the priest class seen in dragon quest 3 and ragnarok online, the Healer class from the disgaea series, or similar cleric-like classes in character creation-type video games. There are also specific characters who specialize in healing magic.
healing animal:
Small mascot-type animals seen in healin' good precure. They become part of a Cure's healing wand and assist their partner in their henshin and battle (except for cure earth, who uses the Earth Windy Harp). There are four Healing Animals, one for each Cure.
- Rabirin (pink rabbit, paired with cure grace)
- Pegitan (blue penguin, paired with cure fontaine)
- Nyatoran (yellow tiger, paired with cure sparkle)
- Latte (brown dog, paired with cure earth)
healslime: In the dragon quest series, a slime (substance) monster with tentacles. Known in the English version of the game as a "Heal Slime" (or, in NES-era translations, "Healer").
health bar:
A bar that represents the current health of a character in video games. Also refers to other various bars such as the "super" bar.
Most commonly seen in fighting and adventure games.
heanna sumire:
An idol from love live! superstar!! She has blonde hair, blunt bangs, and a hairband with a small bow. She also has green eyes and wears white thighhighs with her school uniform.
Voiced by payton naomi.
heart:
The ♥ symbol. Used to signify romance or enjoyment, and is one of the four suits in playing cards. It is a common representation for love.
For the body part, see heart (organ).
heart ahoge: An instance of "expressive hair" where a character's ahoge (lock of hair that sticks up) bends to form a heart, often to indicate that the owner is happy or in love. Distinct from heart antenna hair, which is made from multiple ahoge.
heart antenna hair: When two of a character's antenna hair form together to resemble a heart shape.
heart apron: An apron that is either shaped like a heart or incorporates a heart shape into the design. Don't use this tag for regular aprons with a heart print.
heart arms: Forming a heart shape with the arms.
heart arms duo: Two characters performing a heart arms pose together.
heart arrow: An arrow (projectile) with the tip or feathers shaped like a heart. Often held by cupid.
heart background: One or more hearts are in the background.
heart balloon: A balloon that is shaped like a heart.
heart belt: A belt that has a heart-shaped buckle or gem clasp.
heart button:
One or multiple buttons in the shape of a heart (♥).
Most commonly associated with komeiji satori.
heart censor: A heart positioned in a way to make the image censored.
heart choker: A choker that has at least one heart on it.
heart collar: A collar with a heart-shaped ornament in front, often a heart-shaped lock.
heart cutout: A clothing cutout (often a cleavage cutout) in the shape of a heart.
heart earrings: earrings that are shaped like hearts or have hearts attached to them.
heart facial mark: A facial tattoo or facial mark shaped like a heart.
heart hair:
Hair in the shape of a heart.
This tag refers to hearts made with the main portion of the hair. Don't use this tag for heart ahoge, heart antenna hair, heart cowlick and heart nape hair.
heart hair bun: Any number of hair buns shaped to resemble a heart.
heart hair ornament: A hair ornament or hairpin shaped like a heart.
heart halo: A halo in the shape of a heart.
heart hands:
Forming a heart shape with the hands.
A heart shape made by a single hand is a finger heart, not heart hands.
heart hands duo:
Two characters working together to form a single heart hands pose.
Use heart hands failure if only one person is contributing.
heart hands failure:
When two characters form a heart hands duo pose, but one responds with a different gesture, like a thumbs up or v instead.
Popularized by famous fighting game player justin wong (gamer) when a chun-li cosplayer did the thumbs-up at his expense. Hilariously, the same cosplayer would later try the same gesture with umehara daigo, only for Daigo to do the thumbs-up in turn.
heart hat ornament: A hat ornament shaped like a heart.
heart in eye:
When there's a heart shape inside one's eyes.
Do not mistake with heart-shaped pupils, as the pupils are not actually in heart shape, but with a heart shape inside it.
heart in heart hands: For when a heart symbol exists within the formation of a heart hands.
heart in mouth: A heart shape drawn in a character's mouth, usually on the tongue. Frequently paired with :d.
heart maebari: A maebari in the shape of a heart.
heart necklace: A necklace with a heart-shaped jewel attached on the front.
heart o-ring: A heart-shaped o-ring, which is commonly used to connect the ends of a garment together or as a simple accessory.
heart of string:
Pictures with a line that forms a heart-shaped loop. It's not really important if it's supposed to be an actual string, it may be a ribbon, a typographical element or a background decoration, etc.
The equivalent Pixiv tag is ラインのハート, literally "heart made of a line".
komeiji satori and her sister komeiji koishi sport these frequently.
heart on chest: The heart on the middle or left side chest
heart out of chest: Whenever a heart is out of someone's chest, whether it beating out as if it were in a cartoon, or actually out of their chest.
heart panties: heart print panties. Do not confuse with panties designed in a heart-shape. Use heart bikini instead, as it is still ambiguous and does not yet have tag implications. Since this tag implicates heart print, it should be exclusive to print panties. There are no tags for underwear that take on shapes.
heart pasties: pasties in the shape of a heart.
heart pendant: A pendant shaped like a heart.
heart pouch: A pouch shaped like a heart.
heart print: Clothing or an object that has at least one heart printed on it.
heart ring choker: A choker connected via a heart-shaped ring.
heart ring top: An upper garment connected using a heart-shaped ring.
heart straw: A type of crazy straw that's shaped like a heart in the middle. A common variant is a pair of straws twisted into a heart shape and designed for sharing, as in post #2414544.
heart tail:
When a character has one or more tails bent in the shape of a heart. A common visual gag used for valentine's Day-themed pictures or as a general sign of affection.
Not to be confused with demon tails, which typically have a heart-shaped tip.
heart tail duo: Similar to heart hands duo, this tag describes two characters whose tails meet to form a heart tail. Not to be used for a single character with multiple tails.
heart tattoo: A tattoo of a heart symbol.
heart wand: A wand or staff that has a heart shape affixed at the top.
heart-shaped bag: A bag that is designed to resemble a heart shape.
heart-shaped boob challenge: The heart-shaped boob challenge (Chinese: 桃心胸挑战) is a trend in which women post selfies of themselves making a heart-shape over their breasts such that their hand covers their nipple. The trend, which began in July of 2017 on Chinese social media, was seemingly started by a Chinese live-streamer by the name of Ayi Xi Tai Lǜ (@阿姨洗太绿).
heart-shaped box:
A box shaped like a heart. Popular with valentine gifts containing chocolates.
Not to be confused with the "song":[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n6P0SitRwy8] by Nirvana.
heart-shaped buckle: A buckle in the shape of a heart.
heart-shaped chocolate:
A piece of chocolate in the shape of a heart, often reserved for valentine's Day.
Don't use this tag if you only see a heart-shaped box, but you're not able to actually see its contents. It's only an assumption that it could contain a chocolate heart, but it could also contain anything such as a box of chocolates, candy, or another present.
heart-shaped eyes:
When a character has literal hearts for eyes, like a cartoon character. Generally a sign of being love-struck.
This is NOT for when hearts are inside of a character's eyes (e.g., post #751872). Instead, use heart-shaped pupils or heart in eye.
heart-shaped eyewear:
Eyewear that have heart-shaped frames. 
Do not use for eyepatches, use heart eyepatch.
heart-shaped food: Any food item that is heart-shaped.
heart-shaped gem: A gem that has been crafted into the shape of a heart.
heart-shaped lock:
A lock in the shape of a heart.
Most commonly seen in kantai collection images, after the heart lock feature that allows a lock to be placed on ship girls to prevent accidentally scrapping them.
heart-shaped lollipop: A lollipop shaped like a heart.
heart-shaped mouth: Where a person's mouth is shaped like a heart.
heart-shaped pillow:
A pillow shaped like a heart.
For pillows with heart shapes printed on them, see heart print print pillow.
heart-shaped pubic hair: pubic hair shaped after a heart.
heart-shaped pupils:
When a character's pupils are shaped like hearts. Often a sign of being lovestruck or experiencing sexual pleasure.
See heart in eye for when there are hearts inside the eyes, but the eyes aren't shaped like hearts. See heart-shaped eyes for when a character's entire eyes are literal hearts, like a cartoon character in love.
heartbeat:
This tag is for heartbeat sounds (typically ドキドキ, dokidoki).
For the line with spikes that represents heart activity (post #4068659) see cardiogram.
heater:
A heater, or space heater, is a device used to heat a single small area, such as a room.  These devices generate heat through various means, such as burning fuel or using electricity to heat coils.
##### Types
- kerosene heater
- potbelly stove
- space heater
heather mason: Heather Mason (ヘザー・メイソン, Hezā Meison) is a fictional character in silent hill (series). She is first introduced as a supporting character in the original Silent Hill (1999), and later returns as the main protagonist of silent hill 3 (2003).
heattech leotard:
A meme outfit consisting of a turtleneck leotard made of a ribbed material resembling a sweater. The outfit is sold by uniqlo and is made of HeatTech, a thin material designed to wick away moisture and hold body heat. The outfit comes in red, black, or grey.
The leotards worn by the shadaloo dolls are visually similar except for the neckties, but they should not be referred as such due to the difference in colors as well as overall design. The leotard as sold by Uniqlo is not a thong leotard and does not have the backless design. Furthermore, it is secured by buttons at the crotch.
heaven burns red: A mobile RPG co-developed by key (company).
heaven's door:
stand (jojo) power of kishibe rohan from jojo no kimyou na bouken. Manifests as a short humanoid with a bowtie and hat.
Its power allows Rohan to view a person's memories as if he were reading a book made from their body.
heaven's feel: One of the three routes in the fate/stay night visual novel, focusing on matou sakura.
heavenly boat maanna: ishtar (fate)'s weapon in fate/grand order. It is an airship and a giant bow. Maanna is the boat of god that soars across the Mesopotamian world, and also a interstellar teleportation gate.
heavy: When a character visibly has a hard time handling a very heavy load.
heavy breathing: Usually indicates panting heavily during or after a strenuous activity.
heavy machine gun:
A type of machine gun that use large caliber ammunition (but less than 20 mm). Primarily designed to provide a continuous suppressive fire and pierce through light cover and unarmored vehicles. Usually mounted instead of being handheld due to heavy weight and large size.

heavy metal:
A heavy sounding and agressive subgenre of Rock music.
Emerged from the 1970s with the bands like UFO, Black Sabbath, Thin Lizzy, Rainbow, Cheap Trick and Motörhead.
and evolved from 1980s from bands like Venom, Judas Priest, Iron Maiden, Dio and Metallica.
heavy object: A 2009-current light novel series by Kamachi Kazuma, with illustrations by nagi ryou, serialized in ASCII Media Works' Dengeki Bunko Magazine and published under the Dengeki Bunko imprint. Also adapted into a 2010 manga by inue shinsuke, which was serialized in Dengeki Maou.
hebiyoi tier: A virtual youtuber and member of nanashi inc., formerly in the Sugar Lyric sub-group.
hecatia lapislazuli:
touhou character.
Based on the Greek goddess Hecate, Hecatia is a goddess who governs the Hells of the Earth, Moons and Otherworlds.  Like junko (touhou), she also has a grudge against Chang'e, whose husband shot down Apollo and indirectly weakened Hell, as Hell wouldn't be able to exist without the…
heckler & koch:
Heckler & Koch GmbH is a German arms manufacturer, located in Oberndorf am Neckar in the German state of Baden-Württemberg. It was founded on 28 December 1949 by three former Mauser engineers, Alex Seidel, Edmund Heckler and Theodor Koch.
Use the tag sparingly when the company name, multiple models of H&K-designed weapons or logo appears on the image.
hedge: Trimmed rows of bushes, found in variety of outdoor places such as parks and in front of houses.
hedgehog boy: A boy with real hedgehog features, such as quills, hedgehog ears or a hedgehog tail.
hedgehog girl: Girls with intrinsic hedgehog features, such as quills, hedgehog ears or a hedgehog tail.
heel pop:
When the heel of the foot pops out of the shoe, while the shoe is on the ground.
If the shoe is dangling in the air, see shoe dangle.
heel up:
Standing with both feet on the ground and one heel raised up.
See tiptoes for when both heels are up.
heel-less heels: Shoes with a raised heel, like high heels, only without the actual heel. Common with hoof shoes.
heero yuy: The protagonist of gundam wing. The stoic Heero is one of the pilots sent to Earth to fight against the oppressive Organization of the Zodiac, and primarily handles the controls of the wing gundam and wing gundam zero in both of its incarnations.
heian: Clothes and aesthetics from the Heian period of Japan (794-1185).
heidimarie w. schnaufer:
Heidemarie W. Schnaufer is a character from strike witches. She debuted in the Kimi to Tsunagaru Sora manga, but is more known for her appearance in the movie.
Flight Lieutenant from the Karlsland Air Force 1st Night Fighter Wing 4th Flying Corps.
height: A character's height being shown in the picture.
height chart:
A lineup of characters comparing their height.
A height chart is a reference sheet that most (if not all) character designers do while designing the characters for a ilustration, comic or animation. The principal function of a height chart is to help the artist to draw the characters accurately when they are interacting with objects, other characters and even the background.
height conscious:
When a character is unhappy about their height.
Add height envy if the unhappiness is due to another character in the picture.
height difference: When one character is conspicuously taller than another character.
height mark: Marks on a surface, typically a wall, used to measure someone's height. A common sight in mugshots.
heinrike prinzessin zu sayn-wittgenstein:
A character from noble witches; a Night Witch, from Karlsland, in the 506th joint fighter wing as a Flight Lieutenant. Her Ace Archetype is Heinrich Prinz zu Sayn-Wittgenstein. 
Her weapon is a MG151/20 cannon, and her familiar is the black cat.
heisei:
Heisei (平成, lit. "becoming peaceful" or "peace everywhere") is the official name of the era of Japanese history spanning from 1989 to 2019.
Beginning immediately after the death of emperor hirohito and the ascension of Crown Prince Akihito to the Chrysanthemum Throne, the Heisei era followed the shouwa era (1926-1989), the taishou era (1912-1926), and the meiji era (1868-1912). The Heisei ended on May 1, 2019, when Akihito abdicated and his son Naruhito succeeded him as emperor, marking the beginning of the reiwa.
heisei retro: Aesthetic and fashion style based around nostalgia for the heisei period, primarily featuring elements associated with '90s and 2000s Japanese childhood, especially that of young girls and the clothing that was marketed to them during the time. It is closely related to yume kawaii and y2k fashion. In the West, it is often referred to as "cutecore".
heiter: Heiter was the alcohol-loving priest of the Hero Party, which consisted of Hero Himmel, Mage Frieren, and Warrior Eisen. Heiter is known as a drunkard, which is why Frieren calls him a "Corrupt Priest".
heixiu: Small autonomous clones of luo xiaohei broken off from his tail.
held up: When a character is lifted up by another person holding them. This is often, but not always, against the liftee's volition.
helel ben shalem:
A granblue fantasy character.
A divine servant not seen since antiquity reawakens in a world which to her is the future. She journeys across the skies, determined to fill in the blank spaces that dot her memories.
Voiced by ise mariya.
heles:
Playable Fire-type granblue fantasy character.
She has long silver hair in a single braid and yellow eyes. As an Erun, she naturally has cat ears. She wears a short armored white dress, gold hair tubes, and a blue hairband that creates subtle hair intakes.  Her choice of weapon is a spear.
helicopter: An aircraft that flies using rotor blades to generate lift.
hell: In religion and folklore, hell is a place of eternal suffering and torment, meant to punish evil souls in the afterlife. It is commonly associated with fire and demons.
hello kitty: Hello Kitty is a friendly white kitty with the head larger than her body, small button eyes and nose, but no mouth. She is said to be five apples tall and the weight of three apples.
hellsing: A 1997-2009 seinen manga written and illustrated by hirano kouta, originally serialized in Young King OURs for 89 chapters, which were collected in ten volumes.
helltaker: A short indie puzzle/romance/||bullet hell rhythm|| game created by Polish developer vanripper. The full game is available for free on Steam, and can be comfortably beaten in about two hours.
helluva boss: Helluva Boss is an animated web series set in the same universe of hazbin hotel. The series follows the misadventures of the Immediate Murder Professionals, or I.M.P., an assassination group that kills humans on Earth on behalf of their clients from Hell.
helm:
A medieval-style helmet that completely encloses the head. It offers absolute protection at the expense of being cumbersome and limiting vision greatly. This is the classic knightly armor and is generally build around the entire suit of armor. This is separate from a helmet with a built-in face mask since that is the addition of a component to the helmet while the helm is one-piece.
For depictions of the steering mechanism of a ship, use the ship's wheel tag.
helma lennartz:
Character from strike witches: suomus misfits squadron.
A Flight Sergeant from the Karlsland Air Force. One of the first testers of Jet Strikers. Noted for her deep admiration of gertrud barkhorn due to her similar strict and nagging personality. erica hartmann calls her "Mini-Trude".
helmet: A protective piece of armor designed to protect the cranium from damage. The design and shape can vary because of the time-period, setting, and what the helmet is to protect the cranium from.
helmet over eyes: A character's helmet is covering their eyes, but not the rest of their face.
hemokinesis: blood that is controlled by magical, telekinetic, or otherwise supernatural ability.
henohenomoheji:
A popular doodle of a face that consists of Japanese hiragana characters as shown below.  Normally the "frame" of the face consists of a large "ji", though this is sometimes omitted and cannot be normally typed.
へ へ
の の
  も
 へ
Sometimes found on and associated with scarecrows.
henrietta de tristain: A character from the series zero no tsukaima.
henshin:
Henshin (変身) is the Japanese phrase for "transformation". It is also a visual sequence for transformation prevalent in japanese media, in both tokusatsu and anime such as mecha or magical girl series. 
Although some speculate that the "henshin pose" originates from kabuki or cheerleading, the original inspiration is unclear.
henshin pose:
The pose a character strikes before they transform, mostly associated with Kamen Riders and/or Pretty Cures.
Usually required for transformation, but are sometimes purely cosmetic.
変態王子と笑わない猫。, lit. The "HENTAI" Prince and the Stony Cat.
A 2010-current light novel series by Saraga Sou, with illustration by kantoku, published under Media Factory's MF Bunko J imprint.
henya the genius: A bilingual Japanese virtual youtuber, member of vshojo. Designed by squeaky (artist), illustrated by garan co, and rigged by Iron Vertex's etctr (artist).
heracross:
Pokémon #214 in the National PokéDex, a dual type Bug/Fighting Pokémon.
It can Mega Evolve into mega heracross when using the Heracronite.
Japanese Name: Heracros
Prior Pokémon: shuckle
Next Pokémon: sneasel
herb: A catchall term for any plant with leaves, seeds, or flowers used for flavoring and/or garnishing food, medicine, or perfume.
herb bundle:
Any or all individual specimens or assortments of herbs, flowers, spices, roots, or other plant materials that have been bound together (generally with rope or twine) and hung out to dry.
May often be seen suspended (usually upside-down) from the ceiling, on a wall, along the length of a shelf or doorway, or near a window.
Commonly (but not necessarily) found adorning the interiors of rural households, or within the abodes of alchemists, healers, magicians, witches, et al.
hercule barton: Character from the series tantei opera milky holmes.
herlock sholmes:
Ersatz name for Sherlock Holmes, made-up in 1907 by Maurice Leblanc to avoid getting sued by Arthur Conan Doyle for using his character.
On Danbooru, it refers to the great ace attorney character, the famous detective who works alongside ryunosuke naruhodo.
hermione granger: Character in J.K. Rowling's harry potter (series) series.
hermit crab: A small soft-bodied crab that uses empty seashells to live in, or uses other portable objects- for protection.
hermit purple: stand (jojo) power of joseph joestar (old) from jojo no kimyou na bouken. It manifests as multiple purple thorny vines that spawn from Joseph's right hand.
hermitcraft:
Hermitcraft is a private Minecraft survival multiplayer server, and one of the longest running, having started its first season in 2012.
For a list of characters, see list of minecraft youtubers.
heroman: A 2009 manga illustrated by Oota Tamon and serialized in Square Enix's Monthly Shounen Gangan and 2010 anime created by former Marvel Comics head stan lee in association with BONES.
heshikiri hasebe:
A touken ranbu character. 
The personification of the katana of the same name

hip hop:
A music genre and cultural movement originating from new york city in the 70s. The subculture encompasses a variety of facets, including music, dance, fashion, and DJing. hiroshimaben:
A Japanese dialect spoken in the western parts of hiroshima Prefecture. Usually considered the stereotypical yakuza dialect.
Heavily features the usage of じゃ (ja) as copula instead of だ (da) in Standard Japanese. Prefers のう (nou) as the sentence-final emphatic particle (instead of Standard Japanese "yo" or "ne"), and shortens から (kara) to け ("ke", often elongated to "kee"). "Jakee" will also pop up in place of the standard "dakara" (this can sometimes be deceptive as it can also have a different nuance).  
Female speakers will often use "uchi" as a first-person 'pronoun'.

kaiju:
Kaiju (怪獣) is a Japanese word that means "strange beast," but often translated in English as "monster." Specifically, it is used to refer to a genre of tokusatsu entertainment involving giant monsters.
Related terms include kaiju eiga (怪獣映画, monster movie), a film featuring kaiju, kaijin (怪人, humanoid monsters) and daikaiju (大怪獣, giant monster), specifically meaning the larger variety of monsters.
The most famous kaiju is godzilla. Other well-known kaiju include mothra, anguirus, rodan, gamera, and king ghidorah.

karate: Karate (空手) is a martial art developed in the Ryukyu Kingdom. It developed from the indigenous Ryukyuan martial arts (called te (手), "hand"; tii in Okinawan) under the influence of Chinese martial arts, particularly Fujian White Crane. Karate is now predominantly a striking art using punching, kicking, knee strikes, elbow strikes and open-hand techniques such as knife-hands, spear-hands, and palm-heel strikes. Historically, and in some modern styles, grappling, throws, joint locks, restraints, and vital-point strikes are also taught. A karate practitioner is called a karateka (空手家).

katana:
A type of Japanese sword (nihontou), and is often called a "samurai sword" because of its historical associations with feudal-era Japan.

kimono:
A kimono (着物) is a type of traditional Japanese clothing. It consists of a long, wide-sleeved robe, closed at the front forming a "y" shape. It is held closed with a wide belt-like sash called an obi.
Kimonos are often worn with other traditional accessories, such as zouri (traditional wooden sandals), tabi (split-toe socks), and kanzashi (traditional hair ornaments). A kinchaku (small cloth drawstring bag) is often carried while wearing a kimono.
kimono lift: Lifting up a person's kimono, usually with the intent to show off either their underwear or their bare crotch or butt.

knee blush: When a character's knee appears to be blushing.
knee boots: boots that are roughly knee-high. Knee boots may end slightly below the knee, but should not extend above the knee.

kunreishiki:
Kunrei-shiki romanization is the system for romanizing Japanese characters officially promoted by the Japanese government and taught in schools. It's intended to maintain consistency with the way kana are written without being a literal representation of the way the syllables actually sound (e.g., "sa", "si" and "sya" instead of "sa", "shi" and "sha".) For this reason, many English speakers find that it looks strange and prefer to use Hepburn romanization which is also used in the spelling of tags throughout Danbooru.

The bow itself will be quite long, yet the arrow is still fired in the same manner as the English long bow; its main difference being the lower firing position and the bow usually extend several feet above the archer's head.

Kimono undergarments are known as juban (襦袢).

layered shirt: A character is wearing one shirt on top of another one. The shirt on the upper layer usually has shorter sleeves than the one on the bottom layer, though there are other variations as well.
layered skirt: A skirt that consists of multiple layers of fabric.
layered sleeves: When a character is wearing multiple layers of sleeves.

The LMP1 class has since been replaced by Le Mans Daytona h (LMDh) and Le Mans Hypercar (LMH) spec vehicles, which compete in both the imsa sportscar championship and the world endurance championship.

lectern:

lee-enfield:
The Lee-Enfield is a series of bolt action rifles that came in several models, chambered for .303 British cartridge. The weapon was named after its designer, James Paris Lee—and the rifling design location—the Royal Small Arms Factory in Enfield. It was the standard rifle of British and Commonwealth forces during world war i and world war ii. 
The feed system is detachable 10-round magazine, usually fed from 5-round clips.

left-hand drive:
A motor vehicle with the steering wheel on the left side. Typical for most of the world. 
Exceptions include Japan, Indonesia, Thailand, Great Britain, and many of its current and former colonies. They instead use right-hand drive.
However, left hand drive is popular with imported European cars in Japan due to it feeling more foreign and, in the case of German cars, better.
left-handed: A character who is using their left hand as the dominant hand.  Not as common as right handed people due to both genetics and old views on it.
left-to-right manga:

Basically, if a rifle or shotgun has what looks like a handguard around where the character holds the gun (grip), it is very likely a lever-action gun.

looking at object:
For when a character is looking at any inanimate object.

looking at penis: When a character is looking directly at a penis, usually without awe.

looking at self: This tag indicates a character is generally looking at themselves. Use looking at hand or  looking at hands when a character is specifically looking only at their hand(s), looking at mirror when a mirror reflection is involved, or looking at another when the "self" is actually another iteration of dual persona or multiple persona.
looking at viewer:
When a character is making direct eye contact with the viewer. (i.e. simply looking at the camera/through the fourth wall)
Don't confuse with eye contact, which relates to characters making eye contact amongst themselves.
Don't confuse with facing viewer, which should be used when the eyes are closed, covered (e.g. with a blindfold), or looking at another direction.
looking away: Ambiguous. If the character is deliberately looking away from the viewer or character(s) out of a certain emotion, use averting eyes. If the character is simply not looking at the viewer, use one of the tags that indicates looking direction listed below. If the character is angling their body in some way relative to the viewer or character(s), but has eyes closed or obstructed, use one of the tags that indicates facing direction listed below.
looking back:
Indicates a subject of the image is looking behind their normal plane of vision.  This could mean they are turning their body, head, or only their eyes to look behind themselves. The subject's gaze should be directed fully or almost fully backwards over the shoulder, anywhere from 135 to 180 degrees behind them relative to their front.
Oftentimes combined with from behind and looking at viewer, and also sideways glance if the character's body is partly facing away.
If the character has both of their eyes closed, use facing back instead.
looking down: Perspective or action that has character looking down.
looking inside:
A character looking inside a building, vehicle, or other enclosed space from the outside.
Opposite of looking outside.
looking outside:

looking over eyewear:

looking through own legs:

This is mutually exclusive from view between legs since that tag refers to the viewer's perspective. This tag refers to the character's perspective. Both instances may be seen together though, such as post #3155529.
looking through scope: When character is looking through a telescope or derivative such as binoculars, spyglass, monocular, or a gun's scope.
looking to the side: When a character's gaze is directed to something off to their side. If the eyes are directed more than 45 degrees backwards use looking back instead. If the character looks to the side without moving their head, combine with sideways glance.
looking up: Perspective or action that has a character looking up relative to the character's body. To be specific, the tag should be determined first by the position of the eyes and then by the position of the neck. m1 garand:
An American semi-automatic rifle, primarily chambered for .30-06 Springfield cartridge. Widely replaced the M1903 Springfield and Lee-Enfield bolt action rifles, it became the primary service rifle of the US Army during the world war ii, including Korean War. The weapon is named after its designer, John Garand.
Its feed system is 8-round en-bloc clip. The M1 Garand is well-known for making a “ping” sound after firing the last round when the clip is ejected.
m14:
The M14 is an American-designed 7.62×51mm NATO battle rifle, developed in 1954 by Earle Harvey and Lloyd Corbett at Springfield Armory, adopted by the U.S. military in 1959. Its design was heavily based on the earlier m1 garand, but uses standard 20-round detachable magazines instead of 8-round internal one and select-fire capability.
It began to be supplanted in 1963 by the m16 rifle, eventually being fully adopted into the U.S military by 1969. It continues to be used in secondary (marksman) roles due to its firepower, longer range and accuracy.
m16:
An American-designed 5.56x45mm assault rifle, developed in 1957 by Eugene Stoner at ArmaLite and based on his previous ar-10 design. The rifle had initial bad notoriety due to the original design's tendency to jam with dirt or in some weather conditions, but is also regarded effective thanks to its low weight and high accuracy.
It has been the standard weapon of the US military since 1964. Visually distinguishable by its triangular front sight and integrated carrying handle/rear sight, although newer variants (such as the shortened m4 carbine version) sport removable units.
m16a1: An early version of the M16. Distinguishable by its triangular grip and 20 round magazine.
m16a2: Modification of the m16 with a new barrel profile to allow mounting of the m203 grenade launcher, along with other changes.
m1903 springfield:
The Springfield M1903 (United States Rifle, Caliber .30-06, Model 1903) is an American bolt action rifle built on the Mauser action, fed with an internal 5-round magazine. It was designed in 1903 and mainly manufactured by Springfield Armory.
It was used by US forces, most notably during the Two World Wars, korean war, and vietnam war for limited sniper role. The weapon is recognizable by its straight grip stock, Type C semi-pistol grip stock (M1903A1 variant), bent bolt handle, oblong stock indentation on some models, and an adjustable flip-up rear sight or aperture one (M1903A3).
m1911:
An American single-action, semi-automatic handgun designed by john moses browning. Its short-recoil operation with a reciprocating slide highly influenced modern pistol designs.
The m1911 is visually identifiable by its external hammer, a beaver tail safety, both grip panels being held by two screws and a thumb safety. Chambered for the .45 ACP cartridge, the standard magazine capacity is seven rounds. In 1924, the M1911 was largely revised into the M1911A1, with a shorter trigger and a longer back spur. It was the standard sidearm of the U.S. military from 1911 to 1985.
m1918 bar:

The weapon is recognizable by its bottom-folding bipod installed on the muzzle, rectangular one-piece forearm, and a flip-up rear sight with a windage knob.
This tag also apply to any foreign-produced variants, such as the Polish Browning wz. 28 which notably has a pistol grip (post #6539181) or the French MAS mle 1922.
m203: An American single-shot, muzzle-loading 40mm underbarrel grenade launcher. It was designed to replace the m79, which was a stand-alone weapon. The under-barrel design gave soldiers the advantage of having quicker switch of both rifle and grenade launcher, making them more adaptable in combat. The M203 was originally designed designed for the m16 and m4 carbine but can be fitted to many other rifles without modification.

The MG34 was not suitable for quick mass production and costly. So it was supplanted by the mg42 despite both remained in service.

mg42:
The MG42 (Maschinengewehr 42) is a German world war ii-era open-bolt machine gun, chambered for the 7.92×57mm Mauser round. It supplanted the earlier mg34 in 1942 due to lower manufacturing cost thanks to dominant stamped metal parts. Its highest cyclic rate of fire at 1200 RPM, made the weapon gained the nickname Hitler's Buzzsaw.
The mg42 (girls' frontline) is recognizable by its barrel shroud with squared-off profile and larger perforations. It is belt-fed and also accepts dual drum magazines.

morning glory:
A common name for more than 1000 species of flowering plants in the Convolvulaceae family.
The plant bears funnel-shaped flowers that close late in the day. They are known for their five symmetrical, finely overlapping petals and bright colors in shades of pink, red, blue, and purple; the center is often white. The flowers often have a distinctive star shape in the center, which is often emphasized by artists. Depending on the species, the leaves can be heart-shaped or ivy-shaped (three-lobed). Morning glory vines are often trained to climb trellises but will eagerly climb fences as well.
morning glory print: Clothing or an object that has at least one morning glory printed on it.

mosin-nagant:
A russian 7.62×54mmR bolt action rifle.
It entered service in 1892 with the Russian military and was primarily used in the russo-japanese war, world war i, and world war ii. The Mosin-Nagant features a straight/horizontal bolt handle (except on the sniper variant, which had a bent bolt handle), slot-type gun sling mounts (except for the Finnish variants), and a partially visible 5-round internal magazine in front of the trigger.
mosquito: A slender long-legged flying bug with aquatic larvae. The bite of the bloodsucking female can transmit a number of serious diseases including malaria and encephalitis.
mosquito coil:
Katorisenkō (蚊取線香, 蚊取り線香): a coil of insect-repellent incense originally made from pyrethrum, a chrysanthemum with insecticidal properties. Invented in 1902 in Japan. Often placed in a ceramic kayari buta.
Along with wind chimes, paper fans, sitting on the porch (endai), etc, commonly included in domestic summer scenes.
moss: A small flowerless green plant resembling carpet or short grass that can usually be seen growing on rocky terrain. Not to be confused with algae or mold.
moth: An insect related to the butterfly, but are generally agricultural pests. The domesticated moth Bombyx mori, or silkworm larvae, is bred for silk production.
moth antennae: antennae of a moth. Have a fluffy or frond-like appearance.
moth girl: A type of arthropod girl that has characteristcs of a moth. They are frequently depicted having a thing for lamps.
moth wings: Having wings like that of a moth.

motor vehicle: Any motorized, self-propelled ground vehicle that does not operate on railroad tracks. Commonly wheeled or sometimes has caterpillar tracks.

mp40:
The MP40 (Maschinenpistole 40) is a German WWII-era 9×19mm submachine gun. It was initially designed by Heinrich Vollmer in 1938, and production started in 1940. The weapon features open-bolt mechanism, low cost stamped metal parts, synthetic furniture, and a bottom-folding stock. Feed system is standard 32-round magazine.

multi-strapped bikini: Deprecated, use multi-strapped bikini top or multi-strapped bikini bottom instead.

multi-strapped bikini top:

multi-tied hair:

multicolored background:
Any background that contains multiple colors.
h1. See also
- two-tone background

multicolored bikini: Multicolored bikini has two or more colors on the leg or have blended colors. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored bodysuit: When a bodysuit has at least two colors present on its design. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored bow:
A bow that has two or more colors present in its design. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
Be sure not to confuse a multicolored bow for a multicolored ribbon, since bows are not always made out of ribbons.
multicolored bowtie: A bowtie with at least two different colors.
multicolored bra: A bra that has at least two or more colors. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored buttons: When an item of clothing has buttons of different colors.
multicolored cape: A cape that has at least two or more colors present in its design. This also applies to when the interior layer has a different color of fabric from the main exterior layer, such as post #1488794. See multicolored clothes for further guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored capelet: A capelet that is two or more colors.
multicolored clothes:
Clothing that prominently features two or more distinct colors. For example, a red-and-blue dress.
- White, black, and grey don't count. For example, blue-and-white striped thighhighs don't count.
- Multiple shades of the same color don't count. For example, a light-blue-and-dark-blue shirt doesn't count.
- Trim, bows, or other decorations don't count.
- Simple two-color argyle, plaid, polka dot, checkered, gradient, print, or other patterns that have their own tags don't count.
In essence, multicolored clothes need to have unusual colors and styles that pop out visually to the viewer.
multicolored coat: When a coat has at least two or more colors present. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored dress: When a dress has at least two or more colors present. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored eyes: A character or person depicted has more than one color in the same eye (gradient eyes, for example). For a character where both eyes have irises that are not identical to each other in color, use heterochromia.
multicolored footwear: Footwear of any style, that has a multicolored scheme. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored fur: body fur comprised of more than one color.
multicolored gloves:
Gloves sporting multiple colors for a single glove. If the gloves in a pair are not identical to each other, use uneven gloves.
See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered to be multicolored.
multicolored hair: Hair that has more than one color. All hair colors present should be tagged, if possible.
multicolored hairband: A hairband consisting of multiple colors. Popularized with tenkyuu chimata.
multicolored halo: A halo with more 2 or more colors.
multicolored headwear: This tag has been deprecated for being too broad. Use a more specific tag like multicolored hat, multicolored hairband, etc.
multicolored hoodie: A hoodie with a multicolored pattern.
multicolored horns:
Horns with different colors in them.
See also: gradient horns.
multicolored jacket: A jacket that has two or more distinct colors in its design. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored kimono:
A kimono that has two or more distinct colors present in its design. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
This includes other kimono-styled tops such as yukatas and furisodes.
multicolored legwear:
Ambiguous tag. Use more specific ones like multicolored leggings, multicolored pants, multicolored pantyhose, multicolored socks or multicolored thighhighs.
For differently-colored legwear see instead mismatched legwear.
multicolored leotard: A leotard that has two or more colors. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored nails: When a character has fingernails and/or toenails featuring a variety of colors, typically (but not exclusively) as a result of selective application of nail polish. Each nail may have different colors, or the nails can have multiple colors on each one, such as a ladybug or rainbow pattern.
multicolored neckerchief: A neckerchief that has at least two colors.
multicolored necktie: A necktie that has two or more distinct colors present in its design. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored panties: A pair of panties that have at least two or more colors present in its design. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored pants: A pair of pants that have at least two or more colors present. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored pantyhose: pantyhose that have more than one color present.
multicolored polka dots:
Polka dots that have a multicolored scheme, rather than just one color.
Note that not all multicolored polka dots can qualify as part of multicolored clothes. See the guidelines there on what constitutes multicolored clothing when polka dots are involved.
multicolored ribbon:
A ribbon that has two or more distinct colors present in its design. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
Be sure not to confuse a multicolored ribbon with a multicolored bow. Ribbons should be loose strands of fabric rather than tied into bows.
multicolored scarf: A scarf that has at least two or more colors present in its design. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored shirt: A shirt that has at least two or more colors present in its design. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored shorts: A pair of shorts that have at least two different colors present on their design. See multicolored clothes for detailed guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored skin:
When a character has two or more distinct colors making up their layer of skin. All skin colors present should be tagged, if possible.
This doesn't include naturally occurring differences in colors such as areolae, nipples, bruises, tan and blushing to name a few. At least one of the skin colors has to be unnatural and the colors have to be visually distinct from each other. 
For instance, post #472760 has blue skin and red skin divided evenly on her flesh.
multicolored skirt:
A skirt that has at least two or more colors present in its design. 
Take care when there is an image with a layered skirt in it though, such as post #1850259. If each layer has a single color, then it isn't a multicolored skirt. Each layer can be tagged with each individual color, so for the aforementioned post, the tags would be layered skirt yellow skirt red skirt blue skirt. This tag is specifically when a single layer of short cloth has multiple colors on it.
See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored sky:
A sky that has at least two or more colors. This is especially prevalent during a sunset or sunrise.
This tag implicates sky. Don't use it for posts where the sky isn't a significant part of the image (forum #162192).
multicolored stripes: Clothes that have stripes with 3 or more colors.
multicolored sweater: A sweater that has at least two or more colors present in its design. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored swimsuit: A swimsuit that has at least two or more colors present. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
multicolored tail: An animal tail that has two or more distinctive colors present. This must not include greyscale colors like white, grey and black, unless one of those colors is present in a set of three or more colors, like post #2541737.
multicolored thighhighs: thighhighs that have two or more distinct colors present. The thighhighs need to have the same design on both legs. If not, it's considered mismatched legwear.
multicolored wings:
A pair of wings that have at least two or more colors present, either as a gradient or otherwise.
If one wing is a completely different color than the other one, use asymmetrical wings. Don't use this tag if the asymmetrical wings are colored with greyscale colors (white/grey/black), as they don't fit the guidelines for multicolored.
multilingual: A post with the same text in more than two different languages. May or may not be correctly translated.
multiple 4koma: Two or more sets of 4koma in one image. Extra details besides the 4koma (such as a character standing beside the panels) don't count.
multiple anal: Multiple objects penetrating the anus at the same time.
multiple belts:
For when a single character has more than one belt on them.
Do not tag just when multiple characters are wearing belts.
multiple bracelets: When a character is wearing multiple bracelets.
multiple braids: A character has more than two braids done in their hair.
multiple cats: More than 1 cat in the frame.
multiple condoms: For when there are multiple used condoms, multiple condoms in a roll, or something similar.
multiple crossover:
crossover/fusion/parody involving at least three copyrights.
Crossovers within a franchise (for example all Final Fantasy villains together, or all Links meeting each other) don't qualify unless they also involve two or more other franchises.
multiple dogs:
Images depicting more than one dog.
If there are a lot of dogs, use too many dogs.
multiple drawing challenge: A challenge where artists show multiple different drawings, typically of the same character or copyright or around a common theme, usually in separate panels of a chart.
multiple earrings: When more than one earring has been pierced into one ear.
multiple fusions: Two or more fusions in the same image.
multiple hair bows: When a character is wearing three or more hair bows in their hair. This doesn't apply to when there are just two hair bows since it is very common, nor does it apply when the bows are on a hat or hood. For that, see multiple hat bows.
multiple hairpins: When a character wears more than one hairpins on hair.
multiple hands: Use this tag when either there are more than the two expected hands attached to a character (e.g. post #942632, post #1914774 or post #238700), or a multitude of hands are shown not attached to anyone in particular (e.g. post #3773988, post #3587393, or post #984404).
multiple hat bows:
Any type of headwear that has three or more bows attached to it.
Popularly associated with the Fate series' abigail williams (fate) in her second and third Ascension forms.
multiple hats: A character wearing multiple hats or a hat and other form of headwear at the same time, either on different parts of the head or one on top of another.
multiple heads:
A character with more than one head/neck. Commonly seen on monsters and fantasy animals such as the mythical cerberus and hydra, or dodrio.
Not to be confused with extra faces, to which the character may have more faces compared to the head it possess.
multiple horns: Use this tag when a character has more than two horns.
multiple legs:
A monster girl or mecha with more than two legs.
These additional legs should be normal for the character, such as a spider girl having eight legs. If the legs are abnormal, such as a human having a third leg, then use the extra legs tag instead.
multiple monochrome:
An image which is composed of multiple monochrome subsections, each using a different color.
A common example would be an image in which multiple characters are each drawn using only one color thematically appropriate to them. 
Avoid applying this tag unless each character or distinct object in question could, standing alone, be tagged monochrome. However, this tag can apply to part of an image if the tag holds true for that part (e.g. the background of post #580199).
multiple moons:
Several moons in any order and phases.
Use moon phases when depicting different phases of the moon.
multiple necklaces: More than one necklace on a character's neck.
multiple others: Images depicting multiple ambiguously or non-gendered characters.
multiple penises:
For characters surrounded by penises, see surrounded by penises.
For a single character with more than one penis, see extra penises.
multiple persona: Similar to dual persona, except that there at least three personas of the same character involved. Take note that the solo tag, or singular people counters (1boy, 1girl, 1other) should not be used with this tag. If the instances of the character are identical, use clone instead. no jacket: When a character who is officially and typically depicted wearing a jacket is drawn without one.

no nipples: When a character's bare chest is fully visible and unobscured (e.g. by fog), but their nipples (where expected) are absent.
no nose: When a character has no discernible nose projecting from the face.

no pants:

number pun:

They can also be read as though they had dakuten (゛) or handakuten (゜) added to them if necessary. o-ring:
Any clothing or accessories that have an O-shaped ring through which parts of a garment can pass and then connect together. Any types of clothes that aren't implicated here can just use this tag as a placeholder, rather than creating new tags for every type of o-ring clothing.
For the time being, "o-ring" also covers all other loop shapes, such as ovals, rectangles or any thing else containing a hole. For hearts, use heart o-ring.
o-ring belt: A belt with a prominent o-ring connecting the ends.
o-ring bikini: A bikini that uses circular o-rings to connect the straps or cups of the bikini together.
o-ring bottom:
A bottom where an O-shaped ring figures prominently. For example, a bikini bottom where the sides are connected via large circular rings.
This also includes non-circular shapes, such as ovals, hearts, rectangles or any thing else containing a hole through which parts of a garment can pass and then connect together.
o-ring choker: A choker with an o-ring, usually at the front or the back
o-ring collar: A collar with an o-ring in the front.
o-ring harness: A harness the features an o-ring as part of its design.
o-ring legwear: Any type of legwear that has and/or is held up with an o-ring. Not to be confused with o-ring thigh strap.
o-ring panties: A pair of panties that have an o-ring keeping them together, typically at the sides.
o-ring swimsuit:
A one-piece swimsuit with o-ring(s) prominently displayed.
In the case of a bikini, or other clothing with separate top and bottom, use o-ring top and o-ring bottom where need. If both are present, o-ring bikini should suffice.
o-ring thigh strap:
A thigh strap with an o-ring, this includes heart o-rings. Not to be confused with o-ring legwear which is for any type of legwear with an o-ring.
For o-ring thigh straps that are part of a legwear garter, use o-ring legwear garter instead.
o-ring top:
A top where an O-shaped ring figures prominently. For example, a bikini top where the breast cups are connected in front via a large circular ring.
This also includes non-circular shapes, such as ovals, hearts, rectangles or any thing else containing a hole through which parts of a garment can pass and then connect together.
o3o:
The emoticon of loose or puckered lips, usually as a face fault.

o o:
Eyes drawn as solid white circles with a thick black rim. Used to express surprise.
If the eyes are solid black, use solid circle eyes instead.

oar:

oarfish:

obese: Characters who are fatter than fat.
obi: An obi (帯, おび) is a wide and long embroidered sash for a kimono. Also used to tie attire (usually a robe top) closed. Will often have an ornament in the front but off to the side.

obidome:
Obidome (帯留め, おびどめ) are small brooches worn threaded onto the obijime, making a charming decoration on the front of the obi. Can be made of wood, ceramic, resin, mother-of-pearl, or precious metals. Often in designs such as flowers, small objects, or animals.
The back surface will almost always be flat with two closely-spaced raised rectangular holes, used for sliding the obidome over the thin flat obijime cord.
When an obijime is made specifically to be worn with obidome, it will be thinner and flatter than average, and known as sanbu-himo.
obijime:
Obijime (帯締め, おびじめ) is a small decorative string tied around the obi, used only in women's kimono.
It's about 150 cm (4.9 ft) long and is tied around the obi and through the knot, and which doubles as decoration. It can be a woven string, or be constructed as a narrow sewn tube of fabric. There are both flat and round obijime. They often have tassels at both ends and are made from silk, satin, brocade or viscose. A cord-like or a padded tube obijime is considered more festive and ceremonial than a flat one.
object behind ear: Putting object (pencil, pen, crayon, cigarette, wand, ect) behind the ear.
object floating above hand:
Something floating above a character's hand(s); can either be something intangible, such as an orb, heart or a star symbol, in which a character might be casting a spell - or it might be a physical object, in which it might occur due to telekinesis. 
A character might be cupping one or both hands. The object might also be glowing.
The object may also simply be falling, e.g., such as with a coin flip.
object focus:

object head: A humanoid being with an inanimate object in place of a head.
object in clothes: When a character has an atypical object tucked into their clothes.
object in pocket: A pocket with an item in it.
object in swimsuit: Tucking an object inside one's swimsuit.
object insertion:
When an inanimate object, such as a vibrator, dildo, a carrot, etc., is inserted either vaginally or anally.

object insertion from behind: When an object is inserted, either vaginally or anally, by reaching behind the back or around the legs.
object namesake: A type of pun when a character is paired with any kind of object or animal that makes a reference to their civilian or alter ego's name. For instance, 'Yuri/百合' means 'lily', so a character named Yuri holding a bouquet of lilies would qualify.
object on breast: Something is placed on the character's breast(s).
object on head:

object request: When an object that almost certainly has a name cannot be identified, use this tag.
object through head: An object piercing a person's head, either partially or all the way through.
objectification: Like a reverse personification, objectification occurs when a character is portrayed as an inanimate object.

obliques: This tag is to be used when well-developed oblique muscles are noticeable, i.e. you should not use this tag to describe hip lines or hip bones. october:

Do NOT use this tag if you see a numerical date like 1/14/2012 (January 14, 2012). Please use the dated tag for this format. The month tags are specifically for the actual word, or if a number is directly representing a month in a calendar.

oekaki:
A drawing made with very simple tools, usually imageboard/bbs-embedded drawing software, with very sharp and thin lines.
Oekaki (お絵描き) is Japanese for "scribble" or "doodle". On the Internet, an Oekaki is a message board system that revolves around computer art created by a local art program. Oekaki artists often post their art to other websites, such as personal pages or free gallery websites, in addition to the original board.

off shoulder:
Sleeved clothing articles that rest just below a character's shoulder(s), at around the upper arm level. This includes clothing that has slipped or been pulled off the shoulders.
If they are down further, consider the clothes down tag.
For strapped clothing that has been pulled off the shoulders, use strap slip instead.
off-shoulder bikini: A specific type of shoulder-less bikini designed with a wide low-cut neckline (much like regular off shoulder garments), leaving the shoulders and upper chest area bare. Usually, it is a bikini with sleeves that sit on the arms instead of the shoulders.
off-shoulder coat: A coat that is naturally designed with a low and wide-cut neckline, not covering the shoulders or upper chest area, leaving them bare. However, this tag is infamous for being frequently misused for open or partially-open coats that are worn hanging off the upper arms, regardless of how they were designed to be worn.
off-shoulder dress:
A dress implicitly designed with a low and wide-cut neckline that leaves the shoulders and upper chest area bare. The sleeves must be attached to the dress.
Off-shoulder dresses are meant to accentuate the wearer's shoulders, collarbone, and neck (or nape), with the sleeves of an off-shoulder dress sitting on the upper arms instead of on top of the shoulders.
off-shoulder jacket: A jacket that is naturally designed with a low and wide-cut neckline, not covering the shoulders or upper chest area, leaving them bare. However, this tag is very infamous for being frequently misused among the userbase for open or partially-open jackets that are worn hanging off the upper arms, regardless of how they were designed to be worn.
off-shoulder leotard:
A leotard that is naturally designed with a low and wide-cut neckline, not covering the shoulders or upper chest area, leaving them bare.
Off-shoulder leotards are meant to emphasize and accentuate the wearer's shoulders, collarbone, and neck (or nape), with the sleeves of an off-shoulder leotard sitting on the upper arms instead of on top of the shoulders.
For the leotard to qualify for this tag, the sleeves must be attached to the leotard. If they are not, then it is a strapless leotard with detached sleeves.
Off-shoulder leotards and strapless leotards are mutually exclusive to each other.
off-shoulder one-piece swimsuit:
A shoulder-less, one-piece swimsuit designed with a wide low-cut neckline (much like regular off shoulder garments), leaving the shoulders and upper chest area bare. It is a swimsuit with sleeves that sit on the arms instead of the shoulders.
One of the variations for the Swimsuit Lancer of meltryllis (fate) is an example of this.
For two-piece swimsuits, see off-shoulder bikini.
off-shoulder shirt:
A shirt that is naturally designed with a low and wide-cut neckline, not covering the shoulders or upper chest area, leaving them bare. The sleeves must be attached to the shirt.
Off-shoulder shirts are meant to emphasize and accentuate the wearer's shoulders, collarbone, and neck (or nape), with the sleeves of an off-shoulder shirt sitting on the upper arms instead of on top of the shoulders.
off-shoulder sweater:
A specific type of shoulder-less sweater which is naturally designed with a low and wide-cut neckline which ensures that the garment sits just below the shoulders, leaving them and the wearer's upper chest area bare. Often features a thicker, sometimes mantle-like hem along the top.
Off-shoulder sweaters are meant to emphasize and accentuate the wearer's shoulders, collarbone, and neck (or nape), with the sleeves of an off-shoulder sweater sitting on the upper arms instead of on top of the shoulders.
Frequently appears as a distinct variant of ribbed sweater.
off-topic:
A post that is outside of the scope of Danbooru and in general is against the rules.
This tag should only be used for posts that are indisputably off-topic. Such posts should have nothing to do with anime, manga, games, or any other potential "on-topic" subject matter.
See off-topic status:deleted for examples of content considered to be off-topic.
offering hand:
A hand being offered to you, the viewer. Usually a prelude to holding hands, being helped up off the ground, or a dance invitation. If both hands are offered, consider incoming hug, carry me or outstretched arms instead.
For hands offering any sort of item, see incoming *.
office: A building or room where people engage in business or professional activities at their desks.
office chair:
A type of chair designed for office use. They have wheels on the bottom and can swivel. They usually have adjustable height, armrests, and back support.
Not to be confused with gaming chair.
office lady: A female office worker, including secretaries and clerks.
official alternate color:
alternate colors of official origin. This tag should be used when a significant amount of a character's color palette is different; if only a specific part of a character is a different color, use a different tag instead (for example, if only the hair color is different, use official alternate hair color).
Characters or beings may change colors to represent an alternate idea for the character, which could include an alternate form. This can be encountered in different forms such as a skin for a character in a video game or during a character's special action.
official alternate costume:
alternate costumes of official origin, whether it be from the creators themselves, or from second-parties involved in the given copyright. Generally a costume other than the standard one the character appears in.
These can often times appear in manga/anime (beach episodes, as one example), video games (whether as unlockables or as skins to be bought in gacha games), and on special events. Figures which can have such costumes include virtual youtubers.
Only use this tag for official costumes of the wearer themselves.
official alternate eye color: alternate eye colors of official origin.
official alternate hair color: alternate hair colors of official origin, such as an official alternate costume or via hair dye.
official alternate hair length:
Subset of official alternate hairstyle, where a character's different hair length has official origins.
Do not use this tag with alternate hair length, the tags are mutually exclusive.
official alternate hairstyle:
alternate hairstyles of official origin, whether it be from the creators themselves, or from second-parties involved in the given copyright. Generally a hairstyle other than the standard one the character appears in.
These can often times appear in manga/anime (beach episodes, as one example), video games (whether as unlockables or as skins to be bought in gacha games), and on special events. Figures which can have such hairstyles include Virtual YouTubers.
Do not use this tag with alternate hairstyle, the tags are mutually exclusive.
official art:
Artwork that is made by the official company/artist of a series or character. May have the copyright, company, or artist names emblazoned somewhere on the picture, as well as a copyright notice.
Not to be confused with official style, which is when an unofficial art tries to imitate the art style used in official arts.
official art inset: When a piece of official art is used as a photo inset or reference inset.
official cosplay: cosplay that is released as official material in a series. In video games, these tend to be side content or DLC costumes. In anime or other media, cosplays may be utilized by a studio where characters dress up as characters from another property owned by the same company.
official style:
Fan art that uses the same style as official art of the series.
Not to be confused with style parody, which is for art that mimics the style of another artist or series.
If an official artist (character designer, animator, etc.) shares their own fan art but not in an official capacity, it doesn't qualify for this tag. It should be in pool #19122.
official wallpaper:
A wallpaper supplied by official means.
It was customary for them to be found in the 'Downloads' section of the official website.

ofuda between fingers: A character holding one or more ofuda between their fingers.

oiran:
A traditional Japanese courtesan in Edo (present-day Tokyo), the Yoshiwara. They were a much higher-class subtype of yuujo, the iconic feudal-era Japanese prostitutes.

This gave them a social standing which put them well above any common prostitute, even outside the red-light districts. The companionship of an oiran did not come cheaply, so their clientele were primarily men of high political or social ranking.
