Pidgeotto is a raptor-like avian Pokémon. It is covered with brown feathers, and has a cream-colored face and underside. It has a crest of pinkish-red feathers on its head and black, angular markings behind its eyes.
pidgey:
Pokémon #016 in the National Pokédex, a dual type Normal/Flying Pokémon.
Pidgey is a small, plump-bodied avian Pokémon. It is primarily brown with a cream-colored face, underside, and flight feathers. Both its feet and beak are a pinkish-gray color.
pidove:
Pokémon #519 in the National PokéDex, a dual type Normal/Flying  Pokémon.
Pidove is a mainly gray, pigeon-like Pokémon. It has golden, oval eyes and a tuft of feathers atop its rounded head. It has a short, black beak with a bulbous pink cere, and a black patch on the nape of its neck.
pie:
A baked pastry crust encasing a fruit, chocolate, heavy cream, meat or vegetable filling.
Not to be confused with tart (food), which has an open top.
pie in face: Characters receiving a pie or cake in the face. This could be thrown by another character or be self inflicted.
pie slice: A cut portion of a pie.
pier: A coastal structure composed of raised platforms supported by piles or posts, similar to a one-ended bridge extending out into the water.  May be used as a simple walkway, support structures over the water, or to moor ships and boats.  Commonly made of wood, but may also be made of other materials such as metal or stone.
piercing:
An opening created in the body in which jewelry is worn.
This tag is for face and body piercings. This tag should not be used for ordinary earrings worn in the earlobes.
piercing pull:
When a piercing is pulled, such as by hand, by an object connected to it (such as a nipple chain), or even by gravity if weights are involved.
If the piercing is being pulled with enough force that it affects the pierced body part, tags such as nipple pull, or clitoris pull may be applicable as well.
piercing through clothes:
A piercing goes through both the clothes and the body part.
Do not confuse with covered piercing, which is when a piercing is visible through clothing, but does not go through it.
pierre bichelberger:
Member of the idolmaster side-m unit beit (idolmaster). 
A prince from an unknown country, Pierre is first seen working as a mascot for an amusement park that he owns. Excitable  to a fault and a bit clueless on Japanese customs.
piers nivans:
A young BSAA operative serving under the North American branch's Special Operations Unit Alpha Team, and Chris's partner in resident evil 6.
Piers Nivans, like his captain Chris Redfield, is a naturally gifted marksman, and has become known as "The man who never misses a target" in the B.S.A.A.
pig: Used for the animal and for dolls and other objects depicting one.
pig boy: A boy with pig-like features, such as pig ears.
pig ears: Use when a character has ears of a pig.
pig nose: Use when a character has a nose of a pig.
pig tail:
When a character has the tail of a pig, most notable for its distinctive curl near the tip.
Not to be confused with the pigtails hairstyle, the English equivalent of twintails.
pigeon:
For tagging purposes, pigeons are the mostly-gray birds commonly found in cities.
White birds should be tagged dove instead.
pigeon-toed:
Toes pointing inward when standing, sitting, or walking. 
Also known as in-toeing.
piggy bank: A usually ceramic pig in which coins are inserted as a way of saving money. The proper term is coin bank since there are many others made with different designs and materials that serve the same purpose.
piggyback:
A form of person carrying where the carrier supports a person on their back and holds their legs, while the person being carried wraps their arms around the carrier's chest or neck. 
For when the person being carried is sitting on the shoulders, see shoulder carry.
piglet: A piglet is a juvenile pig, boar, or warthog.
pikachu:
Pokémon #025 in the National Pokédex, an Electric type Pokémon.
A yellow mouse-like Pokémon, arguably the most popular of its type and highly symbolic of the franchise as a whole. Playable in the super smash bros. series.
pikachu ears: Characters who either have, or wear as a fashion accessory, Pikachu ears.
pikachu tail: When a character has a tail reminiscent of the famous Pokemon pikachu. The tail is yellow-colored and jagged to resemble a lightning bolt. Sometimes a black spot is on the tip.
pikipek:
Pokémon #731 in the National PokéDex, a Normal/Flying dual-type Pokémon. 
Pikipek is an avian Pokémon with black plumage. Its gray beak is long with a pointed, black tip, and it has large blue eyes. There is a white, mask-like marking on its face.
It evolves into trumbeak, then into toucannon.
pikmin 4: The fourth main installment in the pikmin (series) series, released for the Nintendo Switch in July 2023.
pile bunker: A fictional melee weapon. Its first appearance was in soukou kihei votoms. An armor-piercing spike just like a pile driver hammered into enemy's armor plate by an explosive charge or electrical power. Other Pilebunker weapons require a bullet to use its exceed force and eject the shell casing from said weapon.
pile of books:
A disorganized collection of books haphazardly placed on top of each other.  
These types of collections may also be composed of book stacks haphazardly placed atop of other book stacks.
pile of corpses: Huge number of dead bodies stacked together, forming a pile. Usually representing the aftermath of a battle, defeat, or mass murder.
pile of skulls: A large collection of skulls littering the floor or ground.
pill: A dose of solid medicine compressed into an easy to swallow size. Usually comes in blister packs or pill bottles.
pill bottle: A small bottle that pills are kept in. They feature wide mouth openings that are ideal for easy filling and dispensing of pills, capsules, vitamins, nutritional supplements and more.
pill earrings:
Earrings in the shape of a pill.
yumemi riamu from idolmaster cinderella girls is shown by default wearing these as seen in her official art - post #3408937.
pillar:
Any upright shaft or structure used as building support or as a stand-alone monument.
For pillars that are decorative, see column.
pillarboxed:
Reverse of letterboxed. An image resizing technique where vertical bars are displayed on both sides of a picture.
Pillarboxed does not count as a border but outside border may be used with it.
pillbox hat: A small hat with a flat crown, straight, upright sides, and no brim. Usually worn by women.
pillbug: A pill bug is the common name for any of the species of woodlice, terrestrial crustaceans, in the family Armadillidiidae. Their notable feature is their ability to curl up into a ball as a defensive behavior.  Other common names for them are roly polies, slaters, and doodle bugs.
pillory:
A device that restrains a person's torso and/or neck, and often the limbs as well. Often in the shape of two boards that lock together, with indentations for the victim's parts; for a representative example see post #4279357. Other designs exist as well, such as the curved design worn by Briar.
For boards that only restrain the limbs, use the tag stocks.
pillow: A pillow is used to sleep on and support the head/neck or other parts of the body while sleeping, lying down or sitting.
pillow fight:
On danbooru, this tag is applied to both "pillow fight" and "枕投げ (Makura-nage, pillow-throwing)"
The difference between the two is written in Wikipedia.
- Wikipedia:Pillow fight
- Wikipedia:Makura-Nage
pillow grab: grabbing one pillow or multiple pillows.
pillow hug:
Hugging a pillow with the arms and sometimes with the legs.
Note that the hug tag should not be used with pillow hug. hug applies only to hugging people, not objects.
pilot: A character who controls an airplane or similar craft, such as a space fighter.
pilot helmet:
A flight helmet is a special type of helmet primarily worn by pilots or (military) aircrew. It largely replaced the softer aviator hats in modern times. Flight helmets provide impact protection. They often feature a visor, headset or microphone for both communication and noise attenuation, mounting system for night vision device and head-mounted display, as well as compatibility with oxygen masks.

pin:
Sharp, slender objects used to fasten things together. Unlike sewing needles, which have a hole used for drawing thread, pins have a head like a nail (hardware), but smaller, round, and usually made from plastic. They are commonly used to secure fabrics for sewing or stick papers and photos to bulletin boards.

pinafore dress:
A pinafore dress or jumper (US English) is a sleeveless, collarless dress intended to be worn over a blouse, shirt or sweater.
Not to be confused with an apron, which has no back, distinctively.

pinching: A character squeezing a body part with their thumb and another finger, usually targeting the cheeks, nose, or stomach.
pinching sleeves:

pincushion: A small cushion used in sewing to poke countless needles into it for easy finding and safety.
pine tree: Trees in the genus Pinus in the family Pinaceae, they are evergreen trees meaning that their shrubs stay green even in winter.
pineapple: Edible fruit plant with a prickly outer skin and sweet, succulent yellow flesh.
pineapple slice: A cut portion of a pineapple.
pinecone: An organ on plants in the division Pinophyta (conifers) that contains the reproductive structures. They are divided between male and female cones, with the males producing pollen and the females producing seeds. The female cones are the more recognizable ones for their large woody appearance.

pipe in mouth: When a character has a smoking pipe in their mouth. They may or may not be smoking through it.

A penguin-like Pokémon which is one of the three default Pokemon the player chooses from in the Diamond and Pearl version of the franchise. Said to have a layer of down to protect them from extreme temperatures.
piranha plant: The Piranha Plant is a common plant enemy from the Mario series found in warp pipes or flower pots. Known as Pakkun Flower in Japan. A potted Piranha Plant appears as a playable fighter in the super smash bros. series, debuting in an Super Smash Bros. Ultimate update after the game's release.
pirate: A maritime bandit and outlaw whose their modus operandi is to raid and steal valuable goods from passerby ships, and oftentimes even capturing the ship for themselves. While piracy is prevalent around the world up until late 19th century, the most well-known pirates are the European and American pirates that operated around the Atlantic ocean between 15th to 18th century, of which the popular culture depiction of pirates in media is derived from.
pirate hat: A hat commonly seen with the skull and crossbones insignia on the front. May or may not be worn by pirates.
pitchfork:
A multi-pronged agricultural tool used to lift and pitch (throw) loose materials such as hay, grass, manure, or other such materials.
If the points are barbed and sharp use trident instead.
pitching: In baseball, pitching is the term referring to when the pitcher throws the ball at the opposing team's batter, aiming to strike the batter out by delivering the ball to the catcher (baseball) without letting the batter hit it. Typically this is done from atop the pitching mound.
pitfall: A type of trap wherein the unsuspecting victim falls into a hidden hole in the ground, often covered by leaves or some such.
pith helmet: A lightweight cloth-covered helmet made of cork or pith. Designed to shade the wearer's head and face from the sun, pith helmets were often worn by people of European origin in the tropics, but have also been used in other contexts. The gear is seen as typical explorer's headwear, and thus will be associated with those exploring wilderness (such as a safari) or going on expeditions.
pixel art:
An image drawn with a pixelated art style, typically with large individual pixels and a limited color palette.
This may be either intentional or as a restriction by the software used to create it. This is common in older GIF images as well as images meant to invoke game sprites.
Different from oekaki, which has less emphasis on being drawn with individual pixels.
pixel heart:
Pixelated heart symbol. Commonly associated with health bars in video games.

pixel-perfect duplicate:
A post that is completely identical to its parent, and was either uploaded afterwards or has no source while their parent does, and thus is inferior for Danbooru purposes.
Pixiv and Twitter posts are often identical, even if they have different filesizes. In 2019 Twitter stopped compressing as harshly as they used to, and in late 2020 Pixiv started losslessly recompressing their JPGs to strip metadata, so typically if there's only a few KBs of difference between two identical pictures from these two sites, it means they're the same exact image.
pixelated:
An image that contains elements of pixel art in contrast to adjacent, traditional line art, often to show an in-setting "digital" or "virtual" quality.  
For censored images that use an obscuring, pixelated blur, use mosaic censoring instead of this tag.

pixie cut:
The pixie cut is a type of women’s hairstyle that typically features very short hair cut at around the jaw's length or less, with descending volume from the top to bottom and little to no styling. The cut often includes sweeping bangs that are positioned close to the eyes, creating a flattering and accentuated facial profile. They are typically low-maintenance, require minimal styling, and are a practical option for those who lead active lifestyles.
The hairstyle is often commonly associated with tomboy characters.

pixiv id: Indicates that the artist's numerical pixiv ID is present somewhere on the image. Not to be confused with pixiv username, which is for the pixiv.me or stacc username chosen by the artist.

pixiv sample:
A image from Pixiv that is an image sample, rather than the original image.
Sample images contain "/img-master/" in the URL. Original images contain "/img-original/".
To avoid uploading a sample, paste a link to the image on the upload page, rather than downloading the image to your computer then uploading it.
This tag is automatically added by a bot to any Pixiv post that is detected to be a sample. Do not add this tag unless you can confirm a difference, or remove it unless the hashes match.
pixiv username: Indicates that the artist's pixiv username (pixiv.me or stacc) is present somewhere on the image. Not to be confused with pixiv id, which is for the numerical ID they are automatically assigned.
pixiv-tan: Pixiv-tan (ピクシブたん/pixivたん) is the mascot of the pixiv site.  Her design varies widely depending on the artist, but she usually has blue and white color palette and carries a pen tablet stylus.
pizza:
A round, baked flat bread that is typically covered in tomato sauce, cheese, and other toppings such as pepperoni and chili pepper according to preference or culture. Usually sliced into eight triangular pizza slices.
Modern pizza were originated from the Neapolitan pizza from Naples, italy.
There are also dessert pizzas that use chocolate, cream, candy and other sweet ingredients to create a treat resembling pizza.
pizza box: A flat box made for delivering pizza.

pizza hut: A popular American franchise of pizza restaurants. The franchise was founded on 1958 by the Carney brothers, Dan Carney and his late younger brother, Frank Carney.

placard: A sign with a stick held by a person to announce or voice something.

plague doctor mask: It is a mask featuring a long bird-like beak which was originally filled with aromatic herbs to protect its user from the bubonic plague during the Black Death pandemic that occur in Europe from 1346 to 1353.
plaid:

planet:
A large spherical astronomical object that typically orbits a star (sky). The tag should be used when at least one planet is seen from outer space or from the surface of another nearby planet. This includes real and fictional planets.  
Scientifically, there has always been some ambiguity as to what constitutes a planet, with some celestial bodies such as pluto (planet) and Ceres being considered at different times or by different people either as planets or as "dwarf planets".
planet hair ornament: A hair ornament shaped to resemble a planet, usually saturn (planet) since it's the most recognizable.
planetarian: planetarian ～ちいさなほしのゆめ～ ("Planetarian: Chiisana Hoshi no Yume", "Planetarian: The Dream of a Little Planet") is a science fiction visual novel developed by Key. Because it offers no choices or alternate endings, Visual Art's co.,ltd (the publisher) calls it a Kinetic Novel.
planetary ring: A ring of debris orbiting around a planet. The rings of saturn (planet) are the most famous example in our solar system.
plank: A flat, elongated and rectangular piece of wood, that is longer than it is wide.

plant girl:
A sub-set of monster girl involving plant-like feminine humanoids.  Many are overtly based upon concepts like the mandragora or alraune (which are the same thing in real life, just from different languages). 
Although many plant girls are called an alraune, alraune are variants who grow from large flower and plants.
If the creature is not feminine and sufficiently humanoid, use plant monster instead.
plant hair: Hair that is composed of plant matter, typically leaves.
plant monster:
A plant that moves, and can attack others.  Usually, this involves a plant-like form of tentacles using vines.  Other than this, or in conjunction with this, they may act like a pitcher plant, venus fly trap, or other predatory real-world plant, dragging characters into a deadly portion of the plant. 
Plant monsters probably shouldn't be humanoid. plant girl is used for (feminine) humanoid plant monsters, while plant boy is used for (masculine) humanoid plant monsters.
plant roots: See roots (hair) for a character's natural hair colour at the base of otherwise dyed hair.
plantar flexion: Movement of the foot in which the toes point downward, creating a straighter line from the lower leg to the toes of the foot. Commonly seen in dancers, e.g. ballerinas standing en pointe. Contrast dorsiflexion.
planted: Something visibly impaling the ground. For example, a sword planted in the ground.
planted sword: A sword whose pointed end is visibly impaling the ground.
planted umbrella: A closed umbrella that is planted (that is, with its tip visibly impaling the ground).
planter:
A planter box is a commonly rectangular container for decorative or edible plants. Also known as flower box or window box. It can stand alone or be attached onto objects like under the window or on railing.
h1. See also
- flower pot, for the commonly cylindrical counterpart. 
- garden
plants vs zombies:
Plants vs. Zombies is a tower defense and strategy video game developed and originally published by PopCap Games for Windows and OS X in May 2009.
In Plants vs. Zombies, players take the role of a homeowner in the midst of a zombie apocalypse.
plap: A Western Twitter meme. A sound effect for sex, especially rough sex or a mating press. Sometimes used as a verb ("to plap someone").
plastic bag: A bag that is made out of plastic. It can be colored and opaque so you can't see what's inside, or clear and see-through so you can see its contents. Seen with shopping bags and gift bags.
plastic memories:
A 2015 anime series by Doga Kôbô.
###### Plot
Giftias, androids possessing a humanlike appeareance and emotions, are available as companions, but they have an expiration date. Meet Tsukasa Mizugaki, a new employee at SAI Corp.
plastic wrap: A thin, transparent plastic film most often used to seal food containers, keeping food fresh for longer.
plate: A flat serving platter for many different types of non-liquid dishes. Usually but not always circular.
plate armor:
Armor that consists of solid, metal plates. 
- list of armor
plate stack: Several plates placed one on top of another.
platform footwear:
Footwear that features extra-thick soles­ of approximately around 2 inches or more. 
Platform soles may be found on shoes, sandals, boots and possibly other types of footwear.
platform heels: High heels which have elevated soles, of approximately around 2 inches or more from the ground.
platinum blonde hair: Use either blonde hair, grey hair or white hair.
platinum the trinity:
Platinum the Trinity is a playable character starting with blazblue: continuum shift II. Her weapon is muchourin.  
She is voiced by yuuki aoi.
play button:
The symbol for a video playback button. A right-pointing triangle: ▶️
For fake screenshots of videos, use fake play button or fake video instead. For the YouTube logo, use youtube logo instead. For the physical play button trophy given to YouTubers, use youtube creator award instead.

playboy bunny:
A character wearing a Playboy bunny outfit, also known as a "bunnysuit" or a "bunny girl".
A stereotypical Playboy bunny outfit consists of a black strapless leotard, fake rabbit ears, a fake rabbit tail, wrist cuffs, a detached collar with a bowtie, fishnet pantyhose or thighhighs, and high heels. Common variations include different outfit colors, or omission of some or all of the accessories.
A Playboy Bunny was originally a cocktail waitress who worked at a playboy Club. The first Playboy Bunny costume was introduced when Hugh Hefner opened his first Playboy Club in Chicago in 1960.
playboy bunny swimsuit: A playboy bunny outfit that features a swimsuit instead of a leotard.
player 2: Videogame character color swap, or a parody thereof. Originated in fighting games, so that if both players chose the same character, they could still be easily distinguished.
playerunknown's battlegrounds: A 2017 multiplayer battle royale shooter game developed and published by Krafton, and one of the earlier contributors to the battle royale craze alongside fortnite. The game is  free-to-play on all consoles as of January 2022, and retains a level of popularity among streamers and eSports players.
playground: An area designed for children's social and recreational activities, usually in outdoor settings such as parks or school grounds. Typical playground installations include benches, swings, slides, sandboxes, and jungle gyms.
playing: The act of engaging in recreational activities just for fun rather than for a practical purpose. Characters can play with an animal, a toy, or with each other.
playing bass guitar:
When a character is playing a bass guitar
Tag holding bass guitar instead if they aren't playing their instrument.
playing card:
A classical set of card consists 52 unique cards, categorized by suit and by rank. The four suits of the french deck are hearts (♥), spades (♠), clubs (♣), and diamonds (♦). The ranks include Ace, the numbers two through ten, and the face cards Jack, Queen, and King. A joker (playing card) or two may or not be present. These cards are used for various games, such as solitaire, poker, blackjack, etc. Often with gambling involved.
If characters are playing games with these cards, remember to tag the card faces accordingly.
playing card theme: Some object or art that has motifs of playing cards.
playing games:
A person playing any type of game.
This tag is not exclusively for video games and can be used for other types of games, such as board games, lawn games, dice games, carnival games, and hand games. This does not include sports.
playing guitar: When a character is playing a guitar. Use holding guitar instead if they are just holding it.
playing instrument: When a character is shown playing a musical instrument in the image.
playing piano: The act of playing a piano.
playing sports: A sport being played by someone.
playing with hair:
A character playing with either their own hair or another's hair.
This is generally frivolous, playful, or meaningless behavior. For example they might be simply twirling or flipping a lock of hair, making a "hair mustache", or "eating", ruffling, kissing or smelling their or another's hair.
If they are meaningfully working with their or another's hair for a concrete goal, instead use one of the following tags as appropriate:
- adjusting hair
- holding own hair
- tying hair
- brushing hair
- drying hair
- bunching hair
- cutting hair
- braiding hair
- washing hair
- brushing hair
playstation 1: The retronym of the original PlayStation, initially called (codename) the PlayStation X.
playstation 2:
The PlayStation 2 (officially abbreviated PS2) is a video game home console manufactured by sony Computer Entertainment and the successor to the playstation 1 as part of the PlayStation series. 
It was first released on March 4, 2000, in japan, and then was released on October 26, 2000 in North America, and November 24, 2000 in Europe.
The second in Sony's line of PlayStation consoles, developed for the sixth generation market to compete against Microsoft's xbox (original), Nintendo gamecube and sega dreamcast.
playstation 3:
The PlayStation 3 (プレイステーション3, Pureisutēshon Surī?, officially abbreviated as "PS3") is the third home video game console produced by sony Computer Entertainment and the successor to the playstation 2 as part of the PlayStation series. 
The PlayStation 3 competes with microsoft's xbox 360 and nintendo's wii as part of the seventh generation of video game consoles. Its big, heavy and low capacity first model was first released on November 11, 2006, in Japan, with international markets following shortly thereafter. A newer and more refined slim model with higher capacity was released in 2009.
playstation 4: The PlayStation 4 (officially abbreviated as "PS4") is the fourth home video game console produced by sony Computer Entertainment and the successor to the playstation 3 as part of the PlayStation series.
playstation 5: The PlayStation 5 (officially abbreviated as "PS5") is the fifth home video game console produced by sony Computer Entertainment. Successor to the playstation 4 as part of the PlayStation series.
playstation controller:
A game controller design released with the playstation 1 game console in 1994.
Like the super famicom/super nintendo's controller, which it was based on, the face of the controller features a d-pad on the left, four action buttons on the right, and initially two buttons in the middle (originally a Start and  Select button). It also features two sets of shoulder buttons, unlike the SNES controllers single set, and improved the ability to use those buttons by adding hand grips.
playstation logo:
The logo for the Playstation line of consoles, consisting of red P over a yellow, green, and blue S lying behind it.
- !asset #21932300
playstation portable:
The PlayStation Portable (officially abbreviated PSP) is a handheld game console manufactured and marketed by sony. 
The system was released in Japan on December 12, 2004, in North America on March 24, 2005 and in Europe and Australia on September 1, 2005.
The PlayStation Portable is the only handheld video game console to use an optical disc format, Universal Media Disc (UMD), as its primary storage medium.
playstation vita:
The PlayStation Vita (プレイステーション・ヴィータ, officially abbreviated PS Vita) is a handheld game console manufactured and marketed by Sony Computer Entertainment. 
It is the successor to the playstation portable as part of the PlayStation series. 
The PS Vita was released in Japan and parts of Asia on December 17, 2011, in Europe, North America, South America and Singapore on February 22, 2012 and in Australia on February 23, 2012. 
It primarily competes with the nintendo 3ds as part of the eighth generation of gaming.
pleated dress: A dress with vertical folds of fabric.
pleated shirt:
A shirt with multiple pleats. Do not use this tag for shirt darts, or simple back pleats near the shoulders.
Vertical columns of pleats beside the placket are predominantly found in white dress shirts. The kobeya uniform and some tuxedos feature this.
Not to be confused with ribbed shirt.
pleated skirt: A skirt with vertical folds of fabric.
plectrum: A small flat tool used to pick or strum any string instrument, such as guitars and harps. Also called a pick.
pleinair: A mascot character of harada takehito. Pleinair is a small girl with a stuffed rabbit named Usagi and a pet shark named Sammy. She is somewhat abusive of them, even using Usagi as a emergency food supply and sometimes tearing an ear off.
pliers: A tool used for gripping something round like a pipe or rod. Some are used for twisting or cutting wires.
plugsuit: A distinct kind of mecha pilot suit worn by the mecha pilots in neon genesis evangelion.
plum blossom print: Clothing or an object that has at least one plum blossom printed on it.
plum blossoms:
The blossoms of plum trees, especially of the genus Prunus mume. The petals are white, pink or red, and bloom in early spring. 
The aesthetic of the plum blossom has always been of major importance across East Asia, and while viewing them was initially a popular practice in Japan beginning in the Nara period, it was overshadowed by the popularity of cherry blossoms during the Heian period. This preference was only reinforced by subsequent generations of intellectuals, who in effect argued the sakura to be more quintessentially Japanese.
plume: An upright ornament made of feathers or horsehair adorning hats and helmets. A part of military uniforms since ancient times, nowadays used by marching bands as well.
plumeria:
A genus of flowering plants in the family Apocynaceae. Most species are deciduous shrubs or small trees that grow in tropical regions. One of the most commonly depicted species is Plumeria rubra, also known as frangipani.
Plumeria flowers are five-petaled with finely defined, overlapping petals. The petal tips are usually rounded. Flowers can be of various colors, but most are multicolored.
In anime art, it is frequently used in beach scenes as a hair ornament or part of a flower necklace.
plump:
Slightly chubby, but not enough to be fat. A saying that goes around for plump is "Fat in all the right places".
The Japanese tags above are Pixiv's equivalent of the word, but be aware that not all Pixiv-centric uses of those tags fit Danbooru's definition. As with all other size-specific tags, observe the body and see if the tag actually needs to be used before adding it; make sure that the body is not simply “curvy” and that it’s not “fat”, either. 
Plump is mutually exclusive with fat and obese.
plunging neckline:
A sharp, v-shaped neckline that plunges through the cleavage down to the stomach.
This should not be used for garments that are closed above the breasts (though they may have laces to hold themselves together), and should only be used for unzipped or unbuttoned garments if they are consistently worn in this manner by an established character.
plus sign: Images that in some way feature a "+" symbol.
plushmallow: An original character belonging to commissioner SquishyGuy/Maximum Potato. A green-eyed fox girl with brown hair and seven fluffy tails.
plusle:

Plusle is a cream-colored, bipedal Pokémon with red markings. It resembles pikachu a lot.

pocari sweat: A brand of soda / sports drink popular in Japan and manufactured by Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd. Recognizable by its logo of a white swirl in a blue background.
pocket:
A small bag or pouch sewn into a piece of clothing, meant to hold small items.
pants, shorts, jackets, coats, and button-down shirts are a few common types of clothing that usually contain pockets. Pockets are more common in men's fashion than in women's.
pocket square: A folded piece of cloth worn in the breast pocket of a formal suit coat.
pocket watch:
A type of handheld clock kept in one's pocket instead of being worn on one's wrist.
It has a similar design to its predecessor, the pendant watch, due to these similarities this tag should be used for ALL depictions not fastened around the neck.
pocky:
A long, thin, chocolate-covered cookie popular in Japan similar to a biscotti. There are other Pocky flavors that are shipped throughout the world. In Europe it is available under the name Mikado.
Thanks to its immense popularity amongst the Japanese and elsewhere, it has been featured in a number of anime, such as Please! Teacher, Please! Twins, X/1999, etc. Due to copyright issues, it is nearly always mentioned under a different name, usually a mangled pronunciation, misspelling, or homonym, such as Pooky, Pochy, Rocky, et. al.
pocky day: Posts referencing 11/11, known as pocky Day, or Pocky & Pretz Day (pepero Day in South Korea).
pocky in mouth: When a character has pocky in their mouth.
pocky kiss: When two people bite a piece of pocky at both ends and, as they eat more of the pocky, grow closer to each other until there's no pocky more left and they kiss.
podium:
A small platform on which a person stands to be seen by an audience. Often used to present medals to the top three competitors in sporting events.
See lectern for the type of podium a person stands behind when giving a speech or lecture.
poem: A form of literary art in which language is used for its aesthetic and evocative qualities in addition to, or in lieu of, its apparent meaning.
poi:
yuudachi (kancolle) from kantai collection's catchphrase-poi.
To be used only when there is particular emphasis on the phrase "poi" (when used standalone, "poi" is in romaji, a pun, etc...) and the use is related in some way to Yuudachi, not just as a comparative particle of sorts-poi.
Not to be confused with the festival goldfish scoop, the tethered weights (sometimes lit) used in the eponymous performance art, the polynesian staple food, a certain cat-eared maid from a certain mobile game or even the 3d adventure platformer game-poi.
poinsettia: Tropical American flowering plant with flashy leaves of scarlet (less often orange, pale green, cream, pink, white or marbled) surrounding the actual flowers, which are small and yellow. Often associated with christmas.
pointed crown: A crown with one or more points (often in the form of a fleur-de-lis) set along its rim. The crown can either be cylindrical in shape, or designed like a tiara.
pointed footwear: Any type of footwear that has a distinct point and/or curve at the tip.
pointer:
A stick (wood, plastic, or metal) used by instructors such as teachers and military persons. Not to be confused with laser pointer.
See arrow (symbol) for arrows pointing to things. See cursor for mouse pointers.
pointing: The act of directing attention to something, usually by using one's index finger. Don't confuse with index finger raised.
pointing at another: Someone is pointing at someone else.
pointing at self: Someone is pointing at himself or herself.
pointing at viewer:
Someone is pointing at the viewer.
Sometimes they are also looking at viewer.
If it's a weapon being pointed at the viewer, as in pointing sword or aiming, use aiming at viewer instead.
pointing down: A character is pointing at least one finger downwards, indicating for the viewer to glance down.
pointing forward:
When a character is pointing towards their front, based on their own perspective.

pointing sword: When a sword is directed toward a person or thing.
pointing to the side: The act of pointing, usually with the index finger, to the side, usually to the left, or to the right.
pointing up: The act of pointing, usually with the index finger, in the direction of the sky.

pointless condom:
A condom (new or used), a condom wrapper, or some other evidence of a condom is present, but someone has still ejaculated inside a girl or otherwise engaged in behaviour that completely defeats the purpose and thus renders the condom pointless. e.g. post #23768.
Note that this tag is for human carelessness or recklessness, not condoms that have broken accidentally. The tags can overlap when someone sabotages a condom, e.g. post #590912.
pointy breasts: breasts that point and jut forward, with a slight conical/tapered shape. Can either be perky or saggy.
pointy ears: Any ear ending in a point. Usually elf or vulcan-like, but can also refer to animal-like ears.
pointy footwear:
Footwear that have the toe portion sticking out into a distinct point. May or may not have a curl at the end.
Not to be confused with spiked shoes, although both tags may apply in some cases.
pointy hair:
A hairstyle with at least two cone-shaped points that stick out and up, sometimes resembling animal ears. Musashi and toyosatomimi no miko's hairstyles are perfect examples.
Not to be confused with spiked hair, where most of the character's hair, if not the entire hairstyle, consists of sharp spikes; nor hair flaps, where the ear-like flaps come from the sides, and are either flat or down.

poison:

poison ivy:
Poison Ivy (real name: Pamela Lilian Isley) is a Batman supervillain with plant powers. Poison Ivy first appeared in Batman #181 (June 1966) and is created by the late Robert Kanigher and the late Shelly Moldoff.

poke ball:
Japanese name: モンスターボール (Monster Ball)
You know, Poké Balls!
P-O-K-accent-E Balls!
Known as a Monster Ball in Japan, a spherical capsule used to capture and store Pokémon (Pocket Monsters). The most common and recognized Poké Ball is the titular basica variant, which has two colored halves: red on top and white on bottom.
It is one of the central symbols of the franchise.
Normally, captured Pokémon would be stored inside a "pocket dimension" within the ball, though some refuses to went inside the Poké Balls. Ash's pikachu is a notable example.
poke ball print: Clothing or an object with printings of the Poké Ball from the Pokémon franchise.
poke ball symbol: Depictions of a poke ball that don't fall under poke ball print, a poke ball hair ornament or an actual poke ball. For example, this tag would apply to the Poke Ball symbol appearing on some food, e.g. post #6874182.
poke ball theme: Something that is not a Poké Ball, but either ressembles one or is decorated with drawings of one or more Poké Balls.
pokedex: An electronic encyclopedia with information about species of Pokémon.

pokemon battle: A parody of the battle screen of the pokemon (game) games.

pokemon egg:

pokemon hgss: The Generation IV Pokémon remakes (HeartGold and SoulSilver) of the Generation II titles Gold, Silver, and Crystal.
pokemon horizons: The eighth series of the Pokémon anime. It succeeds Pokémon Journeys: The Series. It premiered on April 14, 2023 in Japan with a one-hour special, and on March 7, 2024 in the United States.
pokemon journeys:
A Pokémon anime season announced in 2019 and debuting the same year in Japan.

pokemon legends: arceus: A prequel to Pokémon Diamond and Pearl set in Sinnoh in an era when it was named Hisui. Released for the nintendo switch.

pokemon ranger:
Pokémon Ranger is a series of Pokémon games in which Rangers temporarily control wild Pokémon.

resolution mismatch:
When the image resolution on Danbooru differs from the image resolution at the source. The following two tags can be used with this tag.
- source smaller:
  - One or both dimensions must be larger than the source.
  - heightsource <= heightdanbooru and widthsource <= widthdanbooru
- source larger:
  - One or both dimensions must be smaller than the source.
  - heightsource >= heightdanbooru and widthsource >= widthdanbooru
- Neither:
  - One dimension is larger than the source, and the other dimension is smaller than the source.

rifle:
A long firearm designed to be fired from the shoulder, with a barrel that has a helical pattern of grooves ("rifling") cut into the barrel walls. The rifling causes the speeding bullet to spin, giving it more stability and penetrating power.

rifle cartridge:

A decent rule of thumb is that if the cartridge's length is more than 3.5 times the diameter of the case, it lacks a distinct rim, usually has bottlenecked case and the bullet diameter is approximately a half inch or less, then it is most likely a rifle cartridge regardless of specific caliber.

roman empire:
The Roman Empire (Latin: Imperium Rōmānum) was the post-Republican period of ancient Rome. 
As a polity, it included large territorial holdings around the Mediterranean Sea in Europe, North Africa, and Western Asia, ruled by emperors. 
From the accession of Caesar Augustus as the first Roman emperor to the military anarchy of the 3rd century, it was a principate with Italy as the metropole of its provinces and the city of Rome as its sole capital. 
Later, the Empire was ruled by multiple emperors who shared control over the Western Roman Empire and the Eastern Roman Empire.
roman numeral:
Refers to the ancient Roman way of writing numbers. Likely because of the elegant style, it is still usually recognized and understood by everyday people (at least from 1 to 10), as well as frequently used on clocks.
- 1 = I
- 2 = II
- 3 = III
- 4 = IV (one below 5)
- 5 = V
- 6 = VI (one above 5)
- 7 = VII (two above 5)
- 8 = VIII
- 9 = IX
- 10 = X (can be remembered by how 2 V's form an X; 5*2=10)
- 11 = XI
- 12 = XII
- 50 = L
- 100 = C
- 500 = D
- 1000 = M

It evolves from scyther when traded holding a metal coat and with the Scizorite it can mega evolve into mega scizor.

Next Pokémon: shuckle
scolding: When one character is angrily reprimanding another (or the viewer). Often accompanied by pointing and finger wagging.
scolipede:
Pokémon #545 in the National PokéDex, a dual type Bug/Poison Pokémon.
Scolipede is notable for its huge segmented body, large twin horns on its rear and head, gray, pink, and purple body colors, and its intimidating yellow eyes.
scone: A small unsweetened or lightly sweetened biscuit-like cake made from flour, fat, and milk and sometimes having added fruit.
scooby-doo: A long-running supernatural/comedy cartoon series from hanna-barbera/cartoon network, originally airing in the 1970s. In Japan, it was briefly known as 'Yowamushi Kuruppaa' (Cowardly Crooper/Krupper) before switching to the international name.
scoop neck: A type of neckline that is wide and deeply rounded. A scoop neck top exposes most of the upper chest, but doesn't expose the shoulders and doesn't dip below the breasts.
scooter:
A small two-wheeled motor vehicle with a step-through frame and a platform for the operator's feet. A popular example is the vespa.
For non-motorized scooters, use kick scooter instead.
scope:
An optical magnification device mounted on a gun (typically a rifle of some type) used to improve a shooter's accuracy or allow him to see farther. 
Electronic scopes, which are bulkier in design, give the option to see in different filters, such as night or thermal-vision.
scopedog:
ATM-09 Scopedog
mecha from the 80s anime series Armored Trooper Votoms. While simplistic, it possesses many variants with added armament and performance.
scorbunny:
Pokémon #813 in the National Pokédex, a Fire type Pokémon introduced in Generation VIII.
Along with grookey and sobble, Scorbunny is one of three starter Pokémon available at the beginning of Pokémon Sword and Shield.
It evolves into raboot, which evolves into cinderace.
scoreboard: A large board seen at sports stadiums that can display the score of a game to a huge crowd of people.
scorpion:
Scorpions are predatory arachnids of the order Scorpiones. 
They have eight legs and are easily recognized by the pair of grasping pedipalps and the narrow, segmented scorpion tail, often carried in a characteristic forward curve over the back, ending with a venomous stinger.
scorpion girl:
A type of arthropod girl that has characteristcs of a scorpion, such as the tail with venomous stinger. Her hair can also resemble scorpion body legs, such as scorpion tsuchida's hairstyle. She may or may not have a scorpion body, such as post #629342.
Should also be tagged with monster girl when the girl is sufficiently monstrous.
scott pilgrim: Protagonist of the scott pilgrim (series) series. A nerdy guy in his early 20s who is generally cheerful and friendly towards other characters. Lives with his gay college friend Wallace and mostly mooches off him, though Wallace doesn't seem to mind. Plays in a band called Sex Bomb-omb.
scott pilgrim takes off: Scott Pilgrim Takes Off is an animated adaptation of the scott pilgrim (series) comic book series by Bryan Lee O'Malley, the second after Titmouse's Scott Pilgrim vs. the Animation in 2010. The anime was produced by science saru and released on Netflix in November 2023.
scout movement:
A voluntary non-political movement for young people, consisting of three major age groups: the cub scouts between 5 to 12, the boy scouts, usually between 10 to 18, and the Rover Scouts for those over. Parallel groups would also be created for girls, the most noteworthy being the parallel to the Boy Scouts, the girl scouts, for those between 10 and 14.
The Scout Association of Japan also includes Beaver Scouts, for those aged between 6 and 8, and Venture Scouts, for those aged 14 and 19.
scouter:
A small, single-lens eyepiece originated from dragon ball z that is worn wrapped around the side of the head. The device typically sports a heads-up display that provides its wearer with statistics or information on their surroundings, similar to a head-mounted display. Its most well-known feature, however, is its ability to calculate the power level of any living being, and displayed the result as a number.
Not to be confused with the monocle, another single-lens eyepiece used expressly for correcting vision like glasses.
scowl: A look of displeasure, sullenness, or discontent in an angry kind of way. A kind of "I-really-don't-like-this" kind of look.
scp foundation:
To secure, contain and protect.
A series of open-source fictional works dealing with the paranormal and especially its capture and containment.
scrafty:
Pokémon #560 in the National PokéDex, a Fighting/Dark dual type Pokémon.
Scrafty is a bipedal lizard-like Pokémon. It has oval, wide-set eyes with small pupils and gray eyelids, as well as small nostrils and a wide mouth with bared teeth.
scraggy:
Pokémon #559 in the National PokéDex, a dual type Fighting/Dark Pokémon.
Scraggy is a bipedal, lizard-like Pokémon. Its oval eyes are set to the sides of its head, and its teeth appear to be constantly exposed. There is a small red scale on its yellow head.
scrape: A minor injury where the outer layer of skin is rubbed off, as by fall on hard ground.
scratches:
A shallow cut on a surface, commonly by accident or wear. Also called solutions of continuity. Can be seen on armor and weapons of hardened or old warriors.
Minor wounds qualify too.
scratching: The act of using the fingers to lightly claw at a surface of skin, usually to get rid of an itch. The marks left behind are scratches.
scratching cheek: A character scratching their own cheek with one finger, usually out of embarrassment, shyness, and/or uncertainty.
screaming: Someone is screaming, whether from sheer terror, or the orgasmic throes of sex. Always add open mouth along with this tag.
screen:
A variety of forms or formats of information display, such as viewing surfaces or areas for movies or motion pictures, slide presentations, information viewing areas for electronic device display output, various areas of video games, etc. divided into separate screens, or visual data or images displayed on computer screens.
Large screens are often used for screen zoom projections on stage performances.
H4. See also
- concert
- display
- screen light
- stage
- monitor
screen light: A monitor or other electronic screen that is also a light source, illuminating whatever or whoever it faces.
screen zoom: Projections on large background screens during stage performances to provide a better view for back row audiences. Has a similar effect to zoom layer.
screenshot:
A screenshot taken from something other than an anime or a game.
If the screenshot is from an anime, use anime screenshot. If the screenshot is from a game, use game screenshot. If it is only the background of an image, use game screenshot background. If it's inset in the image, use game screenshot inset.
screenshot background:
Artwork that is drawn over a screenshot of any kind, including webpage screencaps.
If the screenshot only takes up a small portion of the image, use screenshot inset instead.
screenshot inset: A screenshot that is contained as a smaller inset within an image.
screenshot redraw: When an artist redraws a real screenshot.
screentones: Screentone is a technique for applying textures and shades to drawings, used as an alternative to hatching (texture). In the conventional process, patterns are transferred to paper from preprinted sheets, but the technique is also simulated in computer graphics, notably in Flipnote Studio and Macpaint.
screw: A fastener. May be similar in appearance to a bolt (hardware). Screwed in place either by hand or with a screwdriver. Some have a tapered end; but others, such as computer screws, do not.
screw hair ornament: A hair ornament or hairpin shaped like a screw.
screw in head: A screw or bolt (hardware) that goes through (or appears to go through) a character's head. Commonly seen on depictions of frankenstein's monster.
screwdriver:
A tool with a flattened, cross-shaped, or star-shaped tip that fits into the head of a screw to turn it.
Has nothing to do with the cocktail.
scribble: A messy and largely shapeless stroke of lines. Typically used to represent character's annoyance over something.
scribble censor:
A type of censorship that typically consists of irregular meandering lines drawn quickly and without precise control.
Frequently mistagged as bar censor. While bar censor is not always employing perfect rectangles, if it has two or more sharp turns, it can be considered scribble censor.
script: A manuscript with lines of dialogue and stage directions for a motion picture, theatrical play, television program or radio show.
scroll: A long, often rolled up piece of paper typically depicted with writing on it.
scrunchie:
A fabric-covered elastic tie. Usually worn in the hair, but may also be worn on the wrist, arm or ankle as a fashion accessory.
Not to be confused with wrist cuffs or arm garters.
scryed:
Stylized s-CRY-ed.
A 2001 shounen anime by Sunrise. Also a manga written by Kuroda Yousuke and illustrated by Toda Yasunari and light novel by Hyoudou Kazuho with illustrations by hirai hisashi.
scuba: Scuba is an acronym for self contained underwater breathing apparatus.
sculpture: A three dimensional work of art created from plastic (malleable materials such as clay) or hard materials (such as stone or metals) through processes such as carving, modeling, casting, or welding.
scylla:
A type of monster girl resembling a sea octopus, most commonly taking the form in Japanese works of a human upper torso and tentacles for legs.  
Named after a Greek mythological monster that has had many varying descriptions over the centuries.  One later mythological version of the scylla was more or less a mermaid whose serpentine-like lower half was surrounded by snapping dog heads. For that character, use scylla (mythology) instead.
Other names associated with octopus girls are Cecaelia and Dagon.
scythe:
A traditional long handled agricultural tool used to harvest whole plants, such as hemp or wheat. Commonly depicted as a weapon of choice used by the grim reaper as a tool to reap souls, or by other mythological beings. 
Although often seen in fantasy and anime as a weapon, it is only tangentially connected to the "war scythe", which is a polearm having more in common with a glaive (polearm), fauchard or naginata than with the original tool.
scyther:
Pokémon #123 in the National Pokédex.
Evolves into scizor.
Japanese name: Strike
Prior Pokémon: mr. mime
Next Pokémon: jynx
sdf-1:
A legendary, massive, fictional variable spacecraft from the macross science fiction anime series. 
The U.N. Spacy SDF-1 (Super Dimensional Fortress One) "Macross" is the titular space fortress (and mecha) from the anime choujikuu yousai macross released in the 80s.

sea slug: A common name for several marine invertebrates that differ in level of similarity to terrestrial slugs.
sea slug girl: A girl with sea slug traits.
sea turtle: An almost entirely aquatic strain of turtles that live in the sea. Their front legs are adapted for life in the water, taking the form of large flippers.
sea urchin:
Sea urchins are spiny, globular echinoderm animals from the class Echinoidea that live at all ocean depths.
Also served as a delicacy known as "uni."
seagull: Gulls or "seagulls" are sea birds in the family Laridae other than terns, noddies and skimmers.
seahorse: A small marine fish with head and neck reminiscent of a horse and is characterized by segmented bone armor, upright posture, and a curled prehensile tail.
seaking:

seal impression:
The impression made after a seal is pressed in ink and then onto the image. Historically, seals have taken the place of signatures all across East Asia. The impression usually is rectangular or square, with the characters of the author's name in red ink.
For some examples, see "Wikipedia":[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seal(EastAsia)] and "Wikicommons":[https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Chinesesealimprints].
seamed legwear:
Any sort of stockings, pantyhose, thighhighs, bodysuit, or other legwear featuring a vertical seam (not vertical stripes) running up the legs.
This tag encompasses all types of seamed legwear, including back-seamed, front-seamed, and side-seamed. Please use one of these more specific tags when tagging, not just seamed legwear.
seams: Ambiguous tag for seams/visible stitching on clothing and the lines formed where 2 mechanical parts join
seaplane: A airplane designed to land or takeoff from water. They generally come in two forms: Flying boats that utilize a boat-shaped hull, and floatplanes that rely on external pontoons.
seaplane tender princess:
One of the enemy Abyssal ships from kantai collection, introduced in the Summer 2015 Event.
She has very long black hair and glowing red eyes. Her clothing is all gothic lolita fashion—a torn, lacy black dress, a big black hair bow, and a collar with a long chain attached to it.
seaport princess:
Seaport Princess is an enemy found in kantai collection. She was the boss of the third event map during the Spring 2014 event.
She is depicted with very long white hair, red eyes, large clawed hands, a magnificent bust and a single horn, and wears a short ribbed dress.
seaport summer princess:
kantai collection enemy abyssal ship introduced in the Summer 2016 Event. Her voice actress is unknown. She is based on Singapore.
She has long white hair covering the left side of her face and blue eyes. Wears a white dress and a white sun hat with a large black flower on it.
seaport water oni:
Seaport Water Oni is an enemy abyssal ship in kantai collection. She appeared as part of the Spring 2015 Event.
She is essentially an evolved seaport princess visually. She has gargantuan forearms with monstrous clawed hands and her hair is an absurd length.
searching: The act of looking around for something or someone.
searchlight:
An extremely bright outdoor spotlight. Originally used to search for enemy aircraft or escaped detainees at night, hence the name. They were later used for decorative purposes.
This tag can also be applied to posts where character are being "caught" by the searchlight outside of performative purposes. For when characters are being highlighted while performing, use spotlight instead.
seashell: Generic term for the empty shells of various marine molluscs, often adapted for decorative use. Common seashells on Danbooru include the shells of scallops, conchs, clams, and cowries.
season connection: A crossover or parody image wherein the characters present are all from different series, but airing within the same television season.
seatbelt: A belt found in motor vehicles used to keep passengers safe during their journey.
seaweed: A general term for macroscopic multi-cell marine algae. They generally appear like non-arboreal terrestrial plants. They are used for a variety of uses, including food, medicine, and fertilization.
sebastian michaelis:
Titular character of kuroshitsuji.
The current human guise of a demon contracted to ciel phantomhive, acting as his hyper-competent butler. After Ciel finds and gets revenge on the people who murdered his parents, their contract is complete and Sebastian will eat his soul.
sebastian piyodore: A chick who is lize helesta's butler and mascot, nicknamed "Sebas".
second-party source:
A post that, rather than sourced directly from the artist, is sourced to someone who posted it on the artist's behalf.
Examples include:
- official arts posted by a company in which the original artist is affliated with or by a copyright's official social media.
- commissions posted to the commissioner's own account instead of to the artist's account.
  - If a commission is uploaded to Danbooru by the commissioner themselves, use commissioner upload instead.
- artist collaborations between artists posting on each other's accounts.
- gift art posted by the recipient.
security camera: A camera installed in a location to constantly monitor activities. This can help curb petty crimes such as trespassing, theft, shoplifting and leaving without paying, and can also be used as evidence for major crimes.
seductive smile: A sultry expression with usually half-lidded eyes and a smile. Similar to naughty face, but the look is more inviting and assertive, instead of teasing and mischievous. Also known as "bedroom eyes."
see-through bikini: A bikini made with some amount of transparent fabric. It may be transparent only when wet.
see-through body:
When objects behind (and sometimes simultaneously inside) a character can be seen through a character's skin and/or clothes, either partially or wholly. This might include a visible skeleton and/or organs.
See-through bodies might be due to character design - such as for ghost characters, slime girls/boys, etc - or because a character is fading away.
If a character has an entirely different image embedded in their skin/clothes, see double exposure.
see-through bodysuit:
A bodysuit that is either translucent or completely see-through, and is usually shiny to indicate that it's being worn.
Note that it is easy to confuse a character's nude skin for a sheer bodysuit, so exercise good judgment when using this tag.
This tag is for bodysuits made of thick, transparent material. For thin, sheer bodysuits, see bodystocking.
see-through cape: A cape that is see-through, whether because it's made of sheer material or is fully transparent.
see-through cleavage: When a piece of clothing that otherwise would cover the character's cleavage has a portion of see-through material that allows to see it.
see-through coat: A coat that is see-through, whether because it's made of sheer material or is fully transparent.
see-through curtains: Very thin curtains that allows to easily see object or person behind them
see-through dress: If some dress on picture appears to be see-through.
see-through dress layer:
When a layered dress has an additional see-through layer of fabric integrated covering both top and bottom halves.
If the see-through layer covers only the bottom half like  a skirt, it's see-through skirt layer instead.
see-through gloves: A pair of gloves that are see-through.
see-through headwear:
Headwear that appears to be translucent or transparent, regardless of specific colour.
h1. See also
- tag group:headwear
see-through jacket: A jacket that can be seen through.
see-through legwear: Legwear that is very transparent or diaphanous, having little to no color of its own other than the color of the wearers leg.
see-through leotard: A leotard that is see-through enough to see the wearer's skin.
see-through shawl: A shawl that is made of transparent material.
see-through shirt: A shirt that is see-through, whether because it's made of sheer material or is fully transparent.
see-through silhouette:
When the silhouette of a person's body is visible through a translucent object, usually clothing or curtains. Not necessarily see-through clothes, since there can be just enough light to pierce the fabric.
See invisible man for see-through characters.
see-through skirt: A skirt that is see-through, whether because it's made of sheer material or is fully transparent.
see-through skirt layer:
When a layered skirt or the bottom half of a layered dress has an additional see-through layer of fabric integrated.
If the see-through layer covers both the top half and the bottom half like a dress, it's see-through dress layer instead.
see-through sleeves: A pair of sleeves that can be seen through. The sleeves have to either be detached, or different from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).
see-through sports bra: A sports bra that is see-through, whether because it's made of sheer material or is fully transparent, or even wet.
see-through veil: A veil that one is able to see through. Don't use this tag for bridal veils.
seed:
The fetal form of a plant.  Often planted into soil to grow new plants, or eaten as a form of nutrition.
This tag is often used on Danbooru when someone is eating a seed like a hamster.
seele vollerei:
A honkai (series) character. Voiced by nakahara mai.
She has blue eyes and two-tone hair (black and blue). The stigma on her chest has its own twisted alter ego who is sometimes called "Veliona" in the localization. When "she" overtakes, Seele's overall theme is changed from blue to red.
seeu:
SeeU is a Korean vocaloid developed and distributed by SBS A&T, and was released for the VOCALOID3 engine.
She was developed to be bilingual, having Japanese capabilities.
Her appearance was designed by kkuem. She has long light blond hair, blue eyes, and a cat lip.
sefirot:
The Tree of Life (Also known as the Sephirot) are the ten attributes through which God reveals himself in jewish Kabbalah. Made popular by neon genesis evangelion.
Not to be confused with sephiroth.
sega: Sega Corporation (株式会社セガ Kabushiki gaisha Sega), pronounced /ˈseɪɡə/ (US/Canada/UK/New Zealand/Australia) and usually styled as SEGA, is a Japanese multinational video game developer, publisher and hardware development company headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, with various offices around the world.
sega dreamcast:
sega's final video game home console produced for the sixth-generation market of consoles. It was released in November 1998 in Japan and later in September 1999 in other territories. 
Sega ultimately had to withdraw from the console market when it couldn't compete against sony's playstation 2 and nintendo's gamecube, instead sticking to producing games. The company discontinued the Dreamcast in North America early in March 2001, but support for the system continued in Europe and Oceania until the end of 2002.
segawa onpu:
ojamajo doremi character.
A child idol with purple eyes who wears her purple hair in a side ponytail or a one side up.
Usually wears a white t-shirt with short sleeves under a purple pinafore dress with purple shorts underneath and yellow sneakers.
segment display:
An electronic display that displays numbers or letters using a pattern of line segments that can be turned on or off.
The most common type has seven segments, but eight-, nine-, fourteen-, and sixteen-segment displays also exist.
segmented comic:
Some comics have their individual panels posted as separate images (bordered or otherwise), segmenting what otherwise would've been one whole comic page. This tag is for those comics, which have become increasingly common since the 2010s on social media, where they appear together as one whole.
Do not tag these with 1koma, as the panels are not self-contained, but part of a greater whole, nor with splash page, as splash pages are not segmented.
segway: A motorized two-wheeled transporter which moves depending on the direction of the lean of the operator.
seigaiha: A traditional Japanese pattern of stylized waves.

seiken densetsu:
An RPG series produced and published by square enix (formerly as Squaresoft).
Also known as the Mana series. The franchise consists of a mainline series, a World of Mana subseries, plus several spinoffs, remakes, and manga adaptations.
seiken densetsu 2:
Second game in the seiken densetsu RPG series, originally for the super famicom. Known as Secret of Mana in English regions.
Secret of Mana features 3 playable characters. You control one and the computer (or other players) control the other two.
seiken densetsu 3:

seiken gakuin no maken tsukai: A light novel series written by "Yuu Shimizu":[https://twitter.com/shimizuMFJ] and illustrated by toosaka asagi. A manga adaptation illustrated by keigen hichou has been serialized in Kadokawa Shoten's shōnen manga magazine Monthly Shōnen Ace since November 2019 and an anime television series adapta…
seiken no blacksmith:

A light novel series by Miura Isao, with illustrations by luna (reclaimed land). Also a 2009 anime and manga, with illustrations by yamada koutarou.

seiou gakuen school uniform: The school uniform worn by students at the all girls Seiou Gakuen ('Seiou Academy') in gakuen utopia manabi straight!.
seiren academy school uniform: A school uniform worn by the high school students of Seiren Academy in the series Roshidere.
seisenshi dunbine: Seisenshi Dunbine (Sacred Warrior Dunbine), also known as Aura Battler Dunbine, is a mecha anime television series created by  tomino yoshiyuki and produced by Sunrise Studios in 1983. It also had mecha designs by miyatake kazutaka.
seishou elementary school uniform:
The school uniform worn by students of the Private Seishou University-affiliated Elementary School in the lyrical nanoha series.
The female uniform consists of a long white dress with a white jacket. Its design is a prototype of takamachi nanoha's barrier jacket.
seishou middle school uniform:
The school uniform worn by students of the Private Seishou University-affiliated Middle School in the lyrical nanoha series.
The uniform consists of a white shirt, a red ribbon, a brown jacket, and a brown pleated skirt.
seishou music academy uniform:

- A red bowtie.
- A grey jacket.
- A pleated grey skirt.
- Brown loafers.

seishun buta yarou: Seishun Buta Yarou (青春ブタ野郎シリーズ, English language title Rascal Does Not Dream of Bunny Girl Senpai, abbrev. Aobuta) is a series of light novels by kamoshida hajime published by Dengeki Bunko starting in 2014. An anime adaptation began airing in October 2018.
seitokai nimo anawa aru!:
EN: There is also an Opening in the Student Council

seitokai no ichizon:

seitokai yakuindomo: A 2007 4koma manga by Ujiie Tozen, serialized in weekly shounen magazine. Adapted into a 2010 TV anime by TV Kanagawa, a 2017 anime movie, and various OAVs.
seiya kou: One of the Sailor Starlights who are looking for princess kakyuu. Seiya is the black-haired member who gains feelings for Usagi, even though she is waiting for Mamoru to return from America. Seiya transforms into sailor star fighter.
seiyo academy school uniform: The school uniform featured in shugo chara!'s Seiyo Academy.
seiza:
Formal Japanese sitting position. Formed by kneeling on the floor and then resting the buttocks on the heels, keeping the legs folded under the thighs and the top side of the feet flat on the ground.
If the legs are folded out to either side, it's instead known as wariza, and if they are only to one side, it's called yokozuwari.
sekai seifuku: bouryaku no zvezda: Sekai Seifuku: Bouryaku no Zvezda (世界征服 ～謀略のズヴィズダー～, lit. World Conquest: Zvezda's Plot) is an anime series that aired January 2014, directed by Tensei Okamura and co-written with Meteor Hoshizora of Type-Moon. Characters designs by kuroboshi kouhaku and sasaki keigo.
sekaiju no meikyuu: Localized in North America and Europe as Etrian Odyssey. Nintendo DS and 3DS Dungeon Crawler RPG series developed by Atlus—literally, Labyrinth of the World Tree. Variously abbreviated as "SQ" and "MeiQ."
sekaiju no meikyuu 1: 2007 Nintendo DS Dungeon Crawler RPG developed by Atlus. First game in the sekaiju no meikyuu series.
sekaiju no meikyuu 2: 2008 Nintendo DS Dungeon Crawler RPG developed by Atlus. Second game in the sekaiju no meikyuu series.
sekaiju no meikyuu 3: 2010 Nintendo DS Dungeon Crawler RPG developed by Atlus. Sequel to the sekaiju no meikyuu games with a brand-new cast of playable character classes.
sekaiju no meikyuu 4: The fourth main entry of the sekaiju no meikyuu series, released in 2012 in Japan and 2013 internationally. The first nintendo 3ds entry of the series, Sekaiju no Meikyuu 4 features a full-fledged overworld map and a mix of new classes and old.
sekaiju no meikyuu 5: The fifth main entry of the sekaiju no meikyuu series, released on August 4, 2016 in Japan. Sekaiju no Meikyuu 5 features four character races spread out through the classes, all of whose appearances and colors can be customized.
seki hiromi: An iDOLM@STER Cinderella Girls character in the Cute (Pink Flower) category. She is voiced by aizawa saya.
sekibanki:

shouji:
Shouji (障子) are a type of door, window, or room divider in traditional Japanese architecture. They consist of thin, translucent paper on a wooden lattice frame. The paper is thin enough to let light in, but not to see through.
Shouji can be used as sliding doors or as windows. Sometimes, shouji panels may include a small glass window to see through.
Shouji are similar to fusuma, another type of sliding paper panel. The difference is that fusuma are made of thick, opaque paper that doesn't let light through.

sleeves past wrists:

They also do this if they are preparing to deliver a blow to someone in a comical way or if they are getting ready for something difficult.

For pants, see pants rolled up.

Includes sleeves visibly only folded up once. Not to be confused with sleeves pushed up, in which case the sleeves are only pushed up the arm, instead of being folded up.

source quote parody: When a quote is parodied by being slightly altered from its original form.
source request:
No source for the image is known, but is desired by one or more members.
See help:image source for more information on how to source an image.
source smaller:
When the image at the source is smaller (lower resolution) than the image on Danbooru.
This may be because the artist revised the original image and replaced it with a smaller version after it was uploaded to Danbooru, or because the uploader uploaded an upscaled version of the image, or because they uploaded a larger version of the image that actually came from a different source.

soviet:
Anything related to the former Soviet Union, and, to a wider extent, the Warsaw Pact.
The Soviet Union (1917-1991), officially the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR), was a vast communist federated state in what is today russia and other adjacent nations with a state ideology of Marxism-Leninism.
soviet army: The Workers' and Peasants' Red Army, or more known by their shortened name Red Army, was the prime land warfare forces of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republic. It was established in 1917 and was in service until 1946 when the army took the official name of "Soviet Army", It was then in service until its dissolution in 1991 following the dissolution of the Soviet Union. The remaining bulk of the military would be integrated into the russian army.
soviet flag:

soy sauce: Thin brownish sauce made of fermented soy beans, used to season food.
soy sauce bottle:
A type of bottle designed for dispensing small amounts of soy sauce onto food. Since the sauce is incredibly salty and could render the food inedible if poured on too much, the top of the bottle has an angled cap with a spout-like opening which helps limit the amount of soy sauce being poured.
This can also refer to the brown bottles that soy sauce is sold in at supermarkets.
soybean: Small brown beans that are widely consumed around the world. Popularized in east Asia by Buddhism's tendency towards vegetarianism, soybeans in various forms are a stable of billions of peoples diets.

space: Implies that the scene in the image takes place in outer space, a setting usually asociated with science fiction.
space adventure cobra: A space opera adventure manga series by terasawa buichi published on weekly shounen jump, starring the space pirate cobra (space adventure cobra) and his partner lady armaroid. Has multiple anime adaptations, including a movie, two television series, and two short OVA series.
space channel 5: A series of music video games published by sega.
space dandy: Space Dandy (スペース☆ダンディ) is a 2014 Japanese anime series directed by Shinichiro Watanabe and produced by Bones. The series follows Dandy, an alien hunter who is "a dandy guy in space", in search for aliens with his robot assistant QT and an alien cat named Meow.
space helmet: A rounded see-through helmet designed for astronauts.
space print:
When something, usually an article of clothing, has such a print that it resembles outer space.
Space print implicates starry sky print to simplify the relation between both tags, as they share many of the same features. The space print tag is to be used for prints that include celestial bodies other than stars, such as planets or nebulae, or otherwise don't represent a view that could be seen from the surface of a planet. A simple print with only stars should only get the starry sky print tag. (topic #13462)
space shuttle: A plane-like spacecraft launched vertically with aide of a rocket, and landed as a glider with atmospheric control. Examples include the US Space Shuttle and the Soviet Buran
space station: An artificial man-made facility constructed in outer space that serves as a base of operations or as a relay station.

spacecraft:
A spacecraft is a craft or vehicle or machine designed for spaceflight. They are frequently depicted in many works of Science Fiction.
Any vehicle capable of manned spaceflight, includes space shuttles, rocket ships, flying saucers, and any other configuration such as Star Trek's Enterprise, star wars t-65 x-wings and tie fighters, or uchuu senkan yamato's rendition of the Battleship Yamato. 
They can be small enough for one person to use (like the starfighters) or as big as planets.
spacecraft interior: Posts that depict the interior/inside of a spacecraft.
spaceship hair ornament: A hair ornament or hairpin shaped like a spaceship.
spacesuit: A special garment encompassing the whole body to keep the wearer safe from the rigours of outer space (vacuum, temperature, radiation, and so on). Space suits in sci-fi settings are usually much less bulky than those IRL.
spade earrings: earrings that are shaped like the spade card suit.
spade hair ornament: A hair ornament or hairpin shaped like the spade card suit.
spaghetti: A type of pasta shaped like long circular strands when cooked. Arguably the most well-known kind of pasta in the world.
spaghetti strap: A very thin type of shoulder strap typically found on camisoles and other feminine top wear. Note that the spaghetti strap is not a top in and of itself, but describes a thin strap used on various top styles.
spandex: A synthetic fiber known for its exceptional elasticity. Frequently used to make sportswear and other skin tight clothing.

sparkle:
A momentary bright shimmer of reflected light, generally diamond (shape)- or star (symbol)-shaped, and short-lived. Groups of them tend to appear and vanish in various instances.
Sparkle, glint, and diffraction spikes all refer to similar patterns of bright lines radiating from a point. They are not clearly differentiated, and usage tends to be context-sensitive. In general:
- Sparkle is considered the base case. Usually four lines at right angles radiating from a point. Associated with eyes, liquid or particulate matter (e.g. raindrops, snow, sand), or nothing (appearing mid-air).
sparkle background:
A background consisting of sparkles, whether they're drawn really large and easy to see, or the background is flooded with glints of glitter.
Use sparkling aura when it's focused on a specific character or object.
sparkle hair ornament:
A hair ornament themed after a sparkle.
Mainly associated with kagura hikari.
sparkle print: Clothing or a fabric item that has the printed motif of sparkles.
sparkler:
A type of handheld firework. It's a long rod or stick held at one end while the other end burns. senkou hanabi is a specific type of Japanese sparkler.
Don't confuse with sparkle.
sparkling aura:
For multiple sparkles around a certain object or character.
Use sparkle for a single one.
sparkling eyes: When a character's eyes contain star-shaped sparkles in them, adjacent to the pupil.
sparkling sweat:
When there's a sparkle effect around a character that's sweating (post #4961776), or when a sparkle effect is drawn over the sweat (post #4254581)
Could also apply if the sweat is rendered to look like it's glowing or sparkly.
sparks:
A small fiery particle thrown off from a fire, alight in ashes, or produced by striking together two hard surfaces such as stone or metal. It can be seen from pyrotechnics such as sparklers and from metalworking.
Note that the sole presence of fire does not justify the use of this tag.
Compare with embers.
sparrow: A general term for birds in the Passeridae family, as well as similar but unrelated birds in other families.
sparse chest hair:
When chest hair is visible only at the top or mid section of the chest. 
Could also apply when chest hair is drawn very sparsely (like sparse stubble in appearance).
sparse pubic hair:
pubic hair that is particularly light, thin, whispy, or groomed in such a way as to be of minimal area or volume compared to that of typical, natural pubic hair.
This tag is the opposite extreme of excessive pubic hair.

Sold to many police forces worldwide and quite prominent in many action movies, including the terminator.
spasm: Spiky lines drawn bursting out of the body or clothes of a character to express when they have become startled or are feeling thrilled.
spatula: A flat kitchen utensil used for flipping in cooking, transferring food products from one tray/plate to another, or scraping food off a pan or bowl. A spatula can also refer to a flat rubber utensil for spreading frosting over dessert foods.
speaker: A device that converts electronic signals into audible sounds. Often placed on the floor or on a desk mounted to a pole or a wall. Often used a a part of a stereo system, public address system, computer setup, or home theater system.

speculum:
