speech bubble:
A bubble with a pointed end that shows what a character is saying. It can either have text or an object. If it is empty add the tag blank speech bubble.
For a bubble containing thoughts or dreaming use thought bubble.
speech stab: Used for comics showing a character getting stabbed by a speech bubble or a sharp object originating from one.
speed lines:
Lines drawn to emphasize the velocity of a person or object.
When used directly on objects, esp. in the foreground, these may be accompanied by motion blur effects.
When used in (or in lieu of) the background, speed lines indicate that the persons or objects in the foreground are moving past the background at high speed.
Not to be confused with emphasis lines, which do not indicate motion, but rather are used dramatically to draw attention to a specific part of the image.
spell: The act of casting magic, usually with the help of a magical item such as a book or wand. The instance just before the incantation is completed.
spell card:
A magically infused card used to cast spells. 
Most commonly (but not exclusively) seen in touhou-related images. They first appeared there in the sixth game, and have been a mainstay of the series ever since. Spell cards allow the casting of powerful, intricate danmaku patterns or the usage of special abilities.
This tag is only used to denote the presence of an actual, physical spell card. Images that portray a recognizable spell card's spell in action or its effects should be tagged with spell.
sperm cell:

sphinx:
In ancient egyptian culture, sphinx is a creature that has the body of a lion, while the head could be a human, ram, or bird. They are most commonly assigned to protect the sacred places.
In greek mythology, sphinx is an individual monster with human female torso with a lion body. The sphinx in Greek mythology is usually seen preying on the adventurer by asking the riddles to decide their fate.

spicy: A character's reaction to (often too) spicy food: breathing fire, sweating while opening the mouth with the tongue out and tearing up, a reddened face, and so on, depictions of spicy food itself or both.
spider: An eight-legged predatory arachnid with an unsegmented body consisting of a fused head and thorax and a rounded abdomen. Spiders have fangs that inject poison into their prey, and most kinds spin webs in which to capture insects.
spider girl: A type of monster girl that has additional appendages totaling eight, and can spin webbing. Her hair can also resemble spider legs, such as arane's hairstyle. She may or may not have a spider or tarantula body, such as post #1006496.
spider lily:
A poisonous flower (species Lycoris radiata) commonly associated with death. 
A spider lily has 4-6 flowers growing from a central leafless stem, forming a sort of dome. Natural colors include red (most common), pink, white and yellow, sometimes depicted in non-existent black and blue. The most noticeable features are the long stamens, which give it a distinct entangled/spidery look, earning its common English name 'Spider Lily'. 
Its Japanese name is "Higan-bana" (Higan flower) or "Manjushage".
spider lily print:

spider web: A net-like construct of sticky silk thread used by spiders to catch prey.

spiked dildo: A dildo with spikes, studs or ribs.

spiked hairband: A hairband with spikes of any varying length.
spiked halo: A halo with spikes on it.
spiked helmet: A character's helmet that has spikes on it. Can be historical helmets such as the German pickelhaube, or fantasy helmets with spikes on them.
spiked knuckles: Knuckles with spikes on them. Can be found on gauntlets, brass knuckles or grow naturally on someones hands.

spiked penis: A penis that has spikes, studs, barbs, or any other similar natural protrusions.
spiked shell: Such as turtle shell, clam shell, snail shell, et cetera. Shells as in anatomical features, not Ghost-in-the.
spiked tail: A tail with spikes on it.
spiked thighlet: A thighlet with spikes on it, if it's made out of leather or fabric use spiked thigh strap instead, not to be confused with spiked thighhighs
spikes: Sharp, pointy protrusions on a surface or object used for stabbing those who come too close to them. Mainly used for defense.
spill: An accidental overflow of liquid from its holding container.

spine: The spine is the common name for the human vertebral column, one of the major components of the skeleton.

A type of alternate species where a pre-existing character is turned into an inkling or octoling from Splatoon. This includes changing their hair into tentacle hair, and giving them fangs and pointy ears.

splatter: A liquid or liquid-like substance spread across a surface.
splatter background: A background with a splatter formation (e.g. blood, ink , paint ,etc.).
split: A gymnastic position wherein the legs slide into opposite directions away from the body, causing them to be either parallel or perpendicular to the ground.
split crop: When the character is depicted with only one side of the character.
split mouth: An artistic style where the line representing a character's mouth isn't fully connected. The mouth is usually closed but can also be open.
split ponytail: A ponytail that splits at the base into two or more tails.
split screen: When the image is split into two halves with a line. Several uses for this include comparing a character's different forms; placing two characters side by side in two columns (for more columns, see column lineup); or a technique used to convey two clashing characters.
split theme:
Multiple distinct (and usually opposite) themes being represented at the same time, with a split between them as a way to represent contrast. 
The simplest way to do this is to have two opposite themes on each side with a clean split in the middle (see split screen).
Examples:
- Two different characters being portrayed as one (post #1318355)
- While a character is in the middle of a henshin transformation (post #1841349)
- Revealing the "true nature" of a character (post #6870337)
- Comparing how a character looked when they were younger to when they're older
split-color hair:
two-tone hair that is divided vertically into two different colors at the top of the head.
The colors might not be a 50/50 split, and the colors might be mixed together, but the colors should be distinctive enough to tell them apart. Different hues of the same color are acceptable, so long as they are easy to distinguish.
spoilers:
Information that spoils the plot or ending of a work of fiction. As a tag, denotes that the picture contains spoilers.
Please keep gratuitous spoilers out of wiki pages, and mark spoilers in comments or forum posts with ||spoiler goes here|| tags.
spoken anger vein:
An anger vein inside a speech bubble.
If you want to use the mark in a translation note, use the 💢 character or use the Unicode character entity reference: 💢.
spoken animal: When any kind of animal is seen in a speech bubble.
spoken blush:
blush sign in a speech bubble, with text or without.
Often appears as several slashes: ///
spoken character:
When a character's face or the entire inset of them appears in a speech bubble. Often used to show an off-screen character's reaction or when the spoken character is referring to that said person.
See spoken letter or spoken number for a character as in a letter or number.
spoken ellipsis: When a speech bubble contains only an ellipsis (...). Meant to show that a character is at a loss for words.
spoken exclamation mark: An exclamation mark symbol (!) that is spoken aloud, often in a speech bubble.
spoken expression: When an emoticon is expressed inside a speech bubble. The expression may or may not already be used as a tag on Danbooru. If it is, then both can be used.
spoken flying sweatdrops: flying sweatdrops that appear inside a speech or thought bubble.
spoken food: When any kind of food item is seen inside a speech bubble, used to indicate that the character has a craving for a particular food.
spoken heart:
"♥!"

stasis tank:
A liquid-filled container (usually a tube or a tank) with transparent walls. Possible uses include keeping living organisms in stasis, accelerating growth or development after undergoing a cloning process, or even post-injury healing and recovery.
An archetypal stasis tank design can be seen in post #607235. science fiction commonly depicts people floating in these tanks, such as shown in post #80217. 
(Note that this tag can apply to a wide variety of containers/vats/tanks, as long as have a description and function similar to what is outlined above.)
static: A random pattern of colored or black-and-white pixels displayed on a television or other screen when no signal is present.
stationary restraints:
When a character's limbs or body is held in place by objects or devices that are made of rigid materials and locked into position such that they will not budge or sway if the victim struggles.
Key examples are pillories or stocks mounted in place, shackles bolted or screwed to a surface, (such as a wall, floor, or table) cuffs holding the subject inside a sex machine, and pipe arrangements built around the subject.
Restraints that are tethered by ropes or chains do not count, nor do tentacles.
stationery:

stats: A graphic with captions (usually metrics) describing the subject in detail.
statue: A lifelike free-standing sculpture usually depicting a human, animal, or deity. Statues memorializing specific historical figures are particularly common. Statues vary in scale from life-size to colossal proportions. Small-scale statues are known as statuettes.

A broken chain lies at her feet. The statue has become an iconic symbol of freedom and of the United States.
steak: A cut of meat that is cooked to varying degrees of doneness, ranging in the following: very rare - rare - medium rare - medium - medium well done - well done. Without a qualifier, steak refers to beefsteak. Other types of steaks are defined, such as fish steak or venison steak.

stenciled rose:
A highly stylized design where a rose is drawn without lines, as if with stencils. Very frequently drawn in monochrome.

The stenciled rose differs from the mackintosh rose in that it usually depicts a matured bloom rather than a younger bud, features more space between wedges, and exhibits more variety and irregularity of shape amongst its pieces.

stethoscope: The stethoscope is an acoustic medical device for auscultation, or listening to the internal sounds of an animal or human body. stew: A combination of solid food ingredients cooked in a liquid and served in the resulting gravy.

AUG HBAR is the light machine gun variant with a longer, heavier barrel and a bipod.
stg44: A world war ii-era German selective fire rifle chambered for 7,92×33mm Kurz cartridge. Sturmgewehr is a German word for "assault rifle". It influenced the design of many post-war weapons such as the kalashnikov rifle.
stick: A long piece of wood. Not to be confused with canes, also known as "walking sticks".
stick figure:
Extremely simple drawing/pictogram of humans or animals, the heads are basically circular and body parts are rendered as  few lines with few or no curves.

stick poster: Posters that are usually longer and more slender than many pin-up posters. By definition, they are actually like illustrated versions of vertical rectangular banners.
stickam:

Artists would sometimes post artwork on Pixiv to announce when they were streaming. These pictures were often deleted after a short amount of time.
'Stickam Delivery' means the art is a delivery of the completed artwork from the live stream.
sticker: A piece of paper or plastic, sticky on one side and non-stick on the other, with a design or text printed on it. Stickers are often used for play or advertising.
sticker on face: A sticker on a character's face.
sticky note: A small piece of paper with a strip of glue on its back, made for temporarily attaching notes to documents and other surfaces. Usually colored yellow due to the ubiquity of 3M's Post-It brand.
stielhandgranate: German for "Stalk hand grenade." Standard grenade for the German Army from WWI until the end of WWII. Also known as the "potato masher" for its distinctive shape.
stiff tail: A normally flexible tail that has visibly stiffened with the character's emotional response to something. Can occur with any emotion that may cause increased tension in the body, but often seen with intense anger, shock, fear, pain, and sometimes with arousal as well.
stifled laugh:
Preventing oneself from laughing out loud, usually by covering their mouth with their own hand.
May result in giggling.
stile uniform: The uniform worn by the waitresses in blend s. It consists of a buttoned-up, short-sleeved, collared short dress a white frilled waist apron, a white headscarf, white gloves, white thighhighs and black loafers. Each character wears a different color version of the uniform.
stiletto heels: Stiletto heels are long, thin high heels found on some boots and shoes, usually for women.
still life: A work of art depicting mostly inanimate objects. fruit bowl paintings are a common example.
stinger: A sharp organ that is usually connected with a poison gland or otherwise adapted to wound by piercing and injecting a poison. Creatures such as bees, scorpions and stingrays utilize these for defensive purposes.
stingray: Any of numerous rays (as of the family Dasyatidae) with one or more large sharp barbed dorsal spines near the base of the whiplike tail capable of inflicting severe wounds.
stirring: The act of rotating a spoon, a stick or even a drinking straw within liquid in order to consistently disperse ingredients or to keep it at an even temperature.
stirrup legwear: Legwear (normally thighhighs, but more rarely socks or pantyhose) that have a stirrup around the sole of the foot, leaving both the toes and heel uncovered.
stitched:
An image made by stitching together multiple separate images posted by an artist.
For example, a full body shot made by combining a lower body shot and an upper body shot posted by the artist as two separate pics.
Stitches are generally "not considered third-party edits":[/forum_topics/27481] because of their nondestructive nature.
Note that collages don't fall under this.
Not to be confused with stitches.
stitched arm: When one or both character's arm is either attached to the rest of the body with stitches or has a significant amount of stitches on it, commonly seen on zombies
stitched face: When a character has stitches running across a significant portion of their face.
stitched leg: When one or both character's legs is either attached to the rest of the body with stitches or has a significant amount of stitches on it, commonly seen on zombies
stitched torso: When a character has stitches running a significant portion of the torso, commonly seen in zombies
stitches:
Tag used to describe visible thread-holdings on clothing or ones body, you will often see this on stuffed animals and zombies too. It has a distinctive train track look or appear as X's going in a line.
Sutures (also known as stitches) are used to hold skin and all other tissues of the human body together, after someone has been injured or went through surgery. This is done with a needle and preformed by a doctor or nurse.
Not to be confused with stitched.
stitching: One in-and-out movement of a threaded needle in sewing or in closing a wound.
stocks:
Planks that restrain only one's arms or legs.
For boards that restrain a person's body or head, use pillory.
stole: A band of fabric or fur draped around the neck or shoulders. Similar to a scarf but with its ends hanging down untied. There are two common types: a formal women's garment worn around the shoulders, or a religious garment worn around the neck by priests.
stomach:
An exposed frontal abdomen, specifically the area around the navel and above the groin. For images pertaining to the internal organ itself, use stomach (organ).
Should only be used when the stomach is a prominent, noticeable part of the image, not merely in the background or partially exposed.
Unlike midriff, stomach can be used when the stomach is visible between underwear, bikinis, and when the character is nude, bottomless, or topless (topless male for male characters).
stomach bulge:
A visible protrusion of the stomach caused when something (usually a penis, tentacles, etc.) pushes against the stomach from the inside.  Like cervical penetration, it is impossible to occur in reality without fatal damage.
If the bulging of the stomach is caused by the stomach filling up with something (usually a fluid), it is called inflation.
stomach cutout: A clothing cutout that exposes the stomach.
stomach day: A date pun. November 7th is "Good Stomach Day".
stomach growling: The sounds of stomachs growling are caused by contractions and movement of air and gas; mixed with fluids in the digestive system to make a rumbling, gurgling, or growling sound. This can occur inside the stomach, and also the intestines. The noises can happen regularly, but are heard louder when the stomach and intestines are empty after several hours without eating, which causes the air and gas pockets to make a more audible growling sound. Stomach growling is translated borborygymi, and indicates hunger, digestion, or gas moving around inside the belly.
stomach punch: A punch to the stomach. Commonly seen in ryona art.
stomach tattoo: A tattoo on the stomach, but not above the pubic area like a pubic tattoo.
stomping:
When a character is in the process of forcefully stepping on someone or something. Motion lines can be found in these posts.
For when just a foot is on someone but there is no stomping motion, see stepped on.

This ritual is frequently translated into English as "Midnight Anathema Ritual." Every night, the ritual takes place during "Ushi no Koku," the name of a time period used in traditional Japan, representing 1:00 to 3:00 in the morning.

street:

A street is usually designed to accommodate both vehicle and pedestrian traffic, with intersections, traffic lights, sidewalks, and crosswalks. A highway is usually designed only for high-speed or long distance vehicle traffic and doesn't have these features.

tank:
An armored, tracked military vehicle with a single cannon (some  tanks may have mounted machine guns or more than one cannon). Its heavy armor protects  the crew from enemy fire while the tracks let it traverse difficult terrain or obstacles.
For tagging purposes this tag may also be used on any tank-like vehicle, whether real or fictional. This may include things such as tank destroyers (ex: sturmgeschutz iii), self-propelled artillery (ex: m109 howitzer), rocket artillery, and the like.
For the container type tank, use the tag: tank (container)
tank cupola:
A tank's cupola is a raised, armored structure on the roof of a tank/armored vehicle or tank turret that often carries observation devices and has a hatch. 
Tanks of WW2 often had large cupolas on their turrets to allow space for periscopes or windows to give a crew member, often the commander, a much better view outside the vehicle. Usually they were also the most logical place for the commander's hatch, as it would allow them to stand partially outside the vehicle for a better view or to operate a top-mounted machine gun.
tank destroyer: A combat vehicle specifically designed to combat against armored vehicle, typically based on a tank chassis. Most are turretless or have open turrets. They were mostly used in world war ii.
tank helmet: A protective piece of equipment issued to tank or vehicle crew, primarily designed to withstand concussions against the vehicle interior. They come in different designs and shapes depending on what nation and time period. One of the most recognizable tank helmets is the Soviet/Russian TSh-4.
tank interior: Posts that depict the interior/inside of a tank.
tank shell: A shell is a payload-carrying projectile which, as opposed to shot, contains an explosive or other filling, though modern usage sometimes includes large solid projectiles properly termed shot
tank top: A sleeveless top with wide straps, worn by both genders. A top for women with thin spaghetti straps is called a camisole, while a camisole that goes past the hips might be either a chemise or a babydoll.
tank turret:
A type of turret designed to be mounted on a ground military vehicle, often but not exclusively a tank.
Tank turrets are generally compact and low profile, smaller than naval turrets, typically seating one to three crew members. The single main gun or cannon is usually centrally-mounted and of small or medium-caliber, often 20-125mm. May also feature additional coaxial or top-mounted armament,  mostly machine guns but occasionally smaller cannons.
tankard:

Due to the nostalgic design of tankards, they are commonly seen in medieval European fantasy settings, particularly in taverns.

tantou:
A single or double-edged short sword carried by samurai in Japan or by noblewomen for self-defense. The sides of the blade are nearly flat.
Early tantous had no aesthetic quality and were pure weapons, but up until the 16th century, the tanto was preferred to the wakizashi for use in battle by samurai while a wakizashi was used for ceremonial occasions. After this period, they were used interchangeably. Can be used either for stabbing or slashing.
tantrum: An emotional episode fueled by feelings of anger, distress or refusal. Often involves screaming, crying, lying/rolling on the floor, flailing of arms, or throwing objects. There are two kinds of tantrums; the sort done by children in order to get their way, and the sort done by adults who are at their boiling point.
tanuki:
The Japanese name for the Japanese raccoon dog. In Japanese folklore, a tanuki is a playful shape-shifting traditional youkai.
Not to be confused for the raccoon, which looks similar to the tanuki but is not the same animal. A key difference is their fur color: tanuki tend to have brown fur while raccoons have grey fur.
The words "tanuki" (狸), "mujina" (貉), and "mami" (猯) were historically confused in Japan. "Mujina" and "mami" used to mean badgers in some areas, while on the other areas these terms used to mean raccoon dogs. There are some areas in which badgers were called tanuki.

traffic: An image that pays special attention to road traffic, including vehicles, pedestrians, traffic signals, and related elements.
traffic barrier: A barricade designed control the flow of vehicular or pedestrian traffic in a specified area.  Commonly used to keep vehicular traffic within the roadway or prevent them from hitting obstacles or running off steep slopes.  They're also used to bar entry, such as on blocking access to incomplete roads and bridges.  Such barriers are also used to protect pedestrians from vehicles, and may be placed to separate areas of high pedestrian traffic from vehicular traffic.
traffic baton: Also called a signal baton or marshalling wand, a traffic baton is used by police for directing traffic or by ground crews for aircraft marshalling. Simple versions are essentially flashlights with translucent plastic covers attached to the front.
traffic cone: Traffic cones, also known as safety cones or road cones, are cone (geometry)-shaped markers used to create merge lanes during road construction projects or traffic accidents.
traffic light: A traffic light (also known as a traffic signal or stoplight) is a signaling device positioned at road intersections, crosswalks, and other locations in order to control the flow of vehicular traffic.  Traffic lights consist normally of three light signals of the colors red, yellow, and green/blue arranged vertically or horizontally in that order.  While this is standardized internationally, variations may exist.
traffic mirror: Traffic mirror or convex mirror (sometimes simply called a curved mirror) is a type of road safety mirror that's curved outwards. The purpose of this curved bulge is to expand the field that's visible in the reflection, making them ideal for improving road safety.
trailer:

train:

Do not use this tag if a train is only seen from the inside. train interior will suffice.

train interior: The interior of a train (as opposed to the exterior).
train station: Terminal where trains load or unload passengers or goods.

wanted poster:
A poster distributed by police to warn the public about a criminal who is wanted for arrest. A wanted poster usually has the word "WANTED" at the top, and the fugitive's name and picture on the bottom. Sometimes a bounty or a list of their crimes is included.
In earlier times (or fictional settings), wanted posters would sometimes also read "wanted dead or alive", making the wanted criminal an outlaw in the literal sense (i.e. a person from whom the protection of the law was withdrawn and who could be killed without official repercussions by anyone).
war:
An organized, armed, and, often, a prolonged conflict that is carried on between states, nations, or armed political organization using armies and soldiers. Typically to either resolve diplomatic or political disputes or as an aggressive diplomatic tool against other countries. War are usually carried out between two or more military of the opposing factions.
This tag can be applied to any depiction of war, either historical or fictional, as well as various aspects of it (such as death and destruction), either literally or symbolically.
war fan:
A Japanese war fan is a fan designed for use in warfare. Several types of war fans were used by the samurai class of feudal Japan and each had a different look and purpose.
There are three kinds of war fan:
Gunsen (軍扇) were folding fans used by the average warriors to cool themselves off. They were made of wood, bronze, brass or a similar metal for the inner spokes, and often used thin iron or other metals for the outer spokes or cover, making them lightweight but strong.
war hammer:
A late medieval weapon of war originally intended for close combat action. It was designed to deliver heavy damage against well-armored opponents through sheer blunt force. Though some adapted it as a versatile polearm weapon instead by giving it a longer handle.
Real life war hammers are comparable in size with a regular carpentry hammer, though with a longer handle and often a spike opposite the blunt head to pierce armor. This tag can also be applied to huge fantasy weapons depicted simply as an oversized hammer/sledgehammer.
Not to be confused with warhammer 40k.

wardrobe:

wardrobe error:
Unintentionally wearing clothes the wrong way, such as wearing a shirt backwards, or a bikini upside-down.
Not to be confused with accidental exposure or wardrobe malfunction, which is when the clothing is worn correctly, but it exposes the wearer through no fault of their own.
wardrobe malfunction:
Failure of an article of clothing, such as a bra slipping or fabric tearing, that exposes some or all of one's private parts.
Not to be confused with accidental exposure, in which the article of clothing does not fail, nor does the person wear it incorrectly, but they are exposed by some external factor, such as wind lift.
warehouse: A large building for storing goods. They commonly have loading docks, cargo pallets, and many shelves. They may also have cranes or other large machinery designed to assist in loading or unloading goods.

warhammer fantasy: Warhammer Fantasy is a tabletop miniature wargame produced by Games Workshop since 1983. It is the precursor to warhammer 40k and takes place in a fantasy setting rather than the latter's grimdark sci-fi setting.

wariza:
Wariza (割座), also known as "w-sitting" or "reverse tailor style sitting" in English, is a sitting posture whereby the butt is on the floor and the legs are bent backwards on each side of the body. It is the traditional informal sitting style for Japanese women. If the legs are folded out to only one side, then it is called yokozuwari.
The other Japanese names are: 女の子座り (onna-no-ko-zuwari, girl's sitting), アヒル座り (ahiru-zuwari, duck sitting) or ぺたん座り (petan-zuwari, flat surface sitting). (In fact, in Japanese, wariza more commonly refers to a yoga pose.)
warming hands: A character is making their hands warmer, typically by breathing on them or holding them to a heat source.
warning sign:
A traditionally triangular sign with an exclamation mark or diamond (shape) (⚠️) in the middle used to indicate dangerous areas/chemicals.

- lightning bolt symbol 
- radiation symbol

warrior:
Someone engaged in or experienced in warfare and fighting. Often clad in bits of armor and drawn with a melee weapon, typically heavy sword or large axe. Can also be applied to a Character Class in various different RPG series.
While the definition is similar to "soldier", the "warrior" tag should be applied to characters with a less "professional" appearance (i.e. no uniforms), and restricted to ancient or medieval era combatants.
warship:
Any type of ship specifically made for military combat uses. Typically operated by the navy.

wasabi: A spice that has an extremely strong flavor. Its hotness is more akin to that of a hot mustard rather than the capsaicin in a chili pepper, producing vapors that stimulate the nasal passages more than the tongue.
wash cloth: A cloth used for washing the face and body, usually made of terry cloth or other absorbent materials.
washbowl:
A large round or rectangular bowl, usually made of plastic, used for washing one's hands and face, small articles of clothing, etc. Most commonly seen during sit down bathing in bathrooms. Also known as a washbasin.
The Naigai Yakuhin Company is known for distributing washbowls to public onsen across Japan to promote their Kerorin brand of aspirin.
washing: The act of scrubbing the body with soap and/or water during a bath to clean off dirt, sweat and dead skin.
washing another: Washing another human or humanoid, whether it be the hair, body, or elsewhere. Typically happens inside a bathtub or shower and includes soap bubbles.
washing hair: The act of cleaning hair with soap or shampoo. A character can wash their own hair, or another character might wash it for them. A child will often be depicted wearing a shampoo hat while having their hair washed.
washing machine: An appliance used to wash clothes. The term applies primarily to machines that use water as opposed to dry cleaning or ultrasonic cleaners. The user adds laundry detergent, sold in liquid or powder form, to the wash water.
washing vehicle:
Washing a car, truck, or other vehicle by hand. For the facility designed to wash vehicles automatically (with brushes or sprayers), use car wash (place).
Washing cars by hand is also frequently used as a means of fund raising, particularly in the US, where volunteers will wash cars in exchange for donations. Some of these car washes may feature women in bikinis to draw in more people, such car washes are referred to as a bikini car wash.
washio sumi wa yuusha de aru: A 2014 light novel written by Takahiro and illustrated by bunbun. wasp: Social or solitary insects that have membranous wings, compound eyes, and a stinger. Unlike bees, they have hairless bodies and large mandibles.
wasteland:
A type of barren, devastated terrain that is inhospitable to life. Whereas polar regions and deserts are naturally barren due to their cold and/or arid climate, wastelands have been rendered uninhabitable by warfare, nuclear fallout, natural disasters, etc. Expect to see rocky terrain and abundant dust clouds, and possibly dead vegetation or the wreckage of ruined civilizations.
Use this tag for landscapes bereft of green plants that aren't merely natural deserts, glaciers, or mountains.

watatsuki no toyohime: A touhou character introduced in the manga silent sinner in blue. Lunarian princess and older sister of watatsuki no yorihime. She has the ability to manipulate boundaries, similar to yakumo yukari, but her power is limited to boundaries involving the moon.

watch: A timepiece that is made to be worn on a person. The term now usually refers to a wristwatch, which is worn on the wrist.
watching:
The act of observing from a distance.
For characters staring at a television screen to watch a program, see watching television. For obsessively watching and following a person, use stalking.
watching television: A character watching a television screen.
watchmen: A superhero comic book series written by Alan Moore and published by dc comics in 1986. It depicts an alternate history where masked heroes emerged in the 1940s, changing many key moments in history, but became outlawed in the 1970s.
water:
A colorless, tasteless inorganic compound with chemical formula H₂O, vital to entire life forms on Earth.
This only applies to water being clearly visible in its liquid state.
Not to be applied alongside underwater though the image has water, much of the picture takes place out of the water.
water balloon: A balloon that is filled with water. water yoyo is a subtype of this.
water bottle: A bottle used for carrying water or other drinks.
water drop: A small amount of water held together by viscosity (surface tension). Usually roughly spherical or teardrop-shaped, but may be deformed by motion.
water gun: A type of toy gun that is designed to shoot water, though other liquids are occasionally also used in them.  Most are shaped like a gun, but other shapes exist as well (such as tube or hose shape). Furthermore while most water guns have a reservoir of water for multiple shots, some designs can only fire once before needing to be refilled.
water lily flower: For the leaves of Water Lily, see lily pad. Please note that these flowers are not actually lilies.
water slide: A wet version of the slide.
water tank:
A container that used for storing water in large amounts for many purposes such as storing water for consumption, agriculture, and irrigation.
Water tanks are usually made of plastic, glass, or steel.
water tower: An elevated structure supporting a water tank constructed at a height sufficient to pressurize a water supply system for the distribution of potable (drinking) water, and to provide emergency storage for fire protection.
water wheel:
A machine used to convert the energy of running water into useful mechanical power. It consists of a wheel with fixed blades that intercept the flow of water. Water wheels were used in the pre-modern era for grinding grain in gristmills or powering industrial machinery, but they have since been replaced with other forms of power.
The modern equivalent of the water wheel is the water turbine, used to generate power in hydroelectric dams.
water world:
Use this tag when the entire surface of the world appears to be covered in water. Buildings or man-made structures like railroad tracks can be visible, but there should be no mountains, hills, islands, beaches, or similar natural landmasses.
Do not use this tag with the underwater tag.
water yoyo: A kind of water balloon on a string. You win them at Japanese festivals by participating in yo-yo fishing, similar to how you get bagged fish from goldfish scooping.
watercolor effect: When an artwork that didn't use any actual watercolor (medium) (usually a digital art) tries to mimic the effects of watercolors.
watercraft: The term watercraft covers a range of different water-borne vehicles, including ships, boats, hovercraft and submarines.
waterfall: A cascade of water flowing over a steep or vertical drop.
watering: The act of using a watering can to sprinkle water onto a plant, although it can jokingly be poured onto another person.
watering can: A portable can with a long open spout extending from one side and a handle on the top, designed for manually watering flowers and plants.
watermark:
An image containing text or a logo superimposed on top of the image. Typically to identify the owner/creator of the work and/or prevent the image from being counterfeited. Some watermarks are also deliberately placed as a "paywall" on "samples" of "paid reward" images.
Posts with watermarks added by third-parties (anyone other than the artist) should not be uploaded.
Add watermark grid if it spans over a majority/the whole image. Add too many watermarks if it's in excess as to be noticeable from the thumbnail.
watermark grid:
A type of watermark that is intermittently spread across an entire image. 
Include sample watermark when applicable.
watermelon:
A large, roundish melon with a hard, green-striped rind and sweet, watery and red (occasionally yellowish) pulp. A tasty summer treat.
Whereas most varieties are oblong, Japanese-grown watermelons are nearly perfect spheres.
watermelon bar:

watermelon beachball:
A beachball designed to look like the outer green rind of a watermelon.
This shouldn't be used if the ball has green patterns similar to what a watermelon looks like, such as post #117985 or post #98446.
Sometimes a watermelon will be present alongside with another distinctly colored/patterned beachball. If you can't tell if the watermelon is a beachball as well, don't use this tag, and use watermelon instead.
watermelon hair ornament: A hair ornament shaped like a whole watermelon or a slice.
watermelon print: Clothing or an object that has the printed motif of a watermelon on it.

standing with the legs crossed at the calf-, knee-, or thigh-level.

wave print: An article of clothing or any object made out of fabric with the printed motif of water visibly crashing in waves. Not to be confused with the traditional wave-like pattern called seigaiha.

waves:
Waves like you see in water, or some other liquid. 
Do not confuse with waving, which is used for the hand gesture.
For sound-produced waves, see sound wave.
For circular concentric waves on a fluid, use also ripples.
waving:
The motion of waving one's hand or arm as if saying any of the following:
- "Hi!"
- "Bye!"
- "Over here!"
To avoid confusion, use "waves" if referring to ocean or tidal waves.
waving arm:
When one is moving one of their arms about, usually to invite someone to come over or say goodbye.
May be flailing.
waving arms: When one is moving both their arms about. May be flailing.
wavy eyes: When a character's eyes are shown to be wavy circles instead of smooth ones. Can be part of the artist's style, that the character is sad or part of a "puppy-dog" ploy to get affection.
wavy hair: A type of hair which resembles waves.
wavy mouth: Not the same as :3. Wavy mouth is usually seen when the character is scared, sad, or embarrassed.
wax:
An organic chemical substance, a type of lipid that is flexible and easy to form at room temperature, has a melting point of 45°C or higher, cannot dissolve in water, and is hydrophobic and repels water.
Waxes such as paraffin and beeswax, and hard fats such as tallow are used for lighting and decorative candles.
wax play: A bdsm sexual act involving using a lit candle to drop or spray a hot wax on another's body. Intended to create a brief stimuli of pain.
wax seal: A drop of wax solidified on an envelope to seal it, usually has text and symbols printed on it using a wax stamp.
wcdonald's: A common brand name imitation for the mcdonald's fast food chain. It eventually became an official brand co-opted by McDonald's themselves for an anime-themed international advertising campaign in Spring 2024.
weapon:
A tool or object designed to hurt, maim or kill a person.
Use this tag only for handheld weapons, not things like artillery, cannons, turrets, or torpedoes.
weapon bag: A long bag to carry one, two or three shinais. It is made of light materials (cloth, nylon or artificial leather) and often has a shoulder strap.
weapon behind back:
Holding a weapon behind the back.
Use weapon on back when the weapon is worn on the back. Use this tag when the weapon is being held behind the back with the hands.
weapon case:
A type of portable case designed to safely store, carry and transport weapons (including the accessories) in concealed manner. It comes in various colours and shape, though rectangular is the most common one - as well as being made from various material (e.g. fabric, leather, or plastic).
Weapon case can be carried on back just like backpack (post #5190996), or being handheld like a briefcase (post #3566073). It can be soft or rigid container (post #5334885). Some designs feature internal foam pad for extra protection (see post #3702122).
weapon connection: A crossover, cosplay or parody where two characters use the same kind of weapon.
weapon focus:
Images with a major focus on one or more items of weapons. 
no humans may also apply for some.
weapon in mouth: A character holding a weapon inside their mouth, usually with their teeth.
weapon name: The name of a weapon appears in the image. The corresponding weapon should also be visible.
weapon on back:
A weapon worn on the back. Use the applicable weapon tag (often sword or rifle) together with this tag.
See weapon behind back when the weapon is being held behind the back with the hands. Use this tag when the weapon is worn on the back.
weapon over shoulder: A weapon being held over the shoulders.
weapon request:
Works like tagme, except you need someone to identify the weapon used in a post.
Using this for any generic-looking revolvers, double-barelled/pump action shotguns or lever action rifles is discouraged. Because most of their specific named models are extremely identical to another. And frequent lack of artistic details or inaccurate ones may render identification almost impossible. Perspective and distance factor also hamper identification.

weather vane:
An instrument for showing the direction of the wind.
They are typically used as an architectural ornament to the highest point of a building. Although partly functional, weather vanes are generally decorative, often featuring the traditional cockerel design with letters indicating the points of the compass. The word 'vane' comes from the Anglo-Saxon word 'fane' meaning 'flag'.

web address: A web address (e.g. www.example.com) is somewhere in the image, usually as a watermark.
webbed hands: Two or more fingers united by a common sheath of skin. Some species of birds and animals use these webbings on their feet for swimming. On Danbooru, this is often seen with aquatic-themed monster people like mermaids, kappa, or frog people.
webcam: A type of video camera designed to be mounted to the top of a monitor for use in video calls or livestreaming.
wedding dress:
A marital dress, typically all white and decorated with frills and veils.
Wedding dresses in nonstandard colors should be tagged using the dress color tags. For example, a pink wedding dress should be tagged as wedding dress and pink dress.
wedding ring:
A ring on the ring finger of the left hand, or a ring that is otherwise obviously a wedding ring, e.g. one used for a marriage proposal.
If a ring has gemstones or other ornaments, use ornate ring too.
wedge heels:
high heels with a thick, raised sole at the back of the shoe, forming a wedge-shaped heel. Also known as espadrilles or simply as wedges.
Unlike normal heels, the bottom of the shoe is flat, with no gap between the sole and the ground.
If the entire sole is thick, but the heel is thicker than the front, then both platform heels and wedge heels may apply.
wedgie:

Note that garments that naturally lie between the buttocks—such as thongs, fundoshi, and one-piece thongs—should not usually have this tag since the wedging is implied.

welrod:
The Welrod is a World War II-era bolt action handgun with an integrated suppressor of British origin. It was designed by Major Hugh Reeves at the Inter-Services Research Bureau  near Welwyn Garden City, which gave the Welrod its name, as well as "rod" for being a gangland slang for gun.
The Welrod is visually recognizable by its roughly tonfa-like shape thanks to its long tubular suppressor, L-shaped trigger and a long bulging trigger guard (while Mk II variant lacks it).
welsh corgi:

wimple:
A type of headwear that typically covers the head in a similar fashion to a detached hood - that is, wound snugly around the head, leaving the face bare, but covering the jaw and ears. When worn in this fashion, it is also referred to as a barbette. 
Derived from medieval times, the wimple is most often seen in depictions of traditional nuns, where it is worn under a veil, and often attached to a guimpe - this is a collar, usually white, that covers the shoulders.
wince: An expression of involuntarily flinching, as from pain, distress, surprise or extreme embarrassment.
winchester model 1897: The Winchester Model 1897, also known as the Model 97, M97, or Trench Gun, was a pump-action shotgun with an external hammer and tube magazine manufactured by the Winchester Repeating Arms Company. An evolution of John Browning's Model 1893, over one million of these shotguns were produced from 1897 until 1957. It was offered in numerous barrel lengths and grades, chambered in 12 and 16 gauge, and as a solid frame or takedown.
wind: Situation in which the image is drawn in such a way that wind is blowing through the subject(s).
wind chime:
Also called a wind-bell, the wind chime is a decorative object suspended in midair that has three basic forms:
- A cluster of small pieces of metal, glass, pottery, bamboo, seashell, or wood that collide with each other and make noise when blown by the wind
- A cluster of tubes or rods, often made of metal or wood, that are rung by a central clapper, to which is attached a flat plate to catch the wind
- A single bell or open-ended glass globe whose clapper is attached to a flat plate to catch the wind.
wind lift:
Where the wind lifts up something, such as clothing (skirt, dress, etc.), parasols or other miscellaneous articles. May be used with dress lift, shirt lift and skirt lift as appropriate.
On pixiv, this may also be known as the Monroe Effect ("モンロー効果":[http://dic.pixiv.net/a/%E3%83%A2%E3%83%B3%E3%83%AD%E3%83%BC%E5%8A%B9%E6%9E%9C]), in reference to an iconic scene in marilyn monroe's "the seven-year itch" where wind from a subway vent lifts her dress.
wind turbine:

window shutter:

Shutters may be mounted on the inside or outside of a window, and they may be fixed or hinged. Some shutters are purely aesthetic in design and may not cover the windows at all.
Contrast with window blinds, which hang freely instead of being set in a frame.
Not to be confused with window shadow, which are shadows created by a window.

wire:

Images that depict coated wires, especially those connected to a machine or piece of electronics, should only use the cable tag instead.  The only exception to this is if the coated wire is also exposing the metal underneath the coat, in which case it can be tagged wire in conjunction with the cable tag.

The belligerents formed two major factions, the Allied Powers (or "Allies") and the Axis Powers (or "Axis").
World War II is considered the deadliest military conflict in human history.

year of the dog:

year of the dragon:

A Year of the Dragon always occurs after a Rabbit year and before a Snake year.
year of the goat:

A Year of the Goat always occurs after a Horse year and before a Monkey year.
The Chinese word (kanji) 羊 refers to both goats and sheep, and is interpreted in Japan only as sheep.
year of the monkey:

year of the ox:
The Ox occupies the second position in the Chinese Zodiac. Years of birth include 1913, 1925, 1937, 1949, 1961, 1973, 1985, 1997, 2009, 2021, 2033.
An Year of the Ox always occurs after a Rat year and before a Tiger year. Artists often portray female characters dressed up as or resembling a cow since cows are simply female oxen.
year of the pig:
The Pig is the last of 12 animals representing the Chinese zodiac. The following are years of the Pig: 1935, 1947, 1959, 1971, 1983, 1995, 2007, 2019, 2031.
A Dog year always comes before the Year of the Pig, and a Rat year always comes afterwards in the next 12-year Chinese zodiac animal cycle.
In Japan, the wild boar is used instead of the (domesticated) pig.
year of the rabbit:
The Year of the Rabbit is fourth in the Chinese Zodiac. These are Rabbit years: 1939, 1951, 1963, 1975, 1987, 1999, 2011, 2023.
A Rabbit year always occurs after a Tiger year and before a Dragon year.
year of the rat:
The Year of the Rat is the first in the Chinese zodiac cycle. Birth years include 1924, 1936, 1948, 1960, 1972, 1984, 1996, 2008, 2020.
A Rat year always occurs after a Pig year and before an Ox year.
year of the rooster:
Every 12 years there is a Year of the Rooster, beginning at Chinese New Year. Years of the Rooster include 1933, 1945, 1957, 1969, 1981, 1993, 2005, 2017, and 2029. 
The Rooster is tenth of the 12 animals in the Chinese zodiac cycle. A year of the Rooster always comes after a Monkey year and before a Dog year.
Artists may portray chicken girls or females dressed up as chickens since chickens are simply female roosters.
year of the tiger:
The Tiger ranks the third of the animals in the Chinese zodiac. Years of birth include 1914, 1926, 1938, 1950, 1962, 1974, 1986, 1998, 2010, 2022.
A Year of the Tiger always occurs after an Ox year and before a Rabbit year.

Western astrologers divide it into twelve signs, named for the constellation that is nearest the position of the Sun for one-twelfth of the year. zoom layer:
An additional layer that magnifies part of the illustration. It's a common technique used for backgrounds in character art. 
There are sometimes small, primarily 2D variations, such as:
- The layer being reversed.
- The layer being rotated.
- The layer being partially transparent, in greyscale, or having other changes in color.
- A character having a different expression.
If the layer is from a different 3D perspective, or there are larger 3D differences such as costumes, poses, or characters, it's a projected inset instead.
